entries.name: Crawling Prescripts
entries: The following Prescripts are meant to be of a "Crawling" speed, which means they should be completed within the timespan of your next long rest or until an entire week has passed.

entries.caption: Crawling Prescripts
rows: Among those you consider your companions, find out which of them is the youngest and acquire as much currency as you can. On the final day of the week, spend all of it to throw a party for your youngest companion.
Nurture the next wounded creature you see back to health, then eat it as dinner after it is healed.
Investigate the first murder you come across and after finding the culprit, abandon the case.
Destroy something which is priceless in front of one who values it.

Create 3 paintings of the most beautiful things you know, then throw them into a fire. (You must truly capture the beauty. To do so, you must spend at least 3 hours or a Long Rest to create a painting by attempting a {@skill Performance} check, successfully painting a work that satisfies you on a DC of 16.)

For the foreseeable future, greet every third person you come across. If reciprocated, you must reverse their gravity centre onto the ground. (You must successfully Grapple the creature and suplex them as an Action, dealing 3d8 + your Strength modifier on a success.)
Slay a beast that is larger than you yet smaller than the last room you have slept or stayed more than 15 minutes at. (This may be a creature of Aberration, Beast or Monstrosity type.)
For the next three days: become the smartest eater. (You must use a combined tool for eating, such as a spork, fpoon or switchblade. You cannot consume food without its use.)
See that no creature finds their eyes open by the end of your violent engagements.

Become a saint in red. (Gift something worth at least 1 gold to 10 or more children. This Prescript is instantly failed if you cause the children to cry or if any harm befalls them until the Prescript is undertaken.)
Cook three waffles and stack them while putting mayonnaise on the bottom waffle. Then serve them to the 9th person you saw this week and wish them a happy birthday.
Stalk the third person you see. In within 7 days but not less of 3 days, attempt to win their heart and break it. Record this experience.

Embrace and conjoin the way of a Hero. (Within a week, bite off one piece of a fresh apple and change into a new personality according to the Heroes Journey every day. (Roll a 1d8, no repeats) (1: Act of the best of intentions (Hero), 2: Guide those who are lost or without reason (Mentor), 3: Assist those who are in trouble (Ally), 4: Give those without reason a task (Herald), 5: Disrupt those with a goal with a hurdle (Trickster), 6: Be of aid or of disdain (Shapeshifter), 7: Test the position of the able-bodied fighters, kill if they are unworthy, spare if they are worthy (Guardian), 8: Vow to kill the first able-bodied fighter you see in a day (Shadow).)

Paint one picture of yourself exclusively using paints made of cadmium and sell them for a week. (You may attempt Sleight of Hand or {@skill Performance} checks for your works quality. The resulting rolls become the DC that any creature who spends more than a day within vicinity of this painting must pass as a Constitution saving throw or become {@condition Poisoned} until receiving medical or clerical aid.)

Find god in a tomato. (Pray every day and plant a whole fruit in the ground while reciting prayers, then roll a d100. On a roll of 90 or greater, it sprouts to a tree sapling mere moments after being planted as if by godly will and you are successful in this Prescript.
Become a mirror of the next being reflected in your eyes. (Act as the first creture that you see after getting this Prescript until someone else points it out.)
In one week, win 5 left shoes in games of cards.

Spread one's wings. (You must help any random person of your choice pursue and at least begin reaching a dream of theirs. An example would be aiding one who wishes to become a wizard enroll in an Arcane Study Institution.)
Act as new. (Act as a person who is incredibly naive and unaware, often unsure of their actions and doubts their every move until someone questions why you are acting in such a way.)
Embrace the natural downpour of greater hearts. (If it rains or snows, use no weather protection and instead stay under the phenomena until the Prescripts completion or until the event ceases.)

Be unlike yourself. (Your alignment must be reversed for the Prescripts duration, neutrals remain neutral with inversed values, such as if they hated undead they now must act as if they love them. Lawful characters must act chaotic and so on.)

Kidnap a person every day for 4 days, on that same day, ask them the meaning of life and why they don't wish to die. If any answer yes, pre-emptively leave and avoid that person for the rest of their life. Otherwise, take note of the answers and leave it in a cleaned plate of food of the next tavern or inn you visit.
Be as of the accursed birds of black feather. (Communicate only by mimicking other's words.)

Experience what it is to be alive. (Within the next seven days, feel the emotions of Hate/Resentment, Anger/Wrath, Anxiety/Bad, Joy/Pride, Calmness/Peace, Disgust/Envy, Innocence/Curiosity, Sadness/Gloom, Shock/Fear, and Love/Longing.)
Steal the hearts of the people who fought and died against you.

Paint your view of heaven and what you wish to see after death. Then show it around to your fellows and hear their opinions. ( This creation must be sincere and contain both your sufferings and yearnings. You may attempt {@skill Performance} checks, yet they mean nothing. When you do so, you must spend at least 5 days doing so, if not longer. Upon each long rest, describe what are the feelings your character is having to go through to reach this ideal vision. In the end, question if it is something you'd deserve or still need to get within grasp of.)
Provide safe passage and sanctuary to the next wounded creature you see. Ask nothing of return except for a single story of their lives.
Do not aid the dreary. (Do not do anything that would result in other creatures being Stabilized, recover Hit Points or that would result in a negative Condition of theirs ending early.)
Visit a church not of your own God and learn their truths and falsities. Then commit either a sin or ten good deeds in their eyes.

Trace the direction of your homeland on a map, then acquire a bow and arrow. Set the ammunition aflame and shoot it toward the sky at midnight for three nights. If it ever hits or narrowly misses a person, monster or creature, regale them with the food of your homeland in a show of genuine hospitality.
Do not ask a single question. Only do as you know best.
Be exceedingly courteous, no matter how rude or debauched your fellows might add.

Play a song to mesmerize the hearts of all that could hear. (If you do not know how to play an instrument, seek a master to do so. After being taught, you permanently gain Proficiency in that instrument.)

In a single swig, drink a glass bottle's worth of poison. (If not Immune to the {@condition Poisoned} Condition: Roll a number of Hit Die equal to your level divided by 3, rounded down. Your Maximum Hit Points are deduced by that value for a week. This Prescript is instantly completed upon consuming the poison.)

Bite your tongue. (Speak only in one language other than Common. If you know no other languages, either only communicate through emoji if playing virtually or through mimicking your meanings if in person or through video.

Become a pretty picture in a pricey wall. (Ask your party members how much they think their heads are worth. Then print or commission an artist to make several bounty posters of your party with their ascribed values. Post them in whichever Tavern, Guild Hall, or Public Post Sign you can.)

Part ways with that which has greatly aided you. (Discard one magic item you have been Attuned to since the last long rest. This item may not be cursed nor be given to a permanent member of the party.)

Speak only in rhymes. If you come across something wearing or that is of orange color, only lie to them instead of rhyming. (This extends to simple conversation, such as saying "Good night" as simple courtesy while it is day.)
At night, before sleep, confess your most painful secret to the one who sleeps closest to you.
Do nothing as the products of your heart stand in the face of death. (Do not heal any friendly creatures or Stabilize them for any reason.)
Embrace the first ideal presented to you, no matter how you may feel about it.
Mock those in power, aggrandize those who have nothing.
Revel in filth and disease. (You must Poison yourself and at least five other creatures.)
Act like a legendary hero or villain of the region. (You must dress like them, change your appearance to be like them and attempt to imitate their personality.)
Harbor no doubt, plant no regrets. (Draw another Prescript. You gain double the effect you would gain upon its completion or failure.)

Push yourself to your limits. (You must reach at least 5 Exhaustion points. You may, once per roll give yourself Advantage after failing a attack, check or save, taking the new result and gaining a point of Exhaustion. You must do so after rolling but before the DM announces the result.)
Spread the word of the Prescripts to seven people. (You must convince seven creatures to Draw at least one Prescript.)
Clutch with the golden hand what is yours. (Do not spend a single gold piece, use an item on another creature or otherwise grant them a gift or material gain.)
Take a measured stride always. (Never take the Dash Action or willingly attempt an {@skill Athletics} or {@skill Acrobatics} check.)
Become yourself. Act like you would before getting your first prescript. (Do you even remember who you were then?)
Handle your share in your utmost lonesome. (Do not accept or take the Aid, help or counselling from other creatures.)
Make peace. (Successfully end hostilities or at least form a truce between yourself and another creature or faction. Alternatively, do so as a mediator between two parties.)
Light the sparks of war. (Successfully pit one party against another without being linked as the source of the conflict.)
Take no part in mysticism. (While out of combat, cast no spells and use no magic items.)
Discover the secrets of at least three of the people that share a meal with you.
Spread or fabricate a legend or myth across your current settlement, or the next one you come across if within the wilderness.
Decline matters of subtleness. (You cannot willingly attempt {@skill Stealth} checks and must always either loudly knock on doors before coming through or kick them open if locked.)

Atone for your past sins while enduring the interminable hell of your own making. (You must do so in a way that is found acceptable after confessing to your nearest Cleric or spiritually adjacent creature. They must dictate how to better atone. For the duration, you must not recover hit points.)
Whenever you tell a lie or are untrustworthy, bite down your tongue with force. (You suffer 3d8 piercing damage whenever you do so. Untrustworthiness delineates lying, cheating or spreading secrets.)
Draw in black the lines of suffering on your body. (Your body must be marked with black dotted lines at the articulations. Hostile creatures gain Advantage to hit you while within 5-ft. of you)

In lack of acknowledgement, light yourself ablaze. (If you do not take responsability for your actions and see them through, as per the DMs discretion, you must set yourself on fire as an Action. You suffer 16 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count instantly.)
Understand the searing pain of death. (Harm yourself with an iron weapon whenever you kill another creature or, if out of combat, cause harm to them. You cannot reduce the damage taken by any means.)
Destroy the sound. (Whenever a creature speaks in a tone louder than casual conversation, such as a scream, perform a weapon attack against them until they are silent. This includes yourself.)
Clap without a sound, slash without a voice. (Start any Combat Hidden and do not fail a single {@skill Stealth} check.)

Refuse yourself the graces, disable your own recital. (Do not make use of your Channel Divinity feature. If you are of another class, do not use its main resource, such as Rage, Ki or Sorcery Points, Sneak Attack and so on. The DM determines what the main resource is. For full-casters such as the Wizard, they cannot spend their highest level Spell Slots or 5th level Spell slots or greater.)
Hold your fellow being as if dancing whenever addressing them. (You must hold a creatures body whenever directly talking to them or Grapple a creature before attacking them during combat.)
Welcome the Wills in minor scale. (During combat, at the start of your turns always draw a Prescript from the Magicked Prescripts table. [From the Oath of Procuration Subclass])

Loudly proclaim your fair crew's namesake at the heat of combat. (Whenever your party has triumph over a challenge, such as interacting with an adverse character, winning a game of dice or entering battle, scream your party's name loudly.)

Act by unpredictable whim. (Always choose your targets randomly. If there are multiple ways of approaching a situation through Skill checks, do so randomly. If you have to make a decision that can be summarized as "yes or no", pick a side and toss a coin to decide.)

Always harm that which harms the Will. (You must always deal damage at least once per turn to creatures {@condition Target of the Prescript|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Marked by the Prescript}. If any other creature refuses or speaks ill of your god, engage in combat against them. You may not kill them.)

Knock on three front doors of three different homes at midnight during three different days. If attended to, ask for food. If refused, starve until a creature gives you food, if given food grant the one who fed you a gift of your choice the next day. (You suffer one point of Exhaustion for each night spent without food.)
Cook three waffles and stack them while putting mayonnaise on the bottom waffle. Then serve them to the 9th person you saw today and wish them a happy birthday.
Acquire a relic of some importance and grant it as a boon to the nearest blacksmith or merchant. (You must give a Magic Item that you have acquired after drawing this Prescript.)
Eradicate that which must not be known, burn a wound into history. (Attempt to burn any books and parchment you touch or a creature intends to give to you within a timespan of 5 minutes.)
See not the world for what it is, but instead of what you wish it to be. (You must blindfold yourself for the duration of the Prescript, becoming {@condition Blinded}.)
Learn of others and have others learn of others in tow. (Ask someone to tell you a personal story and repeat it truthfully to another creature before the week ends.)
Be precise in your curiosity. (In any interaction, you may only ask any individual creature only up to three questions per long rest.

Become a part-time historian, grant the gift of knowledge to the mystics. (Learn the name and history of any landmarks you come across. Log them in a leather-bound book and then give it to another spellcaster.)
Find an object left unattended and attempt to return it to its owner. Upon failure, willingly lose one object of your own choice that is similar to the first object lost.
Lift others burdens, aid those without ability. (You must take the Aid Action whenever another creature attempts a skill check, aiding them.)

Embrace the sheer inexplainable force of luck. (Whenever you roll a d100, do so three more times then decide which is the true roll by rolling a d4. The d100 are presented in the order they were rolled.)

When in doubt, ask the stars. (If your character has a question, ask around the table for other players answers. The DM selects one of the responses given and your character imagines that response while looking up to the sky.)
Once a day for the next week, when the sun hangs at it's highest, find the 5th person you see. Challenge them to duel, if you win thank them for their time. If you lose, apologize for your weakness.

Be a retainer to your friend, sneer your foes. (Act as if you were the humble servant of one party member of your choice. Actively mock and disrespect any who come to disrespect that creature in any way. You may choose pets and companions as a party member for this Prescript.)

Leave no slight unpunished. (If a creature lies to you, you must lie to them enough that they feel unsure of what they are doing in life. If a creature harms you, you must at least leave a lasting injury on their body, such as severing a finger. If a creature slights you, you must make them cry.)

Interrogate nature and reach a tune with it. (Attempt to interview any critter or beast you find in a conversation. The 6th beast you come across gives you a random trinket of your DMs choice, as per their discretion or rolled on any trinket table.)
Simulate a better person than who you are. (Help the homeless when able, avoid killing other creatures and do not commit any sins against any Deities.)
Ignore social etiquette and always respond with the first thing that comes to your mind.

Fish a fish greater in length than your head. Then grill it. Then feast on it with your comrades. Then carve knives out of its bones. Leave these knives within the third hole you see this week after eating the fish. (The length of your head includes horns.)
Be free-spirited in vour consumerism. (Always accept and consume any potions, drinks, food and drugs given to you.)
Allow the stressed hard workers to rest. (For all nights you remain in a settlement, convince and work in stead of an tavernkeeper or similar professional to the best of your ability.)
Whenever you come across a shunned topic or forgotten knowledge, start a conversation around it and attempt to restore any form of glory it once might have had.

Call out your every action. (Creatures have Advantage on {@skill Perception} checks against you. Furthermore, all Spells you cast gain the Verbal component. If they would require a target to attempt a Strength, Dexterity or Constitution saving throw, they gain Advantage.)
Arrange a collection of your favorite colour. (You must pick up and constantly carry all objects of the chosen colour in your person until the end of this Prescript.)

Log your adventure's next three days for those who will come. (Keep a detailed diary of whatever you and your party has done during the day and update it at night. Then leave it at the nearest Inn, Tavern or public space.)
When faced with multiple paths, always take the hardest known route.

Learn and help another learn of the story they tell at night for the next three nights. (Before the next long rest, ask another party member about their most recent dreams and relate it back to them in your own words. Repeat this three times.)
Follow along your path. The Will is watching you. (Simply keep progressing towards your Party's current objective. Acknowledge that it is all part of a grander plan.)
Try something you have never once done in your life.

Have your hair groomed to absolute lusciousness. If you have no hair, have your head shined to a sparkling sheen. (You must spend at least 60 * your Level GP to do so. After doing so, your Charisma score increases by 2 for the next week.)

entries.caption: Magicked Prescripts
rows: Designate the first creature you see as your sibling, refer to them as such for the remainder of the day. If any slights are committed against your sibling no matter how minor, violently avenge them.
After defeating a foe, take their weapon and carve out their initials on their face. (You must spend your Bonus Action to do so.)
Move toward the closest enemy, then kneel down before them and aim for their left leg without damaging their bones. (Do not deal bludgeoning damage.)
When facing the one who had harmed you, return the favor through a minor inconvenience of your choosing.
Hum an unpleasant tune out loud, and attack the second person who is annoyed by it. (You do so as a Free Action.)

When face to face to the one harming you, stand still and strike a pose or approach them slowly until they have hit you. (You must move only half your movement speed per turn toward a creature hostile to you.)
Throw dust over the eyes of the first person (or thing) that intends to touch you.

Challenge the next person that intends to hurt or heal you to a match of Rock, Paper, Scissors, then attack them with the damage most synonymous with the winning throw. (Rock -> Bludgeoning | Scissors -> Slashing | Paper -> Piercing. If they fail to play, you may conclude the Prescript by dealing damage to the target.)
Give the creature closest to you a Prescript. If they do not conclude it until the next 12 seconds, you fail this Prescript.

If you or any creature you view as an ally is slighted or harmed in any way, you must attempt to learn the name of the offending creature and write it down on paper along with the offense they commited and read it aloud to the offending creature.

Scare or Flirt with the person (or thing) that intends to hurt you. If they react to you, cut their eyeballs. (You may perform a Persuasion Check against the targets passive Insight score. On a success, they are Charmed until the start of their next turn.)
Approach the person intending to hurt or heal you in a cheery jog, then, dropkick them. (You become Prone on a hit or a miss.)
When attacking the person who has not attacked you, adjust your hair upwards while doing so. (You must have a free hand to do so.)
On the first round of combat, Grapple the nearest creature to you. Then declare that you are the king of watermelons with pride." (You are a king despite your gender.)
Target any foe that wears purple or cares too much for there hair.

Before killing another foe, ask them for mercy. If they do not grant it, strike yourself instead. If they do, slay them immediately. (You must perform a melee weapon attack against yourself. You hit automatically.)
In your next combat encounter, hop like a frog to reach your enemy. (You can only move using the jump action.)

For the next 24 hours proclaim each of your attacks in overdramatic ways. (You conclude this Prescript if you execute until the start of your turn, but retroactively fail it if you fail to do so for the duration.)
Only speak in Haiku for a while. (You must speak a successful Haiku at least once until the start of your next turn.)

Recite the lyrics of a song or poem to the next person you fight, only stopping once they're Unconcious or dead. (You conclude this Prescript if you execute until the start of your turn, but retroactively fail it if vou fail to do so for the duration.)
Murder five small critters, and attach them to a body.
When choosing a target may your blow fall 10 feet. (You must have the source of your attack, such as a blade or arrow, fall at least 10-ft. before hitting your target.)

If someone looks at you, punch their face. (You must perform a unarmed weapon attack against that target. Their AC is increased by 2 if they have one head only. On a hit, the target is Blinded until the start of your next turn.)

Make a soup for someone who has wronged you or an ally. Upon serving one portion to the individual, remind them that you do not forgive them and splash another portion into their face. (You may prepare this soup as an Action during your turn provided you have any liquid and anything that could be considered edible within within 5-ft. 5-ft, of you.) (Applying fire to heat it may be done as a Free Action if you have a viable source. After you spend your Action to do so, ask the table out of character if the Soup is "Crap", "Mid", "Good" or "Outstanding". You may serve the soup and toss it as a Bonus Action.? (Upon tossing it, make a weapon attack roll against a target within reach. You are proficient in this if you are proficient in Cook's Utensils. If the majority chose the first, the creature suffers 1d8 poison damage when eating the soup and another 1d8 of the same damage upon having it thrown upon their face.) (On the second, the creature is suffers 1d4 damage when the soup is tossed. If its Good the creature is healed by 1d4 hit points when consuming the soup and suffering 1d4 cold or fire damage when it is tossed, and if the soup is "Outstanding" they are healed by 1d12 hit points when consuming the soup and suffer 1d4 psychic damage when it is tossed.)

Take the weapon of the next creature you slay, until the end of the brawl, use only it. (The Prescript is considered complete when you first equip the weapon and is retroactively considered incomplete if you deal damage using anything else other than the weapon or your Paladin spells.)
Whatever you do, do not stop dancing. (Spend at least half your movement speed on your turn.)
Distance yourself from your friends, allies and acquaintances. (You must end your turn at least 30-ft. away from friendly creatures.)
Become touchy-feely. (You must end your turn at least 5-ft. within a friendly creature.)

Do not strike another foe until your current one lies dead. (Do not switch targets after first dealing damage to a creature within your turn. This Prescript counts as concluded upon first ending your turn after hitting said creature and is retroactively failed if you switch targets.)
Be as a dog and walk upon nature. (Only crawl to move until the end of your turn.)
Become a magic man. (Act like the setting's closest thing to a moustache-bearing parlour magician until the end of your turn. You cannot use true spells.)
Act unpredictably in the face of your foes. (Use only different Actions than what you used in your last turn of combat, even if it was a different combat.)

Become a simulacra of a beloved person to your left. (Imitate te tl the closest ally to your characters immediate right. Mimic their voice, mannerisms and use the closest weapon or spells available to you compared to theirs.)

Take the next hit aimed at you. Give it back twofold. (Spend a Bonus Action to lower your AC by 5 until you are hit once. During your next turn, you apply your damage dice twice whenever you next hit a creature with an Attack.)
Drink a potion. If you have none, attack your closest ally.

Aid your closest ally so you feel hopeful of your immediate future. (Take the Help Action targeting the closest friendly creature. If they pass their next roll, you gain the effect of Help for the next two turns.)
Dialogue with the closest hostile creature. Attempt to difuse the situation. If they can't understand your language, do everything in your power to attempt to make them understand.
Make the most of your time. (You must spend your Action, Bonus Action and perform a Free Action until the end of your turn.)

Be merciful on your next fight. (Do not kill anyone present in your next combat. The Prescript is fulfilled once you knock a creature Unconscious, and retroactively Failed if you kill one of the creatures afterward.)
Punish only those you can't touch. (You must only perform ranged attacks until the end of your turn.)
Do as you're told. (Always perform actions dictated by other creatures. You have infinite Reactions until the start of your next turn.)
Fight with your eyes closed for 6 seconds.
Whenever you hit a foe, also headbutt them. (You and the creature suffer 1d6 bludgeoning damage whenever you do so.
Kick a dog. (Or animal closest to a dog. If able, a tortoise.)
Wrestle your foes to submission. (You may refer to WWE wrestlers and other augmented-reality-fighters to do so. Even games like street fighter count.)
Get up close and personal with your foes. (You must only perform melee attacks until the end of your turn.)

Remove the tongue of whomever has disrespected you or people in high-ranking positions. (To do so, you must land an Attack while choosing to have the target have their AC have a +5 bonus modifier. On a successful hit, the target is unable to speak until their tongue is restored.)
Invoke the fury of the elements. (A suggested mechanic for this is only dealing fire, cold or lightning damage until the end of your turn. The DM may choose to accept any other interpretation.)

Wildcard. (Ask the player to your immediate right [Or above you if playing online] for a Prescript. That becomes this Prescript. If it is toward your detriment, that player gains an Inspiration they may use until the end of the fight.)
Crash someone through a window. (You may use the Shove Action to do so. If you do, the creature suffers 3d8 piercing damage.)
Tear of your armor and fight without fear of death. (You unequip your armor as a Bonus Action when done this way.)
Go unseen from the beholding's eyes. (Take the Hide Action until the end of your turn and do so successfully.)
Embrace your pains and endure. (Allow every single attack aimed at you to hit you. Do not become Unconscious until the start of your next turn.)

Impress your friends with a dazzling weapon flourish. (Roll a Performance check with a DC of 14 + half your Paladin Level. On a success, gain half your Paladin Level + 2 of Poise Count. These are halved down.)
Strike yourself once in the rib.
Rob a corpse bare of its belongings and toss them in the nearest trash heap, corpse or body of water.
Start a debate of morals with the one who has hurt you the most. Win it.
Do whatever is in your power to have the creature closest to you mimic an animal of your choice until the start of your next turn.
Give a meaningful gift to one of your foes. If they accept and are commoved by it, cease fighting them immediately unless they strike you.

Shoot upward near another and believe. (You must name one of your ranged attacks and be within 5-ft. of another creature. You and the controller of that creature roll a d100. The one who rolled the lowest is hit.)
Crush your left foot with your right foot. (You take 1d8 plus your Strength modifier in bludgeoning damage and lose 10-ft. of walking speed for two turns.)

Eat this Prescript. If unable, eat a dagger (If you eat the Prescript you must pass a DC 16 Constitution Saving Throw or be Poisoned for the next minute, being able to retry this this Save Save at the end of your next turns.)
Only walk in the direction of lights in respect of those who are gone.
Strike unjust ones with blunt force trauma. (Use bludgeoning damage only. Target creatures who are hostile to creatures of lower level or CR than them.)
Kill all the doors of the ceiling. (Kill at least one hostile creature above you.)
Breach down the walls and forsake those who would forsake you. (Attack a hostile creature that is behind a wall. On a successful hit, that cover is broken if possible.)
Do not acknowledge anyone else but your foes.
Recite your tenets or beliefs aloud, proceeding to strike any being that questions or dares criticize them.
Start a fire and impede it from being put down, for it is not a dog.

Tell your dreams and wants to one of your enemies. If they answer truthfully, ask them for a duel and spare them on a win. If they lie, kill them at all costs. (This Prescript lasts until the end of combat.)
Breach a taboo of the area you are living in. (If in the City as your setting, you may only break a social Taboo. Don't kill yourself over this, please. The Claws have better things to do.)
Stay by your fellows side, defe defend them at all costs. (You must end your turn within 5-ft. of a friendly creature and they cannot have suffered damage until the start of your next turn.)

Give away half your money to the creature farthest from you that you can reach. Toss it with your full force. (You have a reach of 30-ft. times your Strength modifier for this, with a minimum of 15-ft.)

If you see a critter, follow it. (The DM may have any tiny creature such as a butterfly appear to guide you. This may last for up to three turns. At the end, your DM may choose to have you find nothing, an uncommon magic item or a map to somewhere you don't recognize.)
Clean all the dirt and grime from your immediate surrounding. (15-ft. radius centered around you.)

Cause pain with a _ _ _ (This Prescript is blurred out. You can make out the word with a little effort. To make this effort, read the Prescript aloud to your table, the first object named by your party or DM is the word.)
If it is bright, shoot the sun. If it is night, find shelter. (Attack the biggest or shiniest creature or enter cover respectively.)
Tell your greatest fears to your foes whenever you cause them harm. Tell them to spread word that you will hunt these fears down at any cost.
Be a liar, but always involve flowers in your lies.

After the dust settles, compose a song about your exploits in this battle. Sing it at the next one. Draw another prescript. (You complete this upon singing at your first turn of the next battle and may ignore this Prescript toward the total drawn in a single turn. You fail automatically if you don't perceive the happenings of battle.)

Carry your shortest companion in your back and learn to become one for battle. (This prescript lasts for three turns or until it is completed. You may carry a friendly creature this way by going within 5-ft. of them and using your Bonus Action to pick them up, moving them alongside you. Creatures have Disadvantage to hit them while atop you. You conclude this Prescript on killing another creature you and your companion have hit since carrying them.)
Carry your largest companion in your back and learn how to become one for battle. (See Prescript no 81.)
The next time you kill, make it so the body is unrecognizable. (Lasts for three rounds.)

Ask your targets if they like to get beat. If they answer in affirmative, don't attack them. If they say anything else, beat them hurtily. (You deal an additional point of damage until the start of your next turn.)

Always attempt to talk to inanimate objects. If any perceived object responds, drop on your knees and apologize for not treating your objects well enough. If not, let your tools slumber. (This counts if any creature pretends to be an object responding. Otherwise you cannot use any objects until the start of your next turn.)
Disregard your riches. Live without them for a while. (Toss one of your magical items away. You may only pick them up after combat is over or the Prescript will become a failure.)
Plead your heart to one of your allies. If they die, kill yourself. (This is permanent and you will fail this Prescript if that oath is ever broken. Upon failure, gain 4 Karmic Consequences instead.)

Experience what it feels like to taste one of your own. (Make a unarmed weapon attack you are proficient with against a target within 5-ft. of yourself to bite them. On a hit, deal 1 + your Strength Modifier piercing damage and be healed by that many Hit Points. If the creature us Undead or otherwise toxic, take 3d8 necrotic, poison or acid damage as per your DM's choice. Take psychic damage instead if they are just disgusting.)
State your intentions out loud clearly and without lying. (This counts for both what you plan to do in your turn, forcing you to perform attacks at Disadvantage until the start of your next turn.)
Mark the trees to guide a way inside. (You must deal damage against three separate structures within the next three turns.)
Give the one closest to you a Prescript. Do everything in your power to have them fail.
Become the centre of your world when exercising the Will's power. (You must cast a Paladin spell with you as the target.)
Draw back into shade. (You must take the Hide action and remain hidden until the start of your next turn.)
Litter the ground in pincushions and an distinct blood splatters to form a map to the one who will read it. (Use only piercing attacks and move after every attack.)
Punish those with wicked hearts. (Focus all your attacks on creatures that have attacked the physically weaker members of your party or evil-aligned creatures.)

Ask whoever you perceive as a leader of the opposing group what they would have life mean. Note that response, even if unintelligible, in a piece of parchment and toss it in the ground of the next tavern you visit. (This is complete the moment you note down the paper, but you gain two Karmic Consequence count if you do not leave the paper on a tavern.)

Exalt that which is your foe, give them a title and spread it to the winds. (You gain an additional Grace of the Prescripts if you do so for an entire week, or suffer one Karmic Consequence if vou do not.)
Take a moment to remember all that has scarred your heart before and let yourself feel all the pains of yesterday. (You suffer your Level's worth of Sinking count.)

For every time that your friends have suffered, suffer as well. (As a free action you may perform a melee weapon attack against yourself for each time a creature friendly to you took damage since the end of your last turn. You instantly hit.)

Look down. (Roll a d6. Find something according to the number rolled. 1 is an Ornate Coin of somewhere you haven't been before. 2 is the lock of hair of a person that you currently or have once loved. 3 is the scales of a chromatic dragon. 4 is a small bag of holding whose contents are determined by your DM. 5 is a letter written directly to you by another follower of the Will that may either contain directions or something else only you would understand, as per the DM's discretion. 6 is a tear that has fled your eye. For the remainder of the fight, you have at least 1 Sinking count.)

entries.name: Follower of an Order Prescripts
entries: Whenever you draw from this table, re-roll the result if you've drawn this Prescript before. You may choose to add another Prescript Table to this roll, if able, rolling 2d100 and summing the result. On rolling two ones, roll a d4, taking odd numbers as a final result of one and even numbers as a final result of two.
If any of the following Prescripts display a specific time until completion, you may draw your next Prescript as usual while the pecific-timed Prescript remains active.

These are intentionally vague and containing varying levels of interpretation, as such, you may either consider any technical completion of a Prescript as enough, with the DM having final say in the matter.

entries.caption: Follower of an Order Prescripts
rows: "Consume all hair strands of your head until smooth." You may spend your Action to do so. You suffer the Poisoned condition for 1 hour.

"Publicly perform a dance to at least two dozens of people." You may use a Performance check to do so, greatly impressing people on a result of 20 or greater, and greatly humiliating yourself on a 10 or lesser.
"Hunt three squirrels or similarly sized mammals and leave their bodies in the nearest tree-hollow or hole after you are done."
"Drink a litre of milk before performing any major activity." You must drink one litre of milk before any combat.
"Only eat, or write, or fight with your right hand.
"Follow every second command issued by others."
Whenever you first see a sword, slap it off the wielder's person with the back of your hand."
"Find a groom or a bride." You gain a +9 bonus on Charisma Checks against a target with dark brown hair.
"Spill another's insides." You must kill another non-summoned, non-construct creature.
"Act like the first creature you see after waking up for the next 12 hours."
"Stab the nearest person you love most with a knife."
"Paint the insides of a temple, town hall, tavern or shop to be picturesque."
"Bake a cake and gift it to the closest creature sleeping to your right. You must fully insert a needle into said cake before gifting it."
"Find the nearest reflective surface and face it towards another."
"Throw the the object you are currently holding towards the direction you are facing, then pick it up."
"Bite down your nearest friend's arm." Upon a successful bite, you deal 1d6 plus your Strength modifier in piercing damage.
"If you would go to sleep, instead stay up until you encounter the next unknown person of the same race as vou. Challenge them to three-card monty until one of vou has lost five silver."

"Go to a place where alcohol is served and challenge the fourth person you meet to a drinking contest. Should you win, find somewhere to sleep. Should you lose, leave the bar and walk a thousand steps west."
"Find a Wanted Man (Or Woman ), make him wish you brought him Dead instead of Alive."
"Defeat a target with a kick travelling at least 10 feet in the air. Ensure an explosion happens behind you until 10 seconds after you land."
"Ask the person to your left to draw their family members (or loved ones) then burn it in front of them."

"From where you are standing right now light a torch. Then, walk ten paces forwards, however if you cannot do so turn 90 degrees to the right until you can walk forwards towards a torch to light. Then, throw the torch as hard as you can in front of you."
"On your fifth time of rest after receiving this prescript, cut a lock of hair from the shortest member of your party while they sleep and spread it on a river when the witching hour strikes."
"When you meet an object with malnutrition, give it a bird and if it sleeps soundly introduce it to a friend."
"Write a letter to someone you love and do not send it. Burn it at sunset."
"Smile when delivering bad news. Frown when delivering good news."
"Carry a weapon openly but don't use it. Let others decide its purpose."
"Within 12 hours, steal from the 2nd Wizard vou come across."
"Reveal an important secret to a person named _______. This is a name of the DM's choice."
"Eradicate the nearest group of bandits or outlaws."
"Do not utter a single word for the next six hours."
"If the first person you meet outside today answers your greetings by lifting their right hand, sink a blade into their body; if the person ignores your greetings, install a blade into your body."
"Walk 120-ft. to the left, then turn and walk 5-ft. to vour immediate right."
"Discover 3 hidden critters within your vicinity and crush them in front of the eight man you meet today."

"Ask the person to your immediate right to think of a number between one and ten. Guess that number correctly. If the person fails to choose a number within that range or lies, punch them in the stomach."
"Create a moving metallic pendulum that moves with the vibrations of the ground and append a pen to its tip. Leave it near the closest prison or house of law."
"Punch the closest object of the colour red until vour knuckles bleed."
"Draw detailed directions toward your homeland. Bury them near a body of water."
"Mount a horse or other quadruped and ride it for the entire day. Do not dismount until hearing a birdcall in the morning."

"Dice a slice of meat from a monster into five cubes and proceed to salt them until the surface is fully white. Have four other people consume one." Whenever a creature attempts to eat one of these salted cubes, they must pass a DC 18 Constitution saving throw or puke.
"Split the nocturnal lights of the a settlement's district thrice before 6 days pass."
"Deafen the fifth person who smiles at you today."
"Drink a litre of juice in the morning and warm-up before meeting your companions."
"Recite E every time you greet someone."
"Point to anyone who you speak to for the next 12 hours. Speak clearly and loudly."
"Shear 663 strands of hair and enclose them in an envelope, to be deposited at the nearest arcane shop or school."
"Buy groceries for someone you hate."
"Avert your eyes to the world until you go to sleep." You are blinded for this duration. A blindfold is recommended.
"Behead seven beings who resist your blade."
"Face toward the north and walk a mile forward. At the end, leap off the nearest cliff or inclination."
"Write a competent letter of admission toward the nearest institution."
"Kiss more girls than yesterday." At least one more.
"Cut off the tongue of the first person that casts a somatic spell intended to hurt or heal another."
"Make a statue out of the first person that speaks to you today, and gift it as a gravestone for the second person that intends to interact with you today."
"Sing the favourite song of the second person you see, then, make them unable to speak."
"Draw a sheep. Leave the paper inside a clock's glass."
"Etch the bearing of a god into a tomato."
"Sever one's head from their shoulders."

"Give out prescripts to the second, fourth and seventh people you see today. Do not gaze unto their contents." When giving these prescripts, roll on this table to grant them. If their recipients conclude them, they receive a Devotion Point. If they don't, the DM determines their immediate fate.
"Always punish another's mistakes, alternating between a light punishment and a severe punishment each time someone else fails."
"Break open the second lock you see after lunch using a toothpick and the back of a key."
"Inhale smoke and hold it in your mouth for half an hour. Exhale within five seconds."
"Recite the favourite prescript you have carried out to your favourite person."
"Inebriate the third animal or mystical creature you perceive today."

"Use non-weapons as cutlery. Use cutlery as weapons. Switch back after hunting a meal with cutlery and preparing a meal from this hunt using your weaponry. Share this meal with someone else and ask them for their honest opinion, then note it down for future improvement."
"Cut off your pinky finger." Roll a d4, if the result is an even number; cut off your right pinky. If the result is an odd number, cut off your left pinky.
"Get on your knees and pray to the very cool and awesome Index Messenger whom resides in The Undertomes."

"Play a child's game with a kid that wants to play. Let them win without them noticing." You may attempt a Deception, Performance or Sleight of Hand check against their passive Insight score to determine your ability to not let them know.
"Convince the fifth right-handed person you meet that you are their long lost relative."
"Take a personal belonging from the next person you fight. Leave it inside the nearest water fountain."
"Inspect the quality of every second blade you see for the day."
"Compose a song for your own funeral."
"Profess your undying love to every person you can see whenever you hear an animal's call."

"Ask every other person you meet if it is their birthday. .If If it it is, is, give them a gift. If they hair is blonde, red or multi coloured, give them four handfuls of dirt in a satchel instead." The DM may roll a d100 if they haven't decided if the person's birthday is today, with it being their birthday on a roll of 91 or greater. If the result is 1, they were born on a leap year."
"Throw the remains of the first meal you have today in a trash bin. Collect the bin and toss it at who cooked this meal."
"Ask the nearest person to name a profession. Gain employment in that profession within a week and quit on the fifth day of employment."
"Ignore anyone taller than you. Gift one gold piece to any being shorter than you."
"Put on clown make-up and use juggling pins as your weapon until you knock down a living thing."

"Give this prescript to the second person you greet today and tell them to follow this Prescript." If any creature fails to conclude this Prescript, the paper explodes into light and carves a number equal to the number of times this Prescript was concluded into the back of the hand of its last courier's.
"Open your bag, place the nearest object that will fit into it, carry it for three hours. Do not answer why."
"Remove a single item from your possession and give it to the first person you make eye contact with. Then walk backwards 10 feet."

"Pickup the first object that can fit into your hand, name it, carry it, and treat it as if it were a capable of speaking to you for the remainder of the day. Dump it into the nearest body of water at the end of the day."
"Walk in a circle, then stare at the third person you see for 6 seconds. Afterwards, wave at them and proceed to not look at them for at least 3 hours."
"Maintain eye contact with anyone you see until they blink. Do not blink until then."
"Whenever you hear a spell being cast by someone else, stare at its caster's eyes for at least six seconds."
"Wear a bucket on your head for the entire day. Do not answer why. Do not acknowledge the bucket."
"Light any graves or rotting meat you see between this sunrise and the next using a flint and steel."
"Whenever you feel pain, tell a secret less than ten people know."
"Adopt a pet. Name them after someone you hate and buy them at least one piece of jewelry."
"Do not eat, drink or sleep for the next three days. After the 72nd hour comes to pass, write down your current thoughts in a paper, fold it between your fingers and sleep in a public space."

"For three hours you may only speak in a language outside of your common tongue. You may convey meanings through hand gestures, movements, and examples. You may not in any way speak in your common tongue."
"Introduce another person of your choice to the concept of Prescripts and turn them into a neophyte."
"Write an autobiography. Gift the manuscript to the third person you meet."
"Carve a path leading into the heart of the nearest woods or similar ecosystem."
"Swap your left index finger with your right index finger and your right index finger with your left index finger."
"Break the thumbs of anyone you see that is wearing red."
"At some point in the day, capture a small animal, carry it with you, feed it a portion of your meal when you eat. Release it after the first time you feed it."
"Wear a different hairstyle. If anyone comments about it, ask them if they like it."

"Tattoo the name of the first person you've ever felt romantic love toward in the back of your neck. If you have not felt romantic love toward a person, tattoo your favourite word on your left hand's knuckles."
"Jump through every window you see once."
"Do not tell a lie until midnight. Afterward, spend the next hour alone.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: When creating a character who follows the Living Will, it's recommended to sit down and talk to your Dungeon Master about how to best develop a faction of other followers into the setting you wish to play in, as this subclass heavily interacts with fellow followers of the Will. For DMs, consider creating Messenger NPCs that are the usual deliverer's of prescripts towards your player and other followers, also using these Prescripts outside of the pre-written ones from tables to include your own plot-hooks through these orders.

subclassFeature.name: Path of Precognition
entries: {@i "… I've already waited way past with what anyone oughta put up with. And right when I thought I was finally getting my ass outta this goddamn cold, what happens? My Ticket turns into blank scrap paper, all because of that mongrel brat! Ha… Haha… Gimme a fucking break."}

You have found a powerful relic capable of seeing a few seconds into the future, and you have repurposed it into one of your eyes so that your enemies never reach you again. When it overheats, so does your rage, allowing you to hit your enemies with incredible might as a practicioner of La Spada di Palermo, a powerful and fast sword style that confuses most opponents.

You are a washed-up member of the Thumb, a powerful criminal syndicate that values hierarchy above all else. Maybe you were a powerful leader that fell from grace, or you never amounted to much to begin with, but the Thumb has assigned you to be one of the lowest of the low.

Barbarians from the Path of Precognition tend to believe they know everything, and all outcomes were obvious for them. At their best, they are wise leaders that guide their underlings to be their best. At their worst, they're manipulative and vindictive, trying

subclassFeature.name: The Eye of Precognition
entries: {@i "What, having a hard time landing a hit?"}
You have 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. While you have counts of this, you gain the following benefits:

items: Your walking speed increases by 10 feet
Your Armor Class increases by 3

When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

entries: Whenever you hit with an attack, you lose 1 count of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. Likewise, you lose 3 counts whenever a creature misses an attack against you due to your AC bonus, and 5 counts whenever you take no damage after succeeding on a Dexterity saving throw.

Once you lose all counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, you immediately gain 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition - Overheat|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. While you have counts of this, you gain the following characteristics:

items: You always roll an additional damage die of the weapon you are attacking with
Your Armor Class decreases by 3
Whenever taking Fire damage, take an additional damage die of the same value as your eye socket burns.

entries: Whenever you hit with an attack, you lose 1 count of {@condition Eye of Precognition - Overheat|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. Likewise, you lose 3 counts whenever a creature hits an attack against you due to your AC decrease, and 3 counts whenever you take additional Fire damage from a hostile source. Once you lose all counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition - Overheat|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, you immediately gain 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

After completing a Long Rest, you immediately lose all counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition - Overheat|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} and gain up to 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, ensuring you have that maximum count of the Condition.

subclassFeature.name: Colpi di Taglio
entries: {@i "… I've already waited way past what anyone oughta put up with. And right when I thought I was finally getting my ass outta this goddamn cold, what happens? My Ticket turns into blank scrap paper, all because of that mongrel brat! Ha… Haha… Gimme a fucking break."}
This is done through dual weapons, allowing you to make perfected use of Two-Weapon Fighting:

items: You may wield two weapons without the prerequisite of one of them being Light, instead only requiring that neither weapon is Heavy.

Whenever you make an {@action Attack} as per Two-Weapon Fighting rules you still add half your ability modifier to the damage dealt. Whenever you do so, you choose whether you inflict 2 counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on your target, or triggering a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Upon reaching level 10, this count increases to 4.
When you Attune to a pair of magical weapons, they both count as a singular Attunement, taking only one slot and becoming Unattuned if either Attunement is broken.

entries: Additionally, whenever a creature misses you with an attack you may spend your Reaction to use {@i Sezionatura di Coniglio} as an attack against that creature. You may do so an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus per short or long rest.
When entering your Rage, you may use {@i Sezionatura di Coniglio} as an attack against a creature within range without expending a use of the feature.

entries.name: Sezionatura di Coniglio
entries: On a hit, you deal damage as usual and the creature suffers 1 count of both {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Additionally, if you are raging, you gain 1 count of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Creatures that are Small or smaller hit by this attack have disadvantage on their next attack roll.

subclassFeature.name: The Shame of My Famiglia
entries: {@i "… Tsk. Great. Not a single damn idiot left to call over for a drink… Bunch of weak-ass pushovers. Got chewed up by those disgusting bugs and died like trash."}

You have lost a position of power important to you, or perhaps something similar, and it has been difficult for you to recover ever since. You have advantage on saving throws against becoming drunk. You refuse to drink {@item ale (gallon)|PHB|Ale}, but after consuming an entire {@item Fine Wine (bottle)|PHB|bottle of Fine Wine}, you may choose to immediately become affected by the {@condition Drunk|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} condition for 1 minute. You gain the following characteristics when affected by the {@condition Drunk|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} condition:

items: You have disadvantage on {@skill Perception} checks, Strength, Dexterity and Constitution saving throws and ranged attacks.
As a bonus action, you can yell at one of your allies to do better, granting them advantage on their next ability check, saving throw or attack roll, your choice

When you hit a creature that is {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burning}, {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Tremoring}, or Both, you deal an additional {@damage 1d6} die of damage of equal damage to your weapon's damage type
You can substitute one of your attacks for a {@i Sezionatura di Cervo}.

entries.name: Sezionatura di Cervo
entries: On a hit, you deal damage as usual and the creature suffers 1 count of both {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Additionally, if you are raging, you gain 1 count of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Creatures that are Medium or smaller hit by this attack have disadvantage on their next attack roll.

subclassFeature.name: Accelerating Future
entries: {@i "Feelin' confident? Then parry this, asshole."}

As a battle drives on, you have learned how to mark your favored enemies, focusing all of your wrath on a specific being instead of lashing out wildly like a volcano. You may choose to make the last creature you attacked on your turn become your {@condition Game Target|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. When you hit your {@condition Game Target|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} with an attack roll, once per turn, you may choose to convert all of their counts of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} into {@condition Tremor - Scorch|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Tremor Scorch}. Furthermore, whenever you apply counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, to your {@condition Game Target|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, they suffer 1 additional count of each applied.

Additionally, you have learned how to devote extra energy to your {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} to calculate the most likely outcome of the near future. As an action, you can expend 5 counts of your {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} to see 1 minute into the future and discover what the most possible outcomes are. Alternatively, by suffering 1 point of {@condition Exhaustion}, you can see 10 minutes into the future instead.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: This ability is left more vague on purpose for DMs and players to have more fun with it, however, I think it's important to give an example of how it can and can't be used to make it clearer.

Let's say you're trying to find out what to bet on in a cassino, or what an NPC will say before they say it - those things are fully under the DM's control and he should be able to disclose the most likely future according to the perception of your eye.

However, things outside of the DM's control, such as what a player character would do/say or the outcome of a combat decided by the dice, are much less likely to be predicted, so your eyes can provide an incorrect assessment of the furure, or no assessment at all.

subclassFeature.name: Sezionatura di Elefante
entries: {@i "… Tsk. Great. Not a single damn idiot left to call over for a drink… Bunch of weak-ass pushovers. Got chewed up by those disgusting bugs and died like trash."}

You swing your blade with enough strength and speed to leave even the wisest of men unable to comprehend your movements without slowing them down. While raging, you may perform an additional bonus action attack as per Two-Weapon Fighting rules, however, this attack only inflicts 1 count of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Furthermore, you gain 2 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and creatures that are Large or smaller hit by this attack have disadvantage on their next attack roll. If you managed to hit the same creature with all four of your attacks, they must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC = 8 + your Constitution modifier + your Proficiency Bonus) or suffer the effects of the {@spell Confusion} spell until the end of their next turn.

entries.name: Disposal
entries: If you managed to hit the same creature with all four of your attacks and that creature is your {@condition Game Target|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, you may trigger {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on that creature twice, only expending all counts of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} after the second burst. If that kills it, you may perform this ability one more time. Otherwise, you may only perform this ability once per Short or Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Fluttering Life Domain
entries: {@i "Where do humans go upon the final egress from life? You ask a rather stimulating question. I have once written my reflections on the end of life; perhaps we may have a chance to discuss it later."}

A buttefly soars freely through the world, needing not the wind to propel its sails nor a great will to guide its whims. Those who have chosen to dutifully follow the domain of a Fluttering Life srive to be much like that, to find, enact and nurture this freedom to live life through all the sorrows that death brings, acting often not as evangelists but instead as travelling undertakers and funeral orators.

They, at their worst, may come off as stark or even have a downlifting aura about their dour workings, yet when allowed to practice freely they usually become stalwart pillars of comfort and calm enforcers of welcoming acceptance of passing on.

In worlds such as Eberron, these first rose from the cracked ground as manifestation of the battlefields - Undead beings of solidified sorrows that roamed the earth and passed down their teachings not to end undeath of itself, but to finally allow those that couldn't to finally find peace. In others, such as that of the grim lands of Balefire beat their boots through the entire world as a rare, unseen sight - Preventing the malaise of souls from spreading by exhuming the bodies of the fallen and being one of the few, few people who fight back flame not with more flame, but instead with extinguishing the pain that yet assails the world.

subclassFeature.name: Blink, Gone
entries: {@i "It would have been nice to have those who would lament my passing, yet the remembrance of the dead has no place in the hearts of those who live here."}

The butterflies of the afterlife have come to rest their weary wings upon your shoulders, much as you have been trained and ordained as a grave keeper of sorts - caring and nurturing for the dead and passing on of the world. These butterflies, spirits of transience, have chosen to aid you in your goals just as you aid them - Whenever you make a hit a creature you inflict {@condition Butterfly|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count equal to half your proficiency bonus. Whenever you hit multiple hostile creatures with a spell or they fail a saving throw from your spells you instead cause each creature to suffer an amount of {@condition Butterfly|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} equal to half your proficiency bonus plus the spell slot level consumed, split equally amongst every target of the spell. ( To a minimum of one. )

Additionally, these butterflies that surround you have a tendency to perch upon the bodies of those that linger to pass on, giving you Advantage on {@skill Insight} and {@skill Perception} checks to perceive a creature as being of the Undead type. Furthermore, if you cast the {@spell Find Familiar} spell you may choose to summon your familiar as a kaleidoscope of these butterflies, a group that remains with you for prolonged periods of time. These use the {@creature Owl} stat sheet except they are a Medium swarm of Tiny Undead and have the {@i Tranquillity} trait appended to their sheet, as per what is presented below.

entries.name: Tranquillity
entries: The Kaleidoscope of Dead Butterflies uses your Spellcasting modifier, including any bonuses from magical divine foci, to their {@skill Insight} checks to detect the presence of Undead creatures within 15-ft. of themselves and to discern another creatures Alignment. They may report back to you any information gleamed this way through ethereal whispers of a gentle nature.

subclassFeature.name: Celebration for the Departed
entries: {@i "The barrel of the gun does not fire bullets of butterflies; it is merely that butterflies, both living and dead, bloom from where the gun points."}

The memory of fireworks is one that warms the hearts of many people, calling to attention a blast of heat that warms the heart as much as it does the body. You might have come to harbour something near such memories, yet the principle of a spectacle to remark on the importance of life isn't ever lost on you, and that manifests in your weapons of choice. You gain proficiency in Firearms and due to a gathering of knowledge pertaining to celebrations and ceremonies, you are uniquely qualified to preside over funerals and to safely guide souls to a peaceful afterlife.

You may perform funeral rites over a period of at least an hour, granting a lifted weight for the living, yet guaranteeing the restfulness of the dead. The dead subject of this ceremony cannot be revived through any means other than {@spell True Resurrection} under the condition of the spirit being willing as well and may not be contacted through means such as the {@spell Speak with Dead} spell.

To properly complete this ritual you need at least the body of a deceased creature or an item of great importance of the dead. They may be of undead type, but must be Unconscious and willing for the whole duration to become departed.

subclassFeature.name: Domain Extended Spells
entries: {@i "I fear letting even the lightest wisp of frivolity upon this lament... Thus, it's only right that I wreath solemnness upon my heart as I pull their triggers."}

The domain which presides upon the transient state of life unto death concerns itself on the matters regarding both the living and the departed equally, seeing to guide any lingering spirits to the great beyond and make sure any funeral procession goes accomplished without issue.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: Solemn Lament for the Living
entries: Starting at 2nd level, you can use your Channel Divinity to summon and unseal a great coffin that leads into where the dead go to rest, then retrieving the tools for your grave keeping amongst the living.
As an action, you raise your holy symbol and cause a coffin to raise from ethereal mists, then grab one of the following weapons of your choice:

entries.name: Condolences and Eternal Rest
entries: You retrieve a pair of twin revolvers that remain in inverse colours to one another, a set of tools to reap life from those that should remain dead. These have the {@itemProperty Light}, Range (30/60-ft.) and {@itemProperty RLD|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Reload} (6) weapon properties and deal {@damage 1d8} of your choice of radiant or necrotic damage.

entries.name: Quiet Coffin. ( Requires at least 8th Level. )
entries: You forgo simply retrieving a weapon from the inside of the coffin, instead grabbing the coffin itself and shifting its material form to be that of a heavy machine gun. It has the {@itemProperty BST|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burst Fire} (PB), {@itemProperty Heavy}, {@itemProperty RLD|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Reload} (PB) and {@itemProperty Two-Handed|PHB|Two-handed} weapon properties, yet whenever you take the {@action Attack} Action using this weapon you have a reach of a 45-ft. cone starting from you instead of having to select a single target. You roll a single attack roll whose result is considered against the AC of all hostile creatures within that reach, dealing your choice of {@damage 1d4} radiant or necrotic damage. If you make use of this weapon's {@itemProperty BST|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burst Fire} feature you may only select one target for all your attacks.

All these weapons count as divine foci for you, Whenever the {@condition Butterfly|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} Condition would be inflicted through your spells and you are using weapons from this Channel Divinity as your divine focus, you use your full proficiency bonus instead of half that value. ( Whenever aiming at a single or multiple targets. ) And provided you are wielding these weapons only, you inflict an additional {@condition Butterfly|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count whenever you deal damage to a target
To reload these weapons you use no form of bullet, instead relying on the dead butterflies that kindly offer themselves as a source of ammunition.
These weapons also grow in power in tandem with you, becoming +1 magic weapons when you reach 5th level, +2 at 10th level and a +3 at 17th level.

Lastly, these weapons remain corporeal for one minute until they dissipate in thin air. For the duration you may summon a kaleidoscope of butterflies to aid you in locating the dead and undead within a range of 300-ft times the magic weapon bonus you gain from this feature, instantly allowing you to find the general direction of the aforementioned beings provided they are not actively entombed through walls of stone or metal that are at least 5-ft.
{@i He's carrying a coffin. A large coffin to pay tribute to the employees who have nowhere else to go. It is still too small to comfort those innocent sacrifices.}

subclassFeature.name: To Embrace a Fleeting Moment in Life Toward Stillness of Death
entries: {@i "Well do I understand your sentiment on death. Why not lay rest to the impulses in your heart for a moment and converse with me more?"}

Even in a fight you've trained your thoughts to remain calm, to be a guiding light to all those around you. This training has also resulted in a demeanour that pacifies the pain in one's ailing mind to provide at least a moment's clarity. You gain a +2 bonus modifier on {@skill Insight} and Charisma skill checks regarding conversing with the Undead and while within 10-ft. of you, they regain at least the faintest hint of their memories and personality. - enough to enable conversation in the first place. Additionally you may use your Bonus Action to calm Undead creatures and similarly unliving beings. All Undead creatures within 60-ft. that can hear you must pass a Wisdom saving throw against your Cleric Spell Save DC or become {@condition Charmed} by you and non-hostile toward creatures that haven't attacked them for the next minute, awakening some spark of sentience in them.

You do not gain this feature's skill check bonus modifier if the Undead are actively hostile to you or if you have dealt damage to them within the past hour. You may use this feature an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per short or long rest.

Whenever you calm Undead in this way, a butterfly perches upon the shoulder of the yet-to-be-departed, granting them a +1 bonus to Wisdom saving throws and they may choose to spend their Action to instantly die in peace. Upon reaching 20th level in this subclass, whenever a creature dies this way any curse or negative effect of your choice that would be caused, activated or maintained is instantly negated and lifted.

You may give these butterflies to friendly creatures within 15-ft. of you as a Bonus Action, spending an use of the feature. An ally remains with a butterfly for a minute before it flutters off, gaining the same Wisdom saving throw bonus and reducing any {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count they suffer by one. ( To a minimum of one. )
These bonus modifiers to your skill checks and Wisdom saving throws is increased by 1 upon you reaching 12th level in this class.

subclassFeature.name: Hallowed Strikes
entries: {@i "It is a heavy gift that I shoulder a twain of wayward souls in each of my palms, fingers held ever-closer."}

At 8th level, the cleric gains the ability to infuse their weapon strikes with a mixture of balancing energy. Once on each of the cleric's turns when they hit a creature with a weapon attack, the cleric can cause the attack to deal an extra {@damage 1d4} necrotic damage to the target whenever they deal radiant damage, and the inverse when dealing necrotic damage. When the cleric reaches 14th level, the extra damage increases to {@damage 2d4}.

subclassFeature.name: Goodbye Now, A Sorrow in You
entries: {@i "At the heart of a broken mirror, I see the fading butterfly. A wandering butterfly I cannot bloom, yet the duty of lamentation is mine, thus, it is also mine, this melancholy."}

You come to reach a point where you lead a calm life despite all that assails your life, embracing the transience of life as a simple fact, much like day slips into night and night to day. To that end, your lectures toward the dead have come to be an aura that follows you to the ends of the earth. You gain the following:

items: Whenever a creature that you can see dies within 60-ft. of you a small collection of butterflies crowd toward you, granting you two {@condition Butterfly|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count. This Condition has no effect on you and does not change or diminish at the end of your turns, instead you gain a +1 bonus modifier to Wisdom saving throws for each 4 count you currently have, to a maximum of +3. Whenever you would inflict {@condition Butterfly|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} on a creature, you may choose to spend from your count to add the same amount to theirs.
You always have the {@spell Ceremony|XGE} spell prepared and may cast it at will without spending a spell slot.

Creatures that you lay to rest ( through killing or through use of any of your features ) may choose to linger on as a butterfly, using the {@creature Owl} stat sheet except they may speak telepathically through any language they knew in life and they instantly die when wandering further than 360-ft. of you. They become neutral toward you if they were hostile but are otherwise friendly and calm toward you. You may use their butterfly body to revive them through a {@spell Resurrection} or greater spell without requiring their original body.

subclassFeature.name: Way of Crumbling Enlightenment
entries: {@i "Remember not only to refill what you have burned out but also to add new knowledge into your repositories.""}

Knowledge and the body are an organism when in combination, the brain's synapses leading to the fists clenching and bursting forward in a coordinated transfer of energy for devastating power. Monks who dwell in the sects of Enlightenment know this well, and cultivate their minds to accumulate as much intelligence as possible, then taking it apart crumb by crumb to fuel their arts.

Often cloistered with their fellows, these are also the keepers of vast reliquaries that do well in archival and retrieval of all manner of great item that was misplaced or forlorn to time, also holding out special holdings in the nourishing of young minds within their ranks, often acting as orphanages just as well.

entries.subclassFeature: Gathering of Knowledge as Kindling|Monk|PHB|Crumbling Enlightenment|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|3

subclassFeature.name: Gathering of Knowledge as Kindling
entries: {@i "Remember not only to refill what you have burned but also to add new knowledge into your repositories."}

Your free time is often spent in the dwellings of books, absorbing knowledge as if it were oxygen. Whenever you take a long rest you may choose to become Proficient in two skills you weren't Proficient with, then having these Proficiencies lost at the next long rest as the knowledge fades from your mind as you make space for more.

Yet the wisdom imparted to you is left not only in theory, but also used to glimpse {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}s of the world and its ways in a practical manner. You may do the following to gain counts of {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, which is used to fuel certain abilities or to passively bolden yourself:

items: You may spend a Bonus Action to instantly forget one of your skill Proficiencies, gaining 2 {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count.
You may spend a Bonus Action to instantly forget one of your Artisan's Tools, Instrument or Gaming Kit Proficiencies, gaining 1 {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count.

entries: Whenever you forget a proficiency you effectively juxtapose that piece of knowledge to re-frame the world in front of you, aiding in the connection and conceptualization of ideas you may not have seen before, yet you also forget the original purpose of this piece of intelligence, having its base set to crumble within the annals of your mind. You lose the ability to use your proficiency bonus in rolls regarding the lost proficiency until the end of your next long rest.

While you have {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} you gain a bonus modifier to unarmed attacks and Intelligence skill checks equal to half of your current count of the Condition. Additionally, you gain a bonus modifier to your Intelligence saving throws and skill checks equal to your current count. You may have a maximum count of the Condition equal to your proficiency bonus.

If you spend Ki to perform an ability that requires you to have a minimum amount of {@condition Insight|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, you lose one count at the end of your turns. Otherwise, your count is reduced by one per minute spent outside of combat.

subclassFeature.name: Means of Cultivation
entries: {@i "Grow your knowledge. Use exams to motivate and push yourselves further. Only then shall you one day be permitted an audience with the Saints."}

Upon reaching 3rd level in Monk, choose which way you will proceed to acquire your knowledge with - a perception-bending key to your knowledge or to hold and tear it off with your bare hands. You gain the chosen 3rd level feat and a corresponding one upon reaching 11th level.

To Behold Light Through a Gilded Keyhole (Key)|Monk|PHB|Crumbling Enlightenment|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|3

subclassFeature.name: To Behold Light Through a Gilded Keyhole (Key)
entries: {@i "I'm sure you would like to know more about this… key. Hmm~ How do I put this? It's a medium…? A vessel for knowledge…? Kinda hard to explain to someone who hasn't used it before."}

You are of a sect which makes use of special relics to glimpse newfound expertise directly, being one of the select number who learnt how to maximize learning in this way. You carry a gigantic Key of Knowledge, a magic item you are permanently attuned to that doesn't count toward your attunement limit. You gain the following benefits when you choose this feature:

items: Your Key of Knowledge counts as a monk weapon for you and you deal an additional 2 {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on weapon attacks while wielding it. This increases by one upon reaching 8th level in this class.
