You and any other {@condition Fanatic|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} creatures within 30-ft. of you while you are a {@condition Fanatic|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} yourself gain a +2 bonus to Wisdom saving throws, Advantage against being {@condition frightened} and Immunity to being {@condition charmed}.

Creatures who became {@condition Fanatic|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} through you inflict one {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count on a hit and suffer one roll of their Hit Die of psychic damage at the end of their turns. This damage cannot be reduced in any way.
Creatures Immobilized by your Crucifixion ability are instead {@condition paralyzed} until the end of your next turn.
You also gain a +1 modifier to damage for every +1 modifier attack rolls granted by creatures suffering from {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Nails}.
You cannot have your Hit Points reduced below 1 by psychic damage.

If you would be a target to an effect that would cause you to become or {@condition frightened} you may once per long rest spend your Reaction to instantly become a {@condition Fanatic|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} until the source of the Condition is dead or has been out of your sight for at least an hour. If you become or {@condition frightened}, your faith crumbles and pierces through your mind though. Any positive modifiers you would have to rolls instead become negative modifiers, such as your Strength modifier to attack and you suffer {@damage 2d12} psychic damage at the end of your turns while suffering from the Condition.

entries: Additionally, you may indoctrinate other creatures to partake in your faith during long rests. After doing so once, indoctrinated creatures gain an {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to {@skill Religion} checks until their next long rest. Upon doing so twice, they gain {@dice 1d6} instead. Upon the third time, they become permanently Proficient in the skill instead. If you have Expertise in Religion, any creature who has spent fourteen long rests being indoctrinated by you gains Expertise in Religion permanently.

subclassFeature.name: Corporist Specialization
entries: You have decided to lead your very own artistic movement inspired by the hidden beauty inside every living creature. Artificers with the Corporist Specialization aren't afraid to get their hands bloody in search of materials for their craft. To them, the anatomy of every living being is a canvas waiting to be turned into art, and you always research the best methods to heed their call.

subclassFeature.name: Corporist Spells
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Corporist Spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don't count against the number of artificer spells you prepare.

entries.caption: Corporist Spells
rows: 3rd
{@spell charm person}, {@spell inflict wounds}
5th
{@spell hold person}, {@spell spike growth}
9th
{@spell animate dead}, {@spell fear}
13th
{@spell dimension door}, {@spell grasping vine}
17th
{@spell dominate person}, {@spell raise dead}

subclassFeature.name: Anatomize
entries: {@i "Let us explore together—the pulsations of your remaining life."}

Taking parts of others for your creations, your art, is something you have learned to do with great pride. You acquire one {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count whenever you successfully deal damage to a creature within 15-ft. of you. You have a count limit equal to double your proficiency bonus, and due to a tendency to dutifully spend any leftovers on smaller projects during a short or long rest, you may only have up to your proficiency bonus worth of {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} after such.

Additionally, you gain Proficiency with the {@skill Nature} skill. If you already have Proficiency with it, you gain Expertise instead. Your anatomical knowledge knows no bounds, and you always have advantage on anatomy-related checks.

{@b My, How We Love the Flesh and the Blood.} If a {@subclass Iron Maiden|Druid|PHB|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Circle of the Iron Maiden} Druid is within 30 feet of you and makes an attack roll, you can use your Reaction to give that attack advantage. If it hits, it deals an additional {@damage 1d6} Slashing damage and the creature suffers 1 additional count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. This number increases to 2 at level 5, 3 at level 11 and 4 at level 17. After using this ability, if the {@subclass Iron Maiden|Druid|PHB|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Circle of the Iron Maiden} Druid gains {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} due to this attack, you gain the same amount.

subclassFeature.name: Magnum Opus: Tibia
entries: {@i "What do you see... in this piece? I am curious to hear your impressions."}

Your very own body gave birth to the skeletal artifact resting in your hands. It is a Martial Melee weapon that you are considered Attuned with at all times. It counts as a magic item for the purposes of bypassing Resistances and it usually takes the shape of a large sword made out of bones, a complete extension of your old body. It deals {@damage 1d8} slashing damage, has the Reach property, inflicts 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and you may choose to use your Intelligence modifier for its attack and damage rolls.

This weapon is considered an Artifact and can only be destroyed upon a century passing after your death. If it is lost - no, it must never be. Your sole mission must be to keep your Magnum Opus on your person the entire time. You will gain an anxious obsession to recover it otherwise, and will not be able to focus on anything else, gaining disadvantage on any ability checks unrelated to finding it, but advantage on all ability checks related to finding it.
Over the course of a Long Rest, you may spend an amount of {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} equal to your Proficiency Modifier to permanently upgrade it, as per the following:

items: Your attack and damage rolls with your Magnum Opus increase by +1. When you take it again, it increases by +1 again, to a maximum of +3.
You inflict an additional count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on enemies that you hit. Whenever you take this again, you inflict an additional count.
Your Magnum Opus's damage becomes {@damage 1d10}. When you take it again, it becomes {@damage 1d12}.
Your Reach extends by 5 feet and the range of all of your abilities extends by 10 feet. When you take it again, both increase by 5 and 10 feet more respectively.
Rolls of 19 or 20 are considered Critical hits for the purpose of your skills that require Critical Hits. When you take this upgrade again, that number becomes 18.

You can strip a magical weapon bare and feed its scraps to your Magnum Opus over the course of a long rest. The magical item used is permanently destroyed and your Magnum Opus gains its properties, such as a Vorpal Sword's Vorpal enchantment, but not any increases to attack and damage rolls. You may only benefit from a single magical weapon consumed like this at any given time, needing to strip your work to fit another weapon if you wish to do so.

You can use a Bonus Action to point your Magnum Opus at a creature and give them advantage on their next ability check, attack roll or saving throw. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a Long Rest.

After you hit a creature with an attack you can use a Reaction to tear away some of the creature's flesh. They must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become {@condition frightened} of you for 1 minute. Creatures {@condition frightened} this way always suffer an additional count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} whenever it is inflicted and may reroll their saving throws at the end of each of their turn, ending the effect on a success. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a Long Rest.

You can use a Bonus Action to pose with your Magnum Opus. Choose a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. They must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or become {@condition charmed} by you for 1 minute. Creatures that are fighting you have advantage on this saving throw. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a Long Rest.

You can use an Action to extend your weapon and ensnare someone. Choose a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. They must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become Grappled by you and your weapon for 1 minute, and your movement speed is not halved due to the Grapple. Creatures Grappled this way may reroll their saving throws at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success.

As an Action, you may cleave your Magnum Opus across a 15-foot cone in front of you. Every creature in this cone must make a Dexterity saving throw. For any creature that fails the save, choose an order. The first one to fail the save takes {@damage 1d6} Slashing damage, the second takes {@damage 2d6}, and this continues to a maximum of {@damage 4d6} Slashing damage. Every creature that failed the save also suffers 2 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. On a successful save, they only take half damage and suffer no additional effects.

You may use an Action to thrust your Magnum Opus forward in a 30 foot line. Any creature within that line must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become {@condition Heavy Blood|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Heavily Bleeding}. {@condition Heavy Blood|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Heavily Bleeding} instead causes the afflicted creature to suffer {@damage 2d6} damage on the same triggers as the previous Condition and 2 stacks are removed every time it is triggered. The {@skill Medicine} Check required to remove this Condition is increased by 5.

As part of your attack action, you may attempt a vertical attack roll against a creature within Reach. On a hit, they take the damage they normally would and fall {@condition Prone}. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a Long Rest.

As an Action, you may spend 3 {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} to attempt to immobilize a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you. They must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become {@condition restrained} for 1 minute. Creatures {@condition restrained} this way may reroll their saving throws at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success. (lvl 9)

As an Action, you enlarge your sword, making it pierce everything in a 30-foot line. Creatures within that line must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take {@damage 5d8} Piercing damage and gain disadvantage on Strength, Dexterity and Constitution saving throws for 1 minute unless they're healed. This cannot be removed while the creature suffering from it is {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Bleeding}. On a successful save, a creature only takes half the amount of damage and suffers no additional effects. (lvl 9)

As an Action, you shoot a tendon from your sword to wrap around another creature. They must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become puppeteered by you. Immediately after failing this saving throw and on your subsequent turns, you may spend a Bonus Action to force the creature to perform any Action it is able to for you on any target within reach. They may reroll their saving throws at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success. You can only use this ability once per Short or Long Rest. (lvl 9)

As part of your attack action with your Magnum Opus, you may attempt to hit a creature in a vital spot. They must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or become {@condition paralyzed} until the end of your next turn. You can only use this feature once per creature per combat. (lvl 9)

As part of your attack action with your Magnum Opus, you gut the creature in front of you. They must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or suffer 1 point of {@condition exhaustion}. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a Long Rest. (lvl 9)

You pierce your Magnum Opus on the floor, extending its bones underground to hit every creature of your choice within 20 feet of you. The area becomes Difficult Terrain for creatures that are not a part of the Ring and the targets must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 4d6} Piercing damage and suffer 2 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, and you may spend 3 {@condition Corpus Ingredients|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} so that the next attack against each of the affected creatures is done with advantage. On a successful save, they take half the damage and suffer no additional effects. You can only use this ability once per Short or Long Rest. (lvl 9)

Immediately after you kill a creature, you may add parts of its corpse to your Magnum Opus, gaining access to one of their Actions. You can only have 2 different creature actions at a time with this ability. (lvl 15)

As an Action, you can target a creature that you can see within 30 feet of you and extend your Magnum Opus to reach for it. If they have 50 hit points or fewer, they instantly die. Otherwise, they must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 10d8} Piercing damage, suffer 3 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and are immediately pulled towards you. On a successful save, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects. You can only use this ability once per Short or Long Rest. (lvl 15)

entries: You may take each upgrade only once, with the exception of being able to take upgrades marked by your Magnum Opus an additional time upon reaching 5th and 15th levels in Artificer. You are aware that a crowded piece that attempts to convey everything at once is heard by none, so your maximum amount of upgrades is equal to your Known Infusions count and you may exchange an existing one with the same process of creating one. Whenever this feature asks for a saving throw, the Save DC is equal to your Artificer Spell Save DC.

subclassFeature.name: Artful Extra Attack
entries: {@i "Please, do share your impressions!"}

Starting at 5th level, you can attack twice, rather than once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. Additionally, whenever you land a Critical Hit, you get to add your Charisma modifier to the damage.

subclassFeature.name: Gallery Ingredient — A Bloodied Ring
entries: {@i "Allow me to play the curator for our guests—from kitsch to avant-garde, delving deep into each trend of art movement."}

You have developed an extradimensional key that leads you to your very own Gallery of the Ring within its many Corridors. You now have a small key that can be recreated on a Short or Long Rest if lost or destroyed, destroying the old one upon recreation. You can use an Action to insert it into a door or into a space that could be considered a gate between two rooms or spaces, creating a portal to your personal gallery which you immediately enter. Your gallery is 60 feet long and 35 feet wide, with 20-foot high ceilings. Only creatures you allow inside the gallery can enter it with an Action. The interior is completely white, and furnished with pedestals that you can store your various creations inside. Only you can store, remove or give permission to store or remove items in the pedestals.

Creatures can remain inside the gallery up to a number of hours equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus. Creatures exit the gallery early if they use a Bonus Action to leave, if you die, or if the key is destroyed. Creatures can only leave if you allow them to or if you're unconscious. When any creature exits the gallery, they appear in the unoccupied space closest to it. Any objects left in the gallery remain there until carried out, but every creature is expelled in a similar manner to you. If the key is destroyed, every object stored there harmlessly appears in the unoccupied spaces closest to the key's former space. Once you enter the gallery, you can't enter again until you finish a Long Rest.
The key's AC equals your spell save DC. Its hit points equal your Artificer level plus your Proficiency Bonus, and it is Immune to Poison and Psychic damage.
Additionally, when you score a Critical Hit, you regain one use of your Flash of Genius ability.

{@b Installation Art no. 3: Improvised Ribcage.} While inside your gallery, you can use an Action to summon rib cages around a creature that you can see within the gallery in attempts to imprison it. They must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or become {@condition restrained} for a minute. They may reroll this saving throw at the end of each of their turns, ending this effect on a success.

subclassFeature.name: Greta's Melody — Anatomization of the Unanatomized by the Anatomized
entries: {@i "What a beautiful hue it has. A piece worthy of its own pedestal."}

You've become a true master of anatomy, able to bend any bone and tendon to your will. If you kill a non-Construct creature of CR 10 or lower, you may choose to store its body with you until your next Long Rest, during which you may transform it into an Automanikin and revive it under your command. This creature has the same stat block as the original creature, except its creature type is Construct. It listens to your commands as a Bonus Action, but will take the Dodge action if not commanded to do anything else during that turn. Alternatively, you can use an Action to transform Humanoids you have killed into Automanikins. Immediately after creating them, you may order them as part of the same Action to do something, and they will attempt to complete that order to the best of their abilities until they die or the order changes. You can have a maximum number of Automanikins equal to your Proficiency Bonus if they're CR 2 or lower Humanoids, or only one if they are non-humanoid or higher than CR 2.

{@b Closing Time - Installation Art no. 1: Your Flesh and Bones as the Gallery's Seats.} As an Action inside your gallery, you may have any of your art pieces expand their bones and puncture creatures nearby. Choose any number of creatures that you can see up to your Proficiency Bonus. They must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC or be pierced, taking {@damage 8d6} Piercing damage and having to roll on the Lingering Injuries Table. If this kills a creature, they are immediately added to your gallery as one of its sculptures. Once you use this feature, you can only use it again after a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Memoir of a Fallen Stigma
entries: {@i "A single bullet ain't enough..."}

You and the concept of the hunt have been lost in smoke for years, granting you the capability to make manifest fallen memories as if they were still lingering spirits on the world. Once per long rest you may summon two ghoulish apparitions of conflicts past to occupy any unoccupied space you can see within 60-ft. of you.

These beings use the {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} Memory sheet and are unable to speak and are subjugated by your own will, being considered friendly to you regardless of their disposition, they are forced to follow your orders regardless of if it would endanger them.

The appearance of these creatures are usually that of a hazy selection of faces that you have met and taken down in the past - be they friend or foe. You may Bellow Orders as a Free Action during your turn or between other creature's turns, before or after they act.

subclassFeature.name: Curse-Wrought Bullets
entries: {@i "There is neither; no fragments of memories, no need to look into them... fire, only fire!"}

Whatever you touch eventually becomes tainted by the weight of memories you will never be able to run from, yet you have learnt how to focus the smog on your soul into a single point. At the start of your turns you may choose to have a creature become {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, the centre of your everlasting hatred. You may only do so provided there is no creature already {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, or you can use your Bonus Action to switch the victim of your Stigma.

Whenever you hit a creature with a ranged weapon attack you gain 1 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and inflict 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, whenever you hit a {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} creature, gain two additional counts as well.

Whenever you kill a {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} creature you gain {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your proficiency bonus and one {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count, as the already dissolving mental image of that which you have shattered lingers on in your aim. If you kill or knock a friendly creature {@condition unconscious} you gain one {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, yet you may only gain one count per creature per combat.
During your turn you may spend {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} as a Free Action you may take once per turn for the following:

items: {@b Reload, Then Fire.} By spending one {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} you may perform an additional attack as part of your Attack action during your next turn. This extra attack does not stack. Additionally, any ranged weapons you are wielding are instantly reloaded at the start of your next turn provided you have enough ammunition on your person.

{@b Designated Target Fire.} By spending at least three {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count you may spend your Action to perform a special attack, coating an 15-ft. radius within your weapon's range in a red haze that reeks of lingering sweat and charred hair. All creatures of your choice within that radius must pass a Dexterity saving throw or suffer an amount of d10 piercing damage and a sum of 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the amount of {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} spent. Creatures who succeed take half that damage and count instead. Afterward you gain one {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count for each creature damaged through this, with an additional 8 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count if you have killed your {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} creature through this attack. These 8 count do not count toward your turn limit. You cannot gain an amount of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} in a single turn greater than double your proficiency bonus through this way.

entries: You gain an additional {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and deal an additional {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count from ranged weapon attacks after reaching 8th level in Ranger, and then an additional of each count upon reaching 14th level.

Whenever asked for a saving throw by a subclass feature, you use your Ranger Spell Save DC. Additionally, any attacks or effects that consume {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count as magical attacks for the purposes of bypassing Resistances.

subclassFeature.name: Target Watch
entries: {@i "Thus, you sink into a bottomless slumber."}

In any field of battle there is a certain distance you must have in consideration to better deal with trampling down a target with your weapon, but you have learnt how to incarnate a devil from wherever you stand. You may spend your Bonus Action during your turn to shift your stance, changing into one of the following Targetting Settings until the end of your next turn:

items: {@b Close-Quarters.} You shift back your weapon and prepare to take only pot-shots or use its body to bash at your foes, suffering no Disadvantage on ranged weapon attacks while within 5-ft. of your target. Additionally, you may perform melee weapon attacks using ranged weapons, still counting as a ranged weapon attack and dealing the ranged weapon's original damage die in bludgeoning damage. Your ranged weapons long and short Ranges are halved. (Any distance ending in 5-ft. is rounded down.) Your Sweet-Spot is 10-ft. While on Close-Quarters you gain advantage on {@skill Perception} checks that are within your short range.

{@b Medium-Range.} Your stance becomes firm and flexible, ready to change at any moment. Your ranged weapon's short range value is decreased by 10-ft., and your long range increases by 10-ft. While on Medium-Range you gain an {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to {@skill Perception} checks.

{@b Far-Watch.} Your stance becomes more reserved and rooted, halving your movement speed. Attempting to target a creature within short range applies Disadvantage on your attack roll, but targets within your long range do not. Your long range increases by 20-ft. Your Sweet-Spot is any range greater than your short range plus 15-ft. While on Far-Watch you gain advantage on {@skill Perception} checks that are outside your short range.

entries: Each of these Targetting Settings has a Sweet Spot. When you attempt to hit a target within your current Sweet Spot, you gain a +1 to hit against that target and deal an additional damage die matching your wielded weapon's on a hit. Upon targetting a Huge or greater creature, only the spaces in the middle intersections of where they occupy count as a Sweet Spot.

If you kill your {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} creature while it is within your current Targeting Setting you gain an additional 8 {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count.

subclassFeature.name: Volatilized Rush
entries: {@i "Thus, you sink into a bottomless slumber."}

There is smoke in your lungs. You don't know when it got there, or when you failed to exhale it, but that haze has become a part of you. Whenever you would lose {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count from triggering a Posture Critical, only halve your current amount instead. Furthermore, whenever you trigger one while having a {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count of 10 or greater, you may choose to change the attack's damage type to force damage.

Additionally, you gain a new way to march on through your {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Torn Memories}. You may spend one count when you perform a ranged weapon attack during your turn. When you do so, you can see a series of blazing-red reticules in the air that guide your shot toward the targets heart, considering their AC to be lowered by your proficiency bonus for this attack. On a hit you always trigger a Posture Critical hit and this attack bypasses damage Resistances and considers Immunity to your dealt damage type as only Resistance instead.

subclassFeature.name: Memoir of a War-torn Veteran
entries: {@i "Until echoes of gunshots and plumes of smoke bury all that I've ever remembered...!"}

Are you in pursuit of a memory of the past or have you become nothing but a blurred memory yourself? Maybe it is your party that grounds you in reality for the brief moments where you remain wholly yourself, or maybe its just the pursuit of the next target that keeps you going. Nevertheless, you have become a veteran in the war that is your life, wringing out every trick you have needed.

items: While you have at least one {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} Memory summoned, you may spend your Reaction whenever you take damage to only take half that damage and have all {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} Memories within 120-ft. reach of you suffer the other half. If a {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} Memory is killed in this way, you do not receive its benefits.
Upon rolling Initiative you gain 4 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and one {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count.
You inflict an additional 3 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count against creatures within your Sweet Spot.

Whenever you Critically Hit a creature, you may choose to spend one {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} to deal an additional {@damage 2d8} piercing damage and also double any Conditions you would inflict.

For each {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count you have you gain a +2 on {@skill Deception} checks to conceal your identity, as wreathes of red flame gradually consume your face like a mask that actively muddies the perception and memories of those that try to recall you, remaining to them as only a weaponized fire in their minds eye.

subclassFeature.name: Gap Attack
entries: {@i "Stay sharp and focus on the fight if you don't want to snuff it."}

Opening a gap for you and your fellows to strike through is a tough opportunity to pass by, so you create it yourself when no one else will. When you deal damage through your Sneak Attack, you may choose to engage in a swift withdrawal of your blade to have the target suffer a count of {@condition Open Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} and an amount of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your proficiency bonus.
Whenever you perform a Sneak Attack you may choose to inflict {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} after the Sneak Attack.

Additionally, keeping your step clean and your options open cash in your shot is tantamount to you, granting you half your proficiency bonus' worth of {@condition Haste|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count on a successful Sneak Attack.

subclassFeature.name: Wall Stitcher
entries: {@i "We'd better hurry up, or surviving this long will have been for nothing."}

You aren't the top dog and you know that, you don't have the greatest tools nor the greatest skills yet, so you've grown to rely on what you can get everywhere - making the most of what people would just let pass by without another glance. You gain proficiency in your choice of the {@skill Acrobatics} or {@skill Athletics} skill, or Expertise if you were already proficient in the chosen skill.

Additionally you may cling surfaces to aid in staying still if something would move you, being able to spend your Bonus Action to wedge yourself as long as you are wielding a weapon that deals piercing damage. While wedged on walls and ceilings you do not fall at the end of your turn and once per turn you may spend a free action to attempt jumping 10-ft. upward or downward before wedging yourself in another surface within reach or jump down to the ground. You have Advantage on saving throws against effects that would cause you to be moved or knocked {@condition Prone}, such as being Shoved or the {@spell thunderwave} spell. You may unlatch as a free action.

While out of combat you gain a base climbing speed equal to half your walking speed as long as you are wielding a weapon that deals piercing damage, as you can take your time to manoeuvre yourself. This increases by 5-ft. if you are wielding another piercing weapon in your other hand.

subclassFeature.name: Chink in One's Armor
entries: {@i "You're full of openings."}

Your ability to exploit weaknesses has grown in precision, being able to drive your blade right through even the scales of a dragon to ensure that you'll carve your way out of any bad situation. When your attack roll would trigger a Sneak Attack against a creature that is benefitting from armor or natural armor you may focus to pierce straight through the smallest openings available, considering the target's AC is against this attack to be only 10 + their Dexterity Modifier. On a hit using this ability you also inflict an additional 3 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.
You may use this feature an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus, restoring spent uses on a long rest.
Additionally while your {@condition Haste|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count is 2 or greater creatures have Disadvantage on Opportunity Attacks against you.

subclassFeature.name: Seize Ya Chance
entries: {@i "Is this your weak spot?"}

You are a masterful being in the art of quickly finishing the broken and the battered with extreme mercy. Whenever you trigger a Sneak Attack against a creature suffering from {@condition Deep Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, you may choose to plunge your blade deeper for a vicious maiming of that poor soul. They suffer a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and a {@condition Fatal Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} instead. You may use this feature twice per long rest, and an additional third time upon reaching 20th level.

Additionally, if two other friendly creatures within 15-ft. of you have failed a saving throw or ability check that you passed you may offer them a stop of help through a hasty tip or a quick shove, granting them a bonus modifier to their roll equal to your proficiency bonus, potentially turning a failure into a success. You may do so once per short or long rest. Increases to two times upon reaching 18th level.

subclassFeature.name: A Tool That Punctures a Hole in the Heart
entries: {@i "Survival matters the most... I'll do anything for it."}

The rough path that your lifestyle brought you has shaped you into someone who can make the most of themselves and keep living another night no matter which horde comes knocking down your door, no matter the reason why. You gain the following:

items: When you inflict {@condition Open Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} for the first time, inflict an additional count.
Whenever you deal piercing damage, deal an additional {@damage 2d6} piercing damage.
While below half your maximum hit points you gain an additional 10-ft. of movement speed and add half your proficiency bonus as a bonus modifier to Dexterity and Wisdom saving throws.
While below half your maximum hit points you cannot be targeted by Opportunity Attacks.
You inflict double the {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count you would when you trigger a Critical Hit.

subclassFeature.name: Path of the Hammer of Faith
entries: {@i "Everything—I'll burn it all... and my whole disgusting life, too."}

Those who thread this Primal Path, the ones who take up the Hammer of Faith and embody it are rare prodigies who wield their irate belief like a weapon of mass distruction on those infidel to their preachings. There is no qualm taken in avoiding violence when needed, nor a sacrifice too great for the good of all.

These Barbarians are known for their intense fanaticism toward their belief and legends spread about the few who exist, as they often take to battlefields and single handedly decimate hordes upon their single-minded purge toward a pure world, not to mention the sheer brutality that they wield to carry out their wills.

In worlds such as the Forgotten Realms... No, there is no god of such a world that would be capable of enticing such faith. It is in the creeping shadows of Ravenloft that the names of forgotten gods are both whispered and screeched openly, a faith born from nothing and elevated into itself. In others, such as the futuristic world of Keybreak, these are the ones who neglect the integration of flesh and machinery, tearing it apart with gusto so that every corrupted being will have their rotten soul expunged before they can trace fingers upon the sheep who remain pure yet.

entries.subclassFeature: Disgust of the Faithful|Barbarian|PHB|Hammer of Faith|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|3
Scripture of Truth Within|Barbarian|PHB|Hammer of Faith|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|3

subclassFeature.name: Fell Memoir Ranger Archetype
entries: {@i "It promised to give me a gun that can blow up anything, but the catch was that its last shell would land on the head of my beloved."}

Times of war have long since painted history in their glory and gore, tinting red the lives of various people. Yet there are those who are overtaken by a smoke-like feeling that clings to their skin like a plume of flame just near going off. Those are Fell Memoir Rangers.

Usually characterized by a worn-out exterior and carrying an equally well-used gun, they roam the lands in search of more and more targets to blow up, living for the perpetual feeling of being in a conflict - of reliving their own memories and destroying that of others they find in their wake. Now, rarely they may be still clinging to some sort of feeling, an unresolved lack in their own recollection that pushes them onward, yet in most cases they are a blaze waiting to grow large enough to overtake everything one may think of.

entries.subclassFeature: Memoir of a Fallen Stigma|Ranger|PHB|Fell Memoir|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|3

subclassFeature.name: Night Awl Roguish Archetype
entries: {@i "Be quick in your step, thread the night carefully and get the hell out of dodge before you get snuffed out."}
That is the thing that most Rogues who fit in the Archetype of the Night Awl might find themselves hearing from a captain of their gang or even tell themselves.

They are usually people who bear through the brunt of a hard life, away from the flashiness of grandiose magic cast by archmages or the jewel-embezzling tales of bards, instead relying only on themselves and maybe a greater criminal organization where they can punch out a place in, carrying with them only a dirk in hand and a clear goal to be reached with finesse and clarity.

In the Forgotten Realms the Night Awls are a subsidiary of the Zentharim that have earnt themselves some renown, yet through no fault, of their own they are facing adverse times because of poor management. In other worlds such as Keybreak they are small-time info brokers running through the underground webs that connect city to city.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of the Obsidian Stormrider
entries: {@i "His Majesty's Hongyuan converges with your vision for Hongyuan at its culmination, young Miss."}

Loyal as can be, the druids who form the Circle of the Obsidian Stormrider are hardly connected amongst themselves, instead claiming to hold the force of a hundred men on their own - Often choosing to leash their life to a master to whom they serve diligently.

At their best, they are houndlike in their loyalty and steadfast in assuring the growth and protection of those who surround them - However, this is two-fold, with some being easily perceived as sticklers for the rules or extremely demanding of their master for their own sake.

In certain worlds such as in the Forgotten Realms, these can be found as servants of the myriad rich families that litter the lands, often acting as their wardens and caretakers. In others such as Thespis they are roving travellers in search of true guidance toward their future glory, living only to become something grander than they could by their lone selves.
Homebrew Written by Bishop.
Document Design by Bishop.
And as always, many thanks to our enterprising Patrons!

subclassFeature.name: Expanded Spells List
entries: {@i "Thus I felled the rogue rebel as His Majesty has commanded—then, Hongyuan, march on… without fear."}

Your mutations and application of theory into practice grants you access to certain spells. At 2nd level, you learn the {@spell blade ward} cantrip. At 3rd, 5th, 7th, and 9th level you gain access to the spells listed for that level in the Circle of the Stormrider Spells table.

Once you gain access to one of these spells, you always have it prepared, and it doesn't count against the number of spells you can prepare each day. If you gain access to a spell that doesn't appear on the druid spell list, the spell is nonetheless a druid spell for you.

entries.caption: Circle of the Stormrider Spells
rows: 3rd
{@spell compelled duel}, {@spell expeditious retreat}
5th
{@spell pass without trace}, {@spell warding bond}
7th
{@spell crusader's mantle}, {@spell protection from energy}
9th
{@spell death ward}, {@spell stoneskin}

subclassFeature.name: Farrier of the Mind
entries: {@i "I ruminate and ruminate upon the fragments of the incident to learn of what I could have done that the young Miss might have lived."}

Like any other steed that has their heart set on accompanying a master, you have learned a trade or two in pursuance of both increasing your usefulness and to remain of sound mind, taking care of yourself even out of battle. You gain proficiency in one {@skill skill} and one {@item Artisan's Tools|PHB|Artisan's Kit} of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Obsidian Stormrider's Ascent
entries: {@i "Ride, beating of hooves. Rise, grains of sand. Ring, cries of war. Rest, for your flight shall meet a dead end."}

As a Bonus Action you may spend a use of your your Wildshape feature to enter a {@i Stormrider Form} having your body morph and change as a violent gale engulfs it. Your lower body becomes that of a trampling beast for the next minute, granting you the following features:

items: Your movement speed increases by 10-ft and your legs are changed or reinforced, allowing you to use your Kicks as a natural melee weapon you are Proficient with. These have the Finesse property and deal {@damage 1d8} bludgeoning damage on a hit.

You may choose to inflict a value of any combination of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your proficiency bonus on a melee weapon hit. Additionally, whenever you hit a creature for the first time during your turn they suffer one count of {@condition Concussion|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.
For the duration the weapon you wield counts as a Druidic Focus for you to be able to cast Druid spells through it even if you have no free hand to do so.

When you spend a use of your Wildshape to enter this form, you gain an amount of Temporary Hit Points equal to half your Maximum Hit Points. You may benefit form this a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per long rest.

entries: Additionally you may spend your Bonus Action to stamp your hooves in the ground and let a building storm gather around you as you kick up the dust in your path. Gaining a cumulative +1 bonus modifier to your Armor Class for each 10-ft. travelled until the end of your turn.

When you next perform a melee weapon attack you may choose to turn all this momentum into more force for your attack, consuming up to any amount of additional AC gained this way to fling the target toward anywhere within a radius equal to 5-ft. plus an additional 5-ft. per AC consumed this way.

If this creature falls on a wall or at least medium-sized object, it suffers an amount of d6 bludgeoning damage per 5-ft. travelled. If it falls on another creature, they suffer the same amount of damage and the creature being fallen upon must pass a Dexterity save against your Druid Spell Save DC or suffer the same damage. Creatures who suffer this damage become {@condition prone} afterward and you may choose to trigger {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} after dealing this damage.
All bonus Armor Class gained this way is reset to 0 at the start of your next turn and you can't use this ability again until the end of your turn.
Your {@i Stormrider Form} lasts for up to one minute or until you are knocked {@condition unconscious}. Upon leaving this form you lose any remaining Temporary Hit Points gained from it.

subclassFeature.name: Commanding Cry
entries: {@i "Leap upon the first. - And the second. - Break and surmount them."}

There is an order to things that you have long understood, and you have better found a way to convey that to others so that they may find their place in any setting that demands it. You may spend your Bonus Action to shout a Commanding Cry to a creature that can hear you within 60-ft. When you do so, choose one of the following type of order to bark out:

entries.name: Charge Forward! [冲锋!]
entries: The target creature gains an +1 bonus modifier to hit and deal double the damage they would to structures and unworn un-carried objects until the end of their next turn. This bonus is increased to a +2 upon you reaching 12th level.

entries.name: Hold the Line! [坚守阵地!]
entries: The target creature gains a +1 bonus modifier to their AC until the start of your next turn. This bonus is increased to a +2 upon you reaching 12th level.

entries.name: Center Yourself! [静心!]
entries: The target creature gains a {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to all rolls pertaining to one Skill of your choice for the next minute. This bonus is increased to a {@dice 1d6} upon you reaching 12th level.
You may use this feature an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Adept's Cloud-Spitting Ascent
entries: {@i "I have endured it all."}

You have become used to being in your {@i Stormrider Form}, allowing your stance to become perfected. You may perform an additional attack whenever you take the {@action Attack} Action within your {@i Stormrider Form} and your base movement speed is increased by 5-ft.
Additionally, upon reaching this level you may perform the following as an Action by spending a Druid spell slot:

entries.name: Obsidian Stormrider's Crescent Decapitator [黑風馬脚月斬]
entries: You swing your weapon wildly as you go on a thundering stampede that covers a 10-ft. wide line that has a length equal to 10-ft. per Spell slot level spent and that you may change the direction of at each 20-ft. travelled. All creatures within that area must pass a Dexterity saving throw against your Druid Spell Save DC or be trampled, suffering an amount of {@damage d10} bludgeoning damage equal to double the Spell slot level spent and being knocked {@condition prone}, then suffering an amount of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the Spell slot level spent.

subclassFeature.name: Seasoned Veteran's Stride
entries: {@i "Thus, the flame of war burns in Hongyuan.To let slip the lessons of the rotten and the festering, to forget the kindness of his ideality, is what has started the fire."}

The way you carry yourself has changed drastically form where you were once but a beast finding your footing, now boasting a confidence and importance with each step taken, be that transformed or not. You gain the following benefits while on your {@i Stormrider Form}:

items: Whenever you would trigger a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} against a creature, it suffers 2 {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Whenever you would trigger the effects of the latter Condition, you inflict 1 {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count afterward.
While you have Temporary Hit Points you gain a +2 bonus modifier to your AC. This is reduced to a +1 when none remain.

While you have no Temporary Hit Points you also gain an additional 5-ft. of movement and may spend your Bonus Action to perform an attack using your Kicks. You do not add your Ability Modifier to this attack's damage roll. When you do so, you may choose to force the target to pass a Strength saving throw against your Druid Spell Save DC or be flung 10-ft. backward in a line of your choice.

entries: Additionally, while out of combat you may grant yourself and your allies a moment of collective preparation toward whatever dangers you will face ahead by spending 10 minutes doing so. Upon the completion of these talks and small rituals all creatures involved may end one Condition or Curse to immediately end, or have the first time either would be applied in the next Combat be nullified if they were suffering from neither.
You may have this moment of preparation once per long rest. Only Curses that could be ended by the {@spell remove curse} spell are affected by this use.

subclassFeature.name: Fragrant Soul
entries: {@i "Keep the door ajar. The sunbeam... is warm for once."}

Those blessed by a Fragrant Soul are a rare sight to be seen, marking the world with their sorcerous powers like a painter would to a canvas and sowing seeds of growth for others whenever they come by.

They usually become well-trusted leaders of revolutionary movements or groups seeking some sort of improvement on the world, all driven by their desire to experience the small blossoms of ingenuity and beauty that may come along their lifetime, performed by themselves or others.

In worlds such as the Forgotten Realms, Fragrant Soul Sorcerers are found with ease to those seeking them, as they have left their trails through the jungles of Chult in a great cult to bring full unity to the unruly land. In realms such as Thespis, they are the rare spawn of the Nushae who are blessed with a connection to the forests of the Wyrd, brandishing their magic as great magicians of their tribes, usually being cherished and highly-expected by their fellows.

entries.name: Fragrant Soul Origins
entries: Sorcerers who exhibit a Fragrant Soul are obvious to the naked eye, with leaves and branches growing from their bodies like a natural expansion—not to mention the eponymous smell from their eternal partial bloom.
These sorcerers may come from various origins, with only a few presented below, but most of the times they have deep ties to the nature of the world itself or its evolution, man-made or otherwise.

rows: You were born under the solstice of Autumn, blessed by nature itself and your heart is an enchanted organ.
You always had latent power that never seemed to sprout until a certain event changed everything in your life.
The powers granted to you were implanted by a third party without your knowledge, either at birth or later in life. You would only learn of it when first noticing the fragrance others couldn't.
Despair has marked your heart to the point that it became a seed of magic, granting you a power to sweep through the world and raze it to the ground, allowing it all to grow anew,
An archdruid has given you their blessing and infused your soul with druidic magic.
You were raised in a flower-pot and are actually a magician's homunculus.

entries.subclassFeature: Beauty of the Little Things|Sorcerer|PHB|Fragrant Soul|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|1

subclassFeature.name: Fragrant Soul Spells
entries: You learn additional spells when you reach certain levels in this class, as shown on the Fragrant Soul Spells table. Each of these spells counts as a sorcerer spell for you, but it doesn't count against the number of sorcerer spells you know.
Whenever you gain a sorcerer level, you can replace one spell you gained from this feature with another spell of the same level. The new spell must be from the sorcerer or druid spell list.

entries.caption: Fragrant Soul Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell compelled duel}, {@spell entangle}
3rd
{@spell barkskin}, {@spell locate animals or plants}
5th
{@spell plant growth}, {@spell speak with plants}
7th
{@spell freedom of movement}, {@spell grasping vine}
9th
{@spell commune with nature}, {@spell wrath of nature|XGE}

subclassFeature.name: Moment's Floral Breeze
entries: {@i "Welcome. Now what does your heart say... about what you see of my heart?"}

There is life within your heart, one that sets its roots in, grows and flourishes beautifully. With every wave of the hand and every single spell cast, you project more of your nature into the world and help shape its path to blossoming.

Whenever you cast a spell, you gain Lingering Blossoms count equal to the Spell Slot Level spent. Whenever you hit a creature with spell attacks or saving throws, you may choose to spend a value of Lingering Blossoms to inflict equal {@condition Blooming|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} and double that value of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} counts.

You may also spend 2 Lingering Blossoms as a Bonus Action to condense it into a small orb of spice that you can toss to a willing creature within 30-ft. of you as part of the same Bonus Action. That creature gains an {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to one skill check, attack roll or saving throw of their choice for the next minute, consuming the orb as a Free Action.
You may have a maximum amount of Lingering Blossoms equal to double your proficiency bonus, and that value is halved on a short rest and reduced to zero during a long rest.

Whenever a creature becomes {@condition Blooming|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Fully Bloomed} within 60-ft. of you, you may spend your Reaction to reap the blooming flower you have created, liberating the creature from their suffering and potentially having them see the world with fresher eyes.

They must pass a Constitution saving throw against your Spell Save DC or suffer {@damage 2d6} piercing damage plus a number of d8 psychic damage for each 5 Sinking count they are suffering from, to a maximum of {@damage 8d8}, losing an equal count of the Condition afterward.

subclassFeature.name: Beauty of the Little Things
entries: {@i "...Does it sometimes occur to you when you see a remarkable thing that you want to share the wonderment with others?"}

Your soul is one that isn't concerned only with the ever-marching stride of progress, instead you have come to respect and grant love to the small moments of life. You learn the {@spell druidcraft} Cantrip and it counts as a Sorcerer spell for you, but doesn't count toward your total spells known.

Whenever you use this Cantrip you may choose to gain a count of Lingering Blossoms as well, for up to 2 count of the Effect gained this way. Additionally, you gain proficiency in the {@skill Nature} skill, or Expertise if you were already proficient.

subclassFeature.name: Efflorescing Magnificence
entries: {@i "The bud has risen. Effort has borne fruit."}
Your presence as a person is tantamount to magic, enchanting and bedazzling those in your surroundings in various ways. When you first reach 6th level in this Class, choose from one of the following:

items: {@b Flourishing.} Your fragrance is bountiful and invigorating, nourishing others to be at their best behaviour. At the start of your turns, you may spend a count of Lingering Blossoms to grant yourself and friendly creatures within 15-ft. of you {@dice 2d8} Temporary Hit Points. While these Temporary Hit Points remain, the affected creatures gain an {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to Strength, Dexterity and Constitution saving throws.

{@b Liberating.} Your fragrance is that of a free spirit, easing the notion of being unbound and free to go wherever. You and all friendly creatures who start their turn within 45-ft. of you gain an extra 5-ft. of movement speed. Additionally, whenever you use your Bonus Action to grant a creature a bonus modifier to roll as per your Beauty of the Little Things feature, your bonus is instead {@dice 1d6} and you may choose to give another creature within the aura the same bonus by spending an additional Lingering Blossoms.

{@b Withering.} Your fragrance is that of rot, an agent to make way for a fresher world. Creatures suffering from Sinking count suffer an amount of d6 necrotic damage at the end of their turns equal to half their Sinking count, for a maximum of {@damage 4d4}. Furthermore, they suffer the same negative modifier from the Condition to their Constitution and Strength modifiers.

entries: You may choose to change this feature upon great moments of character development as this should be determined by your current outlook on life and yourself, which directly correlates to how their presence and power manifests. You and your DM must agree with the choice.

subclassFeature.name: Culminating Fragrance
entries: {@i "It makes a pungent smell, does it not? It strikes your senses so intensely, you might almost fall to the ground... Such a deep and fragrant scent, it is."}

Whenever you cast a spell, it leaves behind a lingering cloud of spice that nourishes your fellows and harms your foes. This cloud expands from the point it has hit to cover a radius of 5-ft. times the Spell Slot Level used, to a minimum of 5-ft. In the case of spells with multiple targets, this creates multiple clouds whose area is divided by the number of creatures targeted, rounded down.
Friendly creatures gain while starting or ending their turns within the cloud:

items: Recover 2 Hit Points at the start of their turns inside the cloud, unless they are {@condition Unconscious}.
Gain a +1 to Wisdom and Dexterity saving throws, or a +2 when you reach 18th level.
Are considered Lightly Obscured by hostile creatures.

entries: And hostile creatures suffer the following at the start or end of their turns inside the cloud:

items: 2 {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.
A −1 to Constitution and Charisma saving throws, or a −2 when you reach 18th Level.

entries: When ending their turn inside the cloud they must pass a Constitution saving throw or be {@condition Blinded} until the start of their next turn. Any cloud created this way lasts for up to the start of your next turn if you haven't passed through it or ended your turn inside it. Furthermore, any magical gusts may cause the clouds to disperse and mundane ones only have it move 5-ft. in the wind's direction due to their high density.

subclassFeature.name: Bloodsteeped Scent of the World
entries: {@i "Now... Behold. These flowers are in full glory. Once all these flowers have been stained red... that shall be when 'I' bloom as well."}

Blood, sweat and tears stain the garden that is the world as fertilizer for its growth, and you have acted as its gardener and centrepiece for long, absorbing all you need to have your soul bloom like no other. Once per long rest you may spend 10 Lingering Blossoms as a Bonus Action to bloom yourself, and have the world around you follow suit.

When you do so, a 320-ft. radius around you visibly changes to be overgrown with vibrant plants that match your fragrance and view, with your essence being unmistakeable to those therein. When first creating this area, all creatures of your choice within reach instantly lose all their Sinking count and you gain the sum of all count lost this way.

The pains of others serve as no pain of your own, instead washing away all impurities and capturing in time all the chances they have had to bloom, taken or missed. While suffering from Sinking this way, its effects change as you do, causing that whenever you would suffer a negative modifier from the Condition, you gain a positive one instead.

Additionally, you inflict 4 Sinking count whenever you damage another creature and 6 when they fail a saving throw from your spells. Whenever you kill or first knock a creature {@condition Unconscious}, they lose all their Sinking count and you gain it instead. While within this area, you do not create clouds as per your Culminating Fragrance feature. Instead, the entire area is considered a Fragrant cloud.
Whenever you would lose Sinking count, you gain one Lingering Blossoms count for each 3 Sinking lost this way. This area of bloom decays and vanishes when you aren't suffering from Sinking anymore.

subclassFeature.name: Fatalism Domain
entries: Fatalism. "The belief that all events are predetermined and therefore inevitable." Those who follow its domain believe as if the concept itself was God, a force of nature with no parallel or counterweight - And one that if they go against, it'd be as going against their own heartbeat.

These have become empty husks that embraced a prescribed fate to their name, old or new, and molded themselves accordingly. They are often imitations of someone that once was, is or will be and pursue barely any personal goal past what was ascribed to them. Despite that, there are still those that try to look for cracks in "Fate's" mask, to have little actions and pursuits that might change things ever so slightly, all to satisfy imprinting their own will into the world, like a wave trying to form in the sea.

In worlds such as the Forgotten Realms those who follow the Fatalism Domain are the highest members of those under the Living Will, acting as their indirect proxies and undercover agents that are used to shape other settlements in certain ways to go according to plan. In others such as Thespis, there was but one true believer of the Fatalist Domain - Their name lost to time and story far, far ago, and their remains being distorted tales that many a new cleric tried to imitate and reach, attempting to forge their own unbreakable fatalism.
Homebrew Written by Bishop.
Document Design by Bishop.
And huge thanks to our dearest Patrons.

subclassFeature.name: Domain Extended Spells
entries: At each indicated cleric level, add the listed spells to your spells prepared. They do not count towards your limit.

entries.caption: Fatalism Domain Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell ceremony|XGE}, {@spell Heart-Breaking Smite|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}
3rd
{@spell alter self}, {@spell magic mouth}
5th
{@spell Leomund's tiny hut}, {@spell sending}
7th
{@spell compulsion}, {@spell divination}
9th
{@spell dispel evil and good}, {@spell enervation|XGE}

entries: Note¹ - Spell from the Oath of Procuration subclass document.

subclassFeature.name: Multitudes in a Crashing Wave
entries: {@i "Be cheerful in your final moments. For you have been chosen."}

To become a true follower of the Will you have come to understand that you are into the wielder of a weapon as as an extension of yourself, no. You are no more than a weapon that extends from the whims made manifest.

You gain a Wilful Device, a small golden box which displays your Prescripts and contains a black ferrofluid substance that mimics and adapts as much like your soul. If lost or removed from your person, you may recall it to your hand as a Free Action. It is indestructible and may be wielded as a weapon with the Finesse property. At the start of your turns in combat, roll two d8 to determine the shape it takes as per the following table, disregarding the second roll unless both are the same number.

rows: Hatchet
1d6 slashing
Light
Stiletto
1d4 piercing
Light
Bastard Sword
1d8 slashing
Versatile (1d10)
Rapier
1d6 piercing
Hammer
1d6 bludgeoning
Great Sword
2d6 slashing
Heavy, Two-Handed
Lance
1d12 piercing
Reach
Whip
1d4 slashing
Reach of 15-ft.
Any double except 1-1
Scythe
2d6 slashing
Heavy, Versatile (2d8)
Double 1-1
Spork
1 piercing
Whenever you deal damage with this weapon, also inflict {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} equal to your proficiency bonus.

entries: At the beginning of your turns, if there is no creature suffering the Effect, one random hostile creature within 120-ft. of you becomes {@condition Target of the Prescript|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Marked by the Prescript}. You inflict {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your proficiency bonus when attacking a {@condition Target of the Prescript|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Marked by the Prescript} creature.

Whenever you or a friendly creature within 15-ft. of you knocks a {@condition Target of the Prescript|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Marked by the Prescript} creature {@condition Unconscious} for the first time in combat or kills them, you gain {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your proficiency bonus.

Upon reaching 4th Level in Cleric, you gain a +1 to hit and to damage rolls while using your Wilful Device to attack. This increases to a +2 at 10th Level and a +3 at 16th Level. It also counts as a Holy Symbol for you.

entries.name: Designer's Note.¹
entries: This subclass is not meant to be taken as a multi-class with other Dexterity-based classes, since it may provide too-strong a weapon with the Finesse property, which was chosen to be given to all weapons for the sake of greater freedom when designing your player character. We recommend removing the Finesse property and only adding it to Hatchet, Stiletto, Rapier, Lance, Whip and Scythe if multi-classing into a Dexterity-based class to avoid abuse of this feature.

entries.name: Designer's Note².
entries: To define a "random hostile creature" we recommend using the Random Targeting Rule within the Optional Rules & Prescripts section of this document.

subclassFeature.name: To Become a Canvas, Slowly Painted
entries: {@i "Hah... the waves are rolling in."}

The future is pre-ordained, and you are but a gear in a greater plan, slowly letting it shape you and in turn you shape the world around you. At the beginning of every long rest you draw a Prescript from the Crawling Prescripts Table at the end of this document. When you do so, you have up to a week or until you your next long rest to finish its objective, as per described in the Prescript itself.

Upon completing this Prescript, you gain a single count of {@condition Procuration [Hermes]|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. You may have a maximum of this effect equal to half your Proficiency Bonus at any given time, rounded down, and a minimum of -2.
You gain the following effects while you have negative or positive counts of this effect:

items: {@b Lesser than zero.} Your heart is beating at an unsteady rhythm, much like the crumbling road you feel like you walk upon. You cannot spend Hit Die to recover Hit Points during a short rest and only recover half your Maximum Hit Points on a long rest. You suffer a negative modifier to Strength, Dexterity and Constitution saving throws equal to the negative count of {@condition Procuration [Hermes]|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. You suffer Disadvantage on Death saving throws.

{@b Zero count.} You constantly feel uneasy, as if something bad will happen at any given time that you are not working towards your goal. You suffer a −1 negative modifier on Wisdom saving throws and gain a +1 bonus modifier on {@skill Perception} and {@skill Investigation} checks.

{@b Greater than one.} You can feel that all is going according to plan, and this confidence in the greater drives you on with a practiced ease. You gain a bonus modifier to your Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma saving throws equal to your current {@condition Procuration [Hermes]|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count. You deal additional damage equal to that value whenever you deal damage using your Cleric spells and your Spell Save DC increases by the same value.

entries: Additionally, whenever you fail a Prescript drawn from this feature, you suffer 3 {@condition Karmic Consequences|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. Whenever you complete one, you instead gain 2 {@condition Grace of the Prescript|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, except you lose one at the end of your combats. You may only have up to 6 {@condition Grace of the Prescript|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} this way.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: To Paint the Rough Waves
entries: {@i "I shall replicate a passionate heart."}

Starting at 2nd level, you may use your Channel Divinity to unleash a wave of powerful attacks using your Beeper, changing it's fluid shape after every attack and drawing out every ounce of pain so that your goal may be reached. As an action you dash toward up to your movement speed toward a target within reach and perform an amount of weapon attacks using your Wilful Beeper equal to half your proficiency bonus, changing its form as per the Multitudes in a Crashing Wave before each attack.

On a hit, you inflict 2 {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on the target and deal additional psychic damage equal to half their {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, rounded down. Upon killing a creature this way, you may instantly move up to another creature within a reach equal to your movement speed and perform the same number of attacks with the same effects, repeating this process until you fail to kill a creature.

If a creature killed this way was {@condition Target of the Prescript|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Marked by the Prescript}, your next target becomes {@condition Target of the Prescript|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Marked by the Prescript} instead and you gain 4 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. If you fail to kill your target, you perform an final additional attack using the Scythe form of your Wilful Beeper at Advantage. This attack is a Critical Hit on a dice roll of 17–20.

After using this Channel Divinity, its use is not restored after finishing a short or long rest, instead requiring that you consume one count of {@condition Procuration [Hermes]|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} to use it again.

subclassFeature.name: Brandishes to Quell the Innermost Self
entries: {@i "By day as by night, this City... shows itself only as a pale blur, as though the rain has washed its silhouette white"}

To become a better tool yourself, you have mastered many a weapon for its best use, being able to bring out their full potential while they're in your hands. Once every other turn you may replace one of your attacks as part of the Attack Action with a Weapon Brandish according to your current Wilful beeper form, as presented below:

entries.name: Hatchet Brandish: Filo del Ragno
entries: You extend your Hatchet's liquid hilt toward any target creature within 30-ft. of you, performing an weapon attack roll against them. On a hit, you may instantly rush toward them, moving to be within 5-ft. of the target. They have Disadvantage on attacks against you until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Stiletto Brandish: Guida Falsa
entries: You maintain dominance through any battlefield. Perform an amount of melee weapon attacks against a target within reach equal to half your proficiency bonus ( rounded down ), on a hit the target is moved back 5-ft. each time you hit it until the end of your turn.

entries.name: Bastard Brandish: Vuoto Ardente
entries: Though bland, one with a practiced Bastard Sword can put fear into their enemies' core. You perform a weapon attack roll against a target within reach. On a hit, the target must pass a Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition Frightened} of you. While {@condition Frightened}, the target cannot willingly move away from you, as they are paralyzed by your presence. Whenever you finish your turn within 5-ft. of the {@condition Frightened} creature, you gain 2 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries.name: Rapier Brandish: Intecciare
entries: Fencing is all about positioning, and you know how to make your opponent's the worse possible. You instantly gain 3 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and may instantly move to any empty space within 5-ft. of your target to Flank with another friendly creature, if able, then perform a weapon attack roll against them. On a hit target must spend their Action and Bonus Action if they attempt to Disengage from you until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Hammer Brandish: Scindermentes
entries: You bring down your Hammer in a potentially horrid blow to the cranium. Perform a melee weapon attack against a creature within reach, on a hit they must pass a Constitution saving throw or receive a negative modifier to their Intelligence, Wisdom and Constitution saving throws equal to half your proficiency bonus until the end of their next turn, rounded down.

entries.name: Great Brandish: Mannaia Distrettuale
entries: You may swing the Great Sword to paint broad strokes, perform a melee attack roll against a target within reach. The result also counts as if it were targeting any other creatures 5-ft. beside the original target, when you roll damage you do so once for all targets hit, with an additional d6 slashing damage for each hit target.

entries.name: Lance Brandish: Linea di Macellazione
entries: You brace for a reckless dash forward using your lance to raze all in your path. Choose a point within 20-ft. of you to move to. All creatures in a line between you and your end goal must pass a Dexterity saving throw against your Cleric Spell Save DC or be impaled, taking 1d12 + half your proficiency bonus' worth of d12 piercing damage ( rounded down ) and both being knocked {@condition Prone} and forcibly moved to 5-ft. in front of you or the closest available space on a failure.

entries.name: Whip Brandish: .Spezzaarmatura
entries: You may use the Whip's everchanging point to hook and tear away your opponents weapon with ease. Perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach, on a hit they must pass a Dexterity saving throw or have one weapon of your choice that they are holding be flung toward any space within 35-ft. of them.

entries.name: Spork Brandish: Coraggio a Metà
entries: You have to make the best out of the worst with this weapon. Perform a weapon attack roll with this weapon, on a hit you inflict double the {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count you normally would.

entries.name: Scythe Brandish: Riverbero Splendente
entries: Pursuit is the only way to make a weapon sing, and you will pursue until your Scythe runs hoarse. You perform three weapon attacks against a target within reach. If the first two attacks hit, your third attack is considered a Critical Hit if it hits as well.
Furthermore, at the start of your turns you roll a d4, with the following effects occurring:

rows: You deal an additional die of bludgeoning damage whenever you deal bludgeoning damage. You ignore Resistance to bludgeoning damage and treat Immunities as if they were Resistance instead.
You deal an additional die of slashing damage whenever you deal slashing damage. You ignore Resistance to slashing damage and treat Immunities as if they were Resistance instead.
You deal an additional die of piercing damage whenever you deal piercing damage. You ignore Resistance to piercing damage and treat Immunities as if they were Resistance instead.

You deal an additional die of matching damage type whenever you deal bludgeoning, slashing or piercing damage. You ignore Resistance to these damage types and treat Immunities as if they were Resistance instead.

entries: Additionally, once per long rest you may consume one count of {@condition Procuration [Hermes]|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} to always choose your Wilful Beeper's form at the start of your turns. You cannot choose the same form twice in a row this way.

subclassFeature.name: Pre-Ordained Strikes
entries: {@i "...Yet my visage, seared and scorched, permits me not a day of reprieve from pain—oh, how it aches even under the gentlest sun."}

You gain the ability to channel the Will through your fingertips so your swings may always find their mark, even if that puts you in harm's way. When you miss an attack roll, you may choose to still roll damage and deal half the result still, but suffer the same damage dealt. This does not count as a hit for other effects purposes and inflicts only half any Condition/Effect count that would be inflicted.

You may do this an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus per short or long rest. Additionally, once per long rest you may consume one count of {@condition Procuration [Hermes]|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} to always deal full damage on a missed attack, but you still suffer half of that damage.

subclassFeature.name: Feign Folly, Face All, Reign Tall
entries: {@i "here come moments wherein I find myself longing to be tagged unfrozen; alas, my darling daughter appears to have mislaid the memory to do so. Hah... how draining this is."}

A husk is all that remains of you when it comes to obeying the Will, to resonate with it so profoundly that your entire being is made by it. That devotion, however, has not gone unheard, allowing you some reprieve at the hardest of times just to reach your ultimate goal.
You gain the following effects:

items: You have learnt how to fill the empty husk that you are with anything demanded by the greater Will, granting you the ability to use your Wisdom modifier instead of Charisma on any Skill Checks that would use the Attribute.

Every time you would be afflicted with a negative Condition or Effect such as the {@condition Frightened} Condition, roll a d100. On a roll of 75 or greater, you instead suffer nothing as fate seems to miraculously intervene.
Whenever a creature would damage you with a Critical Hit, they must confirm it by rolling a d20, with any result below 15 having the hit instead be a regular attack only.

You may guide others toward the Will's bidding with expertise, become Immune to being {@condition Frightened} and {@condition Charmed}. Additionally whenever you Charm a creature, they benefit from your current {@condition Procuration [Hermes]|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count as a bonus modifier to their attack and damage rolls while friendly to you.

The grace of your God reaches even those who indirectly contribute to it's whims, granting you a 15-ft. aura of where any friendly creature within reach benefits from the d4 effects of your Brandishes to Quell the Innermost Self feature.

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Vast Garden
entries: {@i "Hm. Good eye. I'm a rare talent around here, you know?"}

Study. Discipline. Evolution. The vast garden is a giant monastery that births new talents and prodigies every year. They fight amongst each other to decide who will stand at the top of the garden. You're one of those studious Monks trying to make a name for yourself, learn the deep teachings of the Vast Garden Monastery and either continue to embody them or change them for future generations.

In the Forgotten Realms, this monastery might focus on creating leaders for nations and estates, pitting them against each other so only the strongest survive. In Eberron, they study so that they can strengthen their psionic capabilities and earn control of cities as powerful and wise mayors. In the dark fantasy world of Alacritas, many monasteries train their students to overcome their masters with a lethal blow. Drenched in the blood of an unforgivable sin, they carry the souls of the departed with them on a wrathful journey of conquest, endlessly perfecting their style before starting the cycle anew.

If you want to play as a Monk of the Vast Garden, remember that you are a studious individual trying to become the best of your monastery. Vast Garden monks are usually diligent, listen to their superiors and are constantly trying to train and challenge themselves.

If you're using one as an NPC, they could be guiding the party through a city they have never visited before, or help them learn skills they have been wanting to study. If you want one as a BBEG, they could feel threatened by one of the party members and try to prove themselves by defeating them, or they might be trying to conquer a city or village that the players hold dear.

subclassFeature.name: Launching Maneuver [始動]
entries: {@i "No flower ever endures the fall... or so they say."}

You can use a bonus action to leap up to a distance equal to your remaining movement speed. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks. After you use this bonus action, your speed is reduced by the distance you travelled until the end of the turn.

If you land within 5 feet of a creature, or pass within 5 feet of a creature during this leap, you can make one unarmed strike against that creature as part of the same bonus action. On a hit, the attack deals extra damage equal to one additional roll of your Martial Arts die.

You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses on a Long Rest. Additionally, vou you always try to separate some time for your studies. Once per Long Rest, you can choose a Language, a Tool or a Skill to become proficient with until your next Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Crimson Strike
entries: {@i "Hongyuan's certainly not changed one bit. Except for its roads, I suppose."}
