Whenever you hit a creature, the attack deals extra damage equal to one additional role of your Martial Arts die as long as it has 3 or more Conditions affecting it. Additionally, you have studied many Forms to improve your attacks.

If any Form requires you to roll a Saving Throw, your Form Save DC is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Wisdom modifier. You cannot activate the same Form more than once if it hasn't yet ended. You gain access to the following abilities once per turn:

items: {@b Second Form - Rupture (破).} By spending 1 Ki point, until the end of your turn, you inflict 2 counts of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} whenever you hit a creature.

{@b Third Form - Might (强).} By spending 2 Ki points, until the end of your next turn, whenever you make an attack roll or spend points of Ki you gain 1 count of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, to a maximum of 4.

{@b Fourth Form - Binding (束).} By spending 2 Ki points, until the end of your turn, whenever you hit a creature with an attack roll, they lose 5 feet of movement. If you hit the same creature more than two times, they lose 10 feet instead.

{@b Fifth Form - March (進).} By spending 3 Ki points, whenever you roll your Martial Arts die for damage, you may choose to roll double that amount of Martial Arts die instead, immediately ending this Form afterwards.

{@b Crimson Cleave.} After you have used all of your Crimson Strike Forms at least once, you gain access to this ability. Once you use it, you must activate all of your Crimson Strike Forms at least once to use it again. After you hit a creature, you may choose to transform one of each of their Conditions into counts of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries: They gain 1 count of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for each Condition that they are currently suffering and 2 counts of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for each non-stackable Conditions (such as {@condition Frightened} or {@condition Stunned}). For this attack, they will take additional damage equal to all of their counts of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} instead of half of them.

subclassFeature.name: Rupture-breathing Resolve [破吸自桓]
entries: {@i "Let's take them all out. No need to waste our time here."}

You have been studying the art of proper breathing to unleash powerful techniques. Whenever you or an ally within 5 feet of you kills a creature that had counts of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, you immediately transform all of those into counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for you.

Additionally, once per Long Rest, you may spend up to your proficiency bonus in counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} after an attack to regain 1 Ki point for each 2 counts spent this way.
Furthermore, your studies continue to bear fruit. Once per Long Rest, you can choose a Skill to gain Expertise with until the next Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Crimson Phoenix
entries: {@i "What a... short-lived spring this is..."}

Further mysteries of martial arts have been imparted onto you by your master. If the target has 3 or more Conditions affecting it, you score a Critical Hit on rolls of 19 or 20. Additionally, you have studied more Forms to improve your attacks. You gain access to the following abilities once per turn:

items: {@b Second Form - Destruction (壊).} By spending 2 Ki points, you score a Critical Hit whenever you hit an object or a structure until the end of your turn.

{@b Third Form - Blaze (炎).} By spending 5 Ki points, your next attack that hits does not remove any counts of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} after triggering them, and applies half that amount of counts on the creature.

{@b Fourth Form - Qi (氣).} By spending 3 Ki points, if you would trigger a Posture Critical Hit this turn, you deal an additional d6 of damage and do not lose counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
{@b Fifth Form - Wings (翼).} By spending 4 Ki points, you gain a Flying speed equal to your movement speed for 1 minute.

subclassFeature.name: Crimson Spring
entries: {@i "Hey, this is what money's for. To celebrate good tidings."}

You have reached a point where your moves inspire both awe and fear into your enemies. If the target has 3 or more Conditions affecting it, you gain advantage on all Saving throws related to it and gain advantage on your first attack against them every turn. Additionally, you have studied the final Forms to turn your attacks into decisive blows. You gain access to the following abilities once per turn:

items: {@b Second Form - Passion (熱).} By spending 5 Ki points, whenever you hit a creature with an attack this turn, they must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Form Save DC or become {@condition Charmed} by you for 1 minute. A creature {@condition Charmed} this way continues {@condition Charmed} even if they are hit by an attack, and may reroll the saving throw at the end of their turn, ending the effect on a success.

{@b Third Form - Decapitation (斬).} By spending 5 Ki points, the next time you score a Critical Hit until the end of your turn, you decapitate the attacker, and it dies if it can't survive without its head. If it would not die without a head, deal {@damage 6d8} bludgeoning damage instead. If you do not score a Critical Hit, you also deal an additional {@damage 6d8} Bludgeoning damage on your last attack that hit this turn.

{@b Fourth Form - Flow (巡).} By spending 5 Ki points, you can move this turn without provoking opportunity attacks. If you manage to hit the same creature at least 3 times from different positions, it must make a Constitution saving throw against your Form Save DC. On a failed save, they become {@condition Paralyzed}. On a failed save, they take {@damage 2d8} Bludgeoning damage. Additionally, until the end of your turn, you get to perform a melee opportunity attack when entering the reach of a creature.

{@b Fifth Form - Blossom (花).} By spending 5 Ki points, you immediately gain 5 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. During this turn, if you score a Posture Critical hit, the creature suffers 4 counts of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and you do not lose your counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. At the end of your turn, if you didn't score a Posture Critical hit, the last creature you attacked suffers 2 counts of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

{@b Plastered Sleep, Unrestrained Ripples [酔睡浪浪].} After you have used all of your Crimson Spring Forms at least once, you gain access to this ability. Once you use it, you must activate all of your Crimson Spring Forms at least once to use it again. the next time you hit a creature with an attack, they take a number of d12 Bludgeoning damage equal to the number of Conditions affecting them + 2 rolls of your Martial Arts die in damage (minimum of 1d12 + 2 Martial Arts dice). If that kills them, you can move up to your movement speed and roll a melee attack against a creature within reach, producing the same effect and increasing the number of the martial arts die by one. If the first creature you hit isn't killed, you instead gain resistance to all damage types until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Haunted Toymaker
entries: A Haunted Toymaker does not simply make playthings for children and adults alike, but tense and dangerous objects that could prove lethal to any inexperienced handler. They implement a mixture of sharpness and dark magic in their inventions for a myriad of reasons, such as revenge, a twisted sense of pride or personal entertainment.

If you're going to play as a Haunted Toymaker, be sure to let your party know. You will likely follow the trope of a mad scientist or someone equally unhinged, and not all groups mesh well with a strong personality like that. Haunted Toymakers are always looking for new cursed items to turn into child's play and victims to be the target of their inventions. You will want to create things normal people would naturally shun and you want to not only give them the chance to shine but to take revenge on those that would leak down on their nature.

In the Forgotten Realms, every toy store has at least one of these—no Artificer is completely rid of sparks of madness; Haunted Toymakers simply own it. In Ravenloft, these specialists take a more sinister turn, usually leaving their constructs in unassuming houses to terrorize their inhabitants. In the high fantasy world of Aster, those haunted by the corrupting influence of Salem, The Great Witch, might dedicate themselves to the craft of the abominable.

subclassFeature.name: Tool Proficiency
entries: When you adopt this specialization at 3rd level, you gain proficiency with {@item tinker's tools|PHB}. If you already have this proficiency, you gain proficiency with one other type of {@item artisan's tools|PHB} of your choice.

subclassFeature.name: Haunted Toymaker Spells
entries: Starting at 3rd-level, you always have certain spells prepared after you reach particular levels in this class, as shown in the Haunted Toymaker spells table. These spells count as artificer spells for you, but they don't count against the number of artificer spells you prepare.

entries.caption: Haunted Toymaker Spells
rows: 3rd
{@spell dissonant whispers|PHB|Dissonant Whispers}, {@spell find familiar|PHB|Find Familiars}
5th
{@spell cloud of daggers|PHB|Cloud of Daggers}, {@spell darkness|PHB|Darkness}
9th
{@spell bestow curse|PHB|Bestow Curse}, {@spell fear|PHB|Fear}
13th
{@spell blight|PHB|Blight}, {@spell phantasmal killer|PHB|Phantasmal Killer}
17th
{@spell dream|PHB|Dream}, {@spell mislead|PHB|Mislead}

subclassFeature.name: Scissors and Everything Sharp
entries: {@i "...So you didn't trust me. I told you I'd play scissors!"}

You gain proficiency with {@item battleaxe|PHB|Battleaxes} and you forge a Battleaxe called Scrap Scissors. Scrap Scissors are giant, purple scissors made out of scrap metal with their blades tainted with dried blood, and if it is ever lost or destroyed you can forge a new one during a Long Rest.

Furthermore, you can use your Intelligence modifier for attack and damage rolls with the scissors. Whenever you or a friendly creature within 10 feet of you kills a hostile creature with the Scrap Scissor, you gain 1 Soul. You can carry a maximum amount of Souls equal to your proficiency bonus.
You can spend Souls to construct the items below with an Action. Any item made with a Soul will erode and destroy itself after 24 hours have passed:

items: {@b Strange Doll (1 Soul).} This item is a smiling porcelain doll that seems to follow you with its painted gaze. As an Action, you can see through the doll's eyes, hear what it hears, use your movement speed to make it walk and cast spells through it until the start of your next turn. During this time, you are deaf and blind with regard to your own senses. The doll has Darkvision.

{@b Toy Carriage of Doom (1 Soul).} This item is a small, dark carriage that appears to function on its own. One creature of your choice within 30 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you can use a Bonus Action to force them to use up to half of their movement speed during your turn to walk in a direction you command. On a successful save, they only take {@damage 1d6} Psychic damage instead.

{@b Colorful Pain Brick (1 Soul).} This item is a small, colorful brick covered with nails on its top. Any creature that walks into the area of this item must perform a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, they take {@damage 2d8} bludgeoning damage and suffer 3 counts of {@condition Curse|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. On a successful save, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects.

{@b Jack In the Box (2 Souls).} This item is a box with a nasty, clown-ish surprise inside. When placed on the ground, any creature can interact with it as a Free Action. If a creature interacts with it or it is hit by an Attack, each creature within 15 feet of it must perform a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, they take {@damage 2d10} piercing damage and 3 counts of {@condition Needle|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. On a successful save, they only take half that damage and suffer no additional effects.

{@b Pale Marbles (2 Souls).} This item is a collection of pale white marble spheres. When left on the floor, any creature that walks into the area of this item must perform a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, they fall {@condition Prone} and become {@condition Stunned} until the start of their next turn. On a successful save, they take {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage from the fall.

{@b Bladed Kite (2 Souls).} This item appears to be a kite covered in blades that floats around you. It protects you from incoming attacks, increasing your AC by 2. If you are hit by a melee attack while holding this toy, the attacker takes {@damage 1d6} Slashing damage once per turn.

entries: Finally, you are able to choose an additional Infusion as long as it is a Haunted Toymaker Infusion. At level 5, you are able to choose two additional Haunted Toymaker Infusions, and at level 9 you are able to choose three additional Haunted Toymaker Infusions instead.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: Your Scrap Scissor doesn't need to particularly look like a scissor, it can be any slashing weapon you can think of that fits your character! Furthermore, DMs, the Souls are meant to be acquired through actual fights and not through magical bags of animals and other similar exploits!

subclassFeature.name: Bleeding Extra Attack
entries: {@i "Here folks play by ma rules, or else!"}

You can attack twice, rather than once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn. Additionally, whenever you hit a creature with an Attack Roll, they suffer 2 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

subclassFeature.name: Loser's Penalty
entries: {@i "I don't play with folks who don't trust me."}

Playing games is a part of your essence, it's who you are, and sharing the fun you have in those moments is what you seek to do as a toymaker. As a Bonus Action, you can challenge a willing creature to a game, or force an unwilling creature to play if they fail a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC as long as they aren't Immune to the {@condition Charmed} condition.

A game consists of a challenge explicitly defined by you. It can range from avoiding to take a certain amount of damage in combat, rock paper scissors, not being the last player hunting in tag, a best of three on a game of dice, a simple endurance test etc.

A game cannot last more than a day and usually ends once you tale a Short or Long Rest, unless agreed otherwise by you and your DM. The challenge must not be impossible to be beaten by any of the parties, as that is the fair spirit of haunted games.
The creature that wins the game can choose one of the following benefits until their next Long Rest:

items: You gain advantage on any ability checks and saving throws against the losing creature.
You gain {@dice 1d10} Temporary Hit Points whenever you hit the losing creature with an attack.
The losing creature drops one piece of weapon or armor of your choice.
The losing creature has to give you {@dice 3d10} × 50 gold coins (as long as it has that amount, or as much as possible).
The losing creature gains disadvantage on all ability checks and saving throws related to you.
The losing creature takes 1 additional count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} whenever it is hit by an attack.
The losing creature cannot willingly lie to you, and has to answer one of your questions truthfully to the best of its abilities as long as it is with a "yes" or "no".
The losing creature is hit by your pins and needles, suffering 4 counts of {@condition Needle|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

entries: Additionally, whenever you personally kill a creature, you gain 2 Souls instead of 1.

subclassFeature.name: Will you Play?
entries: {@i "Scissors beats rock. Teehee! That means you lose!"}

Enough time has passed, and your companions no longer fear your creations, but embrace them as a part of who you are—certainly that is true. Whenever a friendly creature is within 5 feet of one of your toys, they gain the following benefits:

items: A bonus of +1 to their AC, to a maximum of +2 per toy.
If the toy is triggered or performs any sort of ability, they gain {@dice 1d10} temporary Hit Points once per turn.
The next time they hit an attack roll, they deal an additional {@damage 1d10} in Psychic damage.
Disadvantage on all saving throws that would give them the {@condition Frightened} condition.

subclassFeature.name: Way of the Bright Star
entries: You have sworn yourself to a life of dedication. There are 108 Heroes that have earned the title of a Star, and your sole goal is to make the Dihui (地會) Star become the one true name people call you by. You utilize the power of Iaido to quickly unsheathe your sword to match your enemies' attacks with expertise and perfection.

In the Forgotten Realms, Monks of the Way of the Bright Star all train under a single roof, then travel to accomplish the tasks set forth by their master so that they can become the next Bright Star, ready to guide the next generation of Monks. In Ravenloft, the sect is much more violent, aiming to kill all other students so that the best and brightest star may stand victorious at the end of the night—it is a matter of hunt and be hunted across the mists. In the cyberpunk world of Genesis, no longer do stars shine in the sky, and Monks of this Monastery will only know they have ascended once they accomplish the impossible—a cut so vast and seamless that the light from the city will be erased, giving way to a beautiful, and naturally illuminated night sky.

Monks of the Way of the Bright Star are diligent students and unerring followers of their master. Consider making a serious character that focuses on nothing else but their goal to reach perfection. If you don't want to play a serious character, what they cannot differ from is their love for the blade and the way, and their desire to see it through, completed.

subclassFeature.name: Singular Focus of Mind
entries: {@i "This lowly self of mine is yet to deserve the name of a Star."}

Focus your breathing - let the world around you go still as you become able to perceive the sound of a falling leaf hitting the ground. During combat, as a Bonus Action, you may spend 1 Ki point to gain 2 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Starting at level 5, you may also spend 3 Ki points to gain 5 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
Additionally, you may use a Bonus Action to spend 1 Ki point and gain a bonus to your {@skill Perception} and {@skill Insight} ability checks equal to a roll of your Martial Arts dice for 1 minute.

Whenever you gain {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count when you already have 4 or more counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, you may choose to convert half of that amount into counts of {@condition Moonlit Azure Blade|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} instead.

subclassFeature.name: Chainstrike [連擊]
entries: {@i "Until such a time arrives that I might inherit the title, I shall continue to be of service to my master and home myself without end."}

You gain proficiency with {@item longsword|PHB|Longswords} and Single-Stroke Katanas, and all swords you hold gain the {@itemProperty DRW|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Draw} ({@damage 1d8}) property. Once per turn, whenever you perform an attack roll, you may choose to unsheathe your blade, attack, then sheathe it again as a part of the same action, gaining 2 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} before the attack.

When you do this, as long as you still have 10 feet of movement remaining, you are able to dash through the attacked creature in a 10-foot line to an unoccupied space, dealing additional damage equal to your Martial Arts dice. Until the end of your turn after dashing this way, you no longer provoke opportunity attacks.
Upon reaching level 6, you can perform this twice per turn, and thrice upon reaching level 17.

Additionally, you may attack with your sword while it is still sheathed, dealing Bludgeoning damage instead of Slashing damage. For each sheathed attack that you hit, you may spend 1 Ki point to gain 1 count of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. If you kill a creature while your weapon is sheathed, you gain 4 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

subclassFeature.name: Nameless Slash [無名斬]
entries: {@i "A single straight stroke to fell them all...!"}

You are now able to connect your sword with the universe, surprising reality itself as you unsheathe your blade and slice it from afar. Once per turn, when you unsheathe your sword to attack, you gain an extra 10-foot reach to that attack. If you attack objects this way, you deal double damage to them. If you destroy structures this way, they are sliced clean.

While performing an attack like this, you may spend 4 Ki points, 5 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or 2 counts of {@condition Moonlit Azure Blade|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} to target an object or item someone is carrying or wearing instead. If it is a magical item, you can still destroy it as long as it is of Rare rarity or lower. Upon reaching level 11 you may destroy Very Rare items, and Legendary items upon reaching level 17.

subclassFeature.name: The Orthodox Blade [整劍]
entries: {@i "Another step closer to that singular Way of the Blade."}

Your dimensional cuts have been getting stronger, and now you can sever the life of more than one enemy at once. At the start of your turn, if you have hit a creature with an unsheathed sword attack last turn, you gain 3 counts of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. Whenever you use a feature that would require you to spend Ki points, you may choose to spend thrice that amount in {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count instead.

As part of your unsheathed attack action, you may spend a number of Ki points equal to 2 per additional creature and attempt to hit a number of additional creatures with your attack equal to your proficiency bonus, as long as they are within 5 feet of the creature that was originally attacked.

subclassFeature.name: Fallstar Slayer [落星一殺]
entries: {@i "Should I return bearing the heads of these fallen foes... Then perhaps, this time, my master might speak of the name Dihui Star... and how I am growing to deserve it."}

The end of your quest is within reach, especially now that you have learned the technique necessary to render universes hostage within your hold. As an Action, you may spend 5 Ki points to create a 10-foot line rift to the Astral Plane in any area within 15 feet of you.

Any creature within 10 feet of the gate must perform a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Wisdom modifier). On a failure, they are sucked through it to a random location on the Astral Plane.
On a success, they take {@damage 10d10} slashing damage but manage to escape the rift's hold. The rift then closes. The rift is one-way only and can't be reopened.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of Procuration
entries: Those who have taken the Oath of Procuration are those who have given up their own desires and judgement in search of executing the Living Will's whims and no more, taking satisfaction in their actions without a second thought—become akin to a guardian devil to whatever it is that such a force comes to desire.

Their personalities might vary, yet a significant characteristic shared among the majority is a seeming lack of a core emotion or understanding of their own actions that can be perceived from how they act. Another characteristic is usually how they are bound in chains, waiting for their unbinding per the Will's whim, and with those chains also always carrying around a device that gives them orders, which is treated much akin to a holy symbol in how fervently they believe in it and cherish it.

In worlds such as the Forgotten Realms, the Will might be a byproduct of the fallen city Netheryl, now using their paladins and shaping them to become great weapons of war and destruction so that the return of such a civilization will then become inevitable. In others, such as Thespis, the tribes of the Lizardmen Nushae have one such Paladin that transforms and shifts without the use of a Wyrdstone—instead channeling the Wyrd directly to enact its lord's will upon the material plane.

subclassFeature.name: Tenets of Procuration
entries: A paladin who takes this oath has the tenets of Procuration has their tenets inscribed at the back of a device they carry around known as a Magicked Beeper or a Procuration Relay. That is a magic item that is Attuned to the paladin, yet doesn't count toward maximum attunement slots.

It cannot be affected by anti-magic effects and if removed from your person, it reappears instantly to be bound to your neck through a collar. You cannot remove the collar by any means short of the Will demanding it, the {@spell wish} spell or through special means.

items.name: Aid the Will With Heart.
items.entry: Nothing matters more than the Will's whims, and you are no exception, follow orders even if they might put you at risk, for that is the Will.

items.name: Follow the Prescripts.
items.entry: Never betray that which binds you to purpose, for procuring their goals is what matter most, for that is the Will.

items.name: Hunt Down Oathbreakers.
items.entry: Those who fail to follow these holy tenets must be struck down by your blade, for that is the Will.

items.name: Recognize That Which is Absolute.
items.entry: Nobody, nothing and no being is above the Will. Bring down any in its path if necessary, for that is the Will.

subclassFeature.name: Oath Spells
entries: You gain oath spells at the paladin levels listed.

entries.caption: Oath of Procuration Spells
rows: 3rd
{@spell arms of hadar}, {@spell guiding bolt}
5th
{@spell knock}, {@spell phantasmal force}
9th
{@spell sending}, {@spell thunder step|XGE}
13th
{@spell divination}, {@spell Weaver's Wright|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Weaver's Write}
17th
{@spell destructive wave}, {@spell steel wind strike|XGE}

subclassFeature.name: Breaking your Oath
entries: When first creating a Paladin of Procurement, its best to consider which path your character might go down. As it stands, this subclass is centered around giving up your free will to be guided by a greater force that altough might be beneficent in certain settings, is mostly serving its own purpose at best or is actively detrimental to most and stiffling to you at worse. As such, this subclass features a modicum of support toward the end of an Oathbreaker.

Through the levels in this subclass you have many features that depend on being in tune with the Will, so it is highly recommended to talk to your DM about planning out if your character will start having doubts and possibly even having their powers fail them suddenly at hours of need for the drama and development.

We also would like to make it clear that the best way to do this (in our perspective) is to have this be a slow-burn development, with your character slowly coming to realize the error in surrendering their self to a greater Will or even through other party members pushing them toward thinking for themselves.

There is a matter as of how to keep mechanics and the flavours of an Oathbreaker in tune during this, and although a Capstone feature is provided for them, their other features aren't provided in such alternatives. In their stead, we recommend having the character coming to learn that all the power driven from their Oath is instead a manifestation of their own Faith that becomes easier to wield as they accept themselves and start believing in their own unfettered potential.
Another thing to keep in mind is how other characters may react to their breach of Oath, since the Living Will and their associated Factions usually employ heavy witch hunts to take out Oathbreakers.
In the future there may have supplemental content to this concept, yet as of now we wish the best of luck for those who can't wait to have their character's develop past the need of another's Will.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: As you might come around reading this s subclass subclass as a whole, you will see that it employs many unique Conditions and Effects. As such, we cannot recommend it for beginners with the 5e System, as it might be too complex to follow for that.

For those intending to use it, we recommend that the Player who plays this subclass keeps track of their own Prescript list, current Poise, Grace, Karma and Unlock counts. Do so either using a simple notepad in your computer or at the corner of your sheet/piece of paper.
As for Sinking application or Grace/Karma on other creatures, we recommend noting such down beside their turn in Initiative so their effects are easier to keep track of when triggered.

subclassFeature.name: Channel Divinity: The Great Magicked Beeper
entries: {@i "'Those whose eyes you have met, and those whose eyes you have not. 72 minutes. Kill.' Tis thou. Flee thee not, for the P-Prescript pointeth to thee."}
When you take this oath at 3rd level, you gain the following two Channel Divinity options.

entries.name: /UNLOCK./
entries: Your heart and soul are entwined with the Living Will, and it's bidding is your own desire. Although bound in chain and key, you may spend your Action to temporarily be removed from such bounds. When you do so, you enter an /UNLOCKED/ state (More may be found below.) for the next minute or until you are knocked {@condition Unconscious}.

While in an /UNLOCKED./ /state, state, a shadowy flame-like emanation covers your arms and sprouts from your forehead like horns, (or covers your horns, if able.) completely synchronizing you with the Will. These count as natural weapons you are proficient with, they deal {@damage 1d8} radiant damage and have the Finesse property, but the formation of claws around your fingers impedes wielding any weapons or shields. Additionally, at the start of your turns, if no hostile creature is The Prescript's Target, a creature becomes the Target as per the effect's description found at the end of this document.

Furthermore, while in this state your Unlocking slowly intensifies to greater outputs of power as you carry out the Will, starting with an Unlock count of 1. You inflict {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} counts on your weapon and spell attacks equal to your current Unlock count. You have Advantage on your first Attack Roll during your turn against the Target.

You gain one further count of Unlock for each cumulative 3 counts of Grace of the Prescript you have, and lose all counts when you exit your /UNLOCKED./ state. You gain one Grace whenever a creature with The Prescript's Target is first knocked {@condition Unconscious} or is killed.

entries.name: /PREORDAIN./
entries: You convene with your magicked device for guidance and clearance on what to do in a difficult path. You may ask any question to your DM, to which they may answer with a simple "Yes." or "No.", or if unable to produce such a clear answer, instead uttering a single word as a tip toward your objective, such as for example:

If you and your fellows are hunting a mad vampire, your DM may answer a vague but usable answer, such as "Spire." Nevertheless, if your objective is one that mav be blessed by the Device (A list can be found below. ), you gain an {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to Skill Checks pertaining to concluding that objective as your intuition grows stronger and more attuned to the Will.
Your /PREORDAIN./ Channel Divinity may come to grant you its bonus modifier in the following situations:

items: Finding a place or locale that you have asked about as part of this Channel Divinity.
For any Checks toward reaching the answer of a piece of research, such as finding a cure for a great plague.
To Charisma checks pertaining to interacting with other creatures to reach a desired outcome as per what you asked in this Channel Divinity.
To survive an immediate threat and escape from it, such as when asking the question of how to run away from a Dragon.
To tame or calm an animal or other similarly bestial creature.
Anything else that your DM agrees is fair to your question and that will lead you to the Will's objective.

entries.name: Designer's Note 1
entries: Usually, a Paladin of this subclass has a special Device that conveys them orders from their deity. It's a good idea to have this be a magic item that is permanently bound to them for as long as their Oath endures, re-appearing on their person if lost or that they may recall with a special ritual. It is also a recommended idea to have this function as a magic focus for the Paladin.

entries.name: Designer's Note 2
entries: Some may find the/PREORDAIN./ Channel Divinity too messy or too difficult to use, and for that we recommend instead using the alternative Channel Divinity that can be found at the end of this feature.

entries.name: Alternate Channel Divinity
entries: {@b /PREORDAIN./ [ALT].} You convene with your magicked device for guidance and clearance on what to do in a difficult path. You instantly cast any Divination spell from the Paladin spell list without spending a spell slot. You may only cast these spells as long as you may cast spells of that appropriate level, such as needing to reach at least 5th-level in Paladin to cast the {@spell locate object} spell.

subclassFeature.name: Aura of Onus
entries: {@i "Seest thou? Verily, the Prescript is absolute!"}
Starting at 7th level, your sheer feeling of duty spreads and covers those around you like an invisible membrane. This aura covers 10-ft. around you while you are not {@condition Incapacitated}.

At the start of any creature's turns provided that they are within the area, they may partake into one Prescript that manifests in front of them, gaining one count of Grace of the Prescript upon its completion, or suffering two counts of Karmic Consequence when failing to complete them until the start of their next turn.

To define a Prescript, it is recommended to roll on the Magicked Prescripts Table found at the end of this document When you take a Prescript in this way, you have two turns to complete it (Ending at the start of the turn after your next one.) and you gain an additional count of Grace of the Prescript upon a Prescript's completion.
Additionally, upon reaching 7th level in this subclass you may use your /UNLOCK./ Channel Divinity without spending a use of the feature, but instead suffering 2 counts of Karmic Consequence.

subclassFeature.name: Efflorescence of Will
entries: {@i "Preordained! Absolute."}

Your own will has been attuned to match a near perfect synchrony with the Will, and that glorious revelation has been set in stone in a way that an overwhelming feeling of pride and relief washes over you whenever you conclude a Prescript. As such, you gain the following:

items: Once per short rest you may choose which Prescription you or another creature gains at the start of their turn instead of rolling on the Magicked Prescripts Table. (Or other suitable Table.)
Whenever you conclude a Prescript you may choose to end one negative Condition that is afflicting you.

entries: Whenever you conclude a Prescript you gain one count of Fulfilled Onus. This counter can be spent to use the following abilities as an Action:

items.name: The Proxy of the Will.
items.entry: You spend one Fulfilled Onus to have your heart beat in tune with the Will, giving up your body momentarily as a conduit of it. You instantly move up to 15-ft. toward any other creature and perform a melee weapon attack against them. On a hit you gain 4 Poise and the target suffers from Mark of the e Prescript until the end of combat or until they are killed.

items.name: Engrave.
items.entry: You spend one Fulfilled Onus to unleash the Will's mark upon the world. You perform two melee weapon attacks against a target within reach. These attacks inflict 4 Sinking count on a hit, or deal half the damage they would on a miss.

items.name: Annihilate.
items.entry: You dutifully follow your orders. You spend three Fulfilled Onus and perform up to five melee weapon attacks against a target within reach. If a creature dies to Annihilate, you may instantly move up to 15-ft. toward another creature and perform any remaining attacks plus one against them, repeating the process up to 3 times. Whenever a creature is killed in this way, you gain one Grace of the Prescript.

subclassFeature.name: To Find That Which is Inside You
entries: {@i "...May as well get used to it, right?"}

As you reach 20th level, a split path is before you and you must make a choice based on the progression of your character thus far. These are split in polar opposites, either embracing the Will fully and having your being be indiscernible from it, or severing your ties to that which points your way and becoming your own being. Upon reaching 20th level, make a choice:

items: その時、下人は迷いを捨てた。 You gain the Unquestionable. Unquestionable. feature.
僕は幸福よりも真理を選ぶ。You gain the Truthful Procuration. feature.

entries.name: Unquestionable. Unquestionable.
entries: {@i "Hear all. Hope all. With these hands, all will…"}

Your heart beats when the Will wills it so, and it will cease beating only when the Will wills it so. The Prescripts that have led, fed and nourished you are all that your heart desires, and you in kind are part of the Will's wishes. Upon reaching the 20th level, you become the living instrument for the Will to enact itself upon the world, gaining the following benefits:

items: In addition to the random creature chosen randomly to become the The Prescript's Target, the first creature you hit during your turn also suffers from the effect. You may not choose another creature to become a Target until your chosen one is dead, and that creature does not count toward your Channel Divinity Feature's limit.
Your /UNLOCKED/ state now lasts for up to 10 minutes and you gain a +2 modifier to AC while in it.
You gain double the counts of Grace of the Prescript and Karmic Consequence whenever you gain either of the Conditions.

entries.name: Truthful Procuration
entries: {@i "I have the talent to walk the path in front of me, if nothing else… Even if I don't have much happiness, I know where to go in the immediate future. And that's enough for me."}

How long has it been since you've last tried to think for yourself, without the input of some magicked "thing" nebulously telling you what to do? Long. But not too long, as your path to healing from that programming has been set on its way, and you to find your own.

Upon reaching the 20th level, you may choose to break your Oath and sever your connection to the Will, but maintain everything that you have learnt while following this path and finally making it your own. You gain the following:

items: You lose your Channel Divinity features.

You may enter your /UNLOCKED/ state as a Bonus Action for one minute or until you are knocked Unconscious. You may do so up to three times per long rest. When you do so, the appearance of the manifestation around your body is that of your body, usually taking some form that represents you as your own person.

Instead of randomly deciding the creature who becomes the The Prescript's Target at the start of your turns, you instead decide to have any one creature you can see that is within 60-ft. of you to become the Target instead. Only you and friendly creatures benefit from the effects benefits.
While in your/UNLOCKED/ state you gain an additional 10-ft. of movement speed and may use your Charisma modifier in place of Dexterity for saving throws and against being Grappled.
Your Karmic Consequence count is reduced by an additional count whenever you finish a long rest.
You gain proficiency in the Insight skill, or Expertise if you were already proficient.

Whenever you draw a Prescript as per your Aura of Onus feature, you gain its benefits whenever you ensure that you and any other creature within 120-ft. of you fails to conclude that Prescript, and suffer its negative effects whenever a Prescript is concluded.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: Breaking a Paladin's Oath is never an easy feature, much less while using this subclass. However, the Will may not be an entirely (if even that) good presence in your campaign and your character's development might be to break away from it and have to start making their own choices through life.

Although it cannot be reflected in the subclass earlier as it is because of Paladin limitations, becoming an Oathbreaker in this subclass does not mean a full mechanical switch to another sub but instead gaining the Truthful Procuration feat. You and your DM may discuss implementing parts of Truthful Procuration's benefits at key moments of your character's development for a more gradual shift toward breaking apart from the Living Will.
Nevertheless, it's always a good idea to think of your character's now and their inevitable future at the creation of said character, so discuss with your DM to determine their best self!

subclassFeature.name: Middle's Blade
entries: {@i "C'mon, Mama! I thought I asked you to knock before barging into my room."}

Those that walk the path of the Middle's Blade are excited up and comers ready to serve the faction however they can. They might not have the muscles and the brawn, but they more than make up for it with speed, precise attacks and the right tools for the job. The Middle is a criminal group that values loyalty above all else, treating members as siblings, and your dream is to be taken into their fold like one of their brothers and sisters, no matter the strength behind one of your punches.

In the Forgotten Realms, the Half is a criminal faction in Waterdeep that is recruiting people to join their familial gang, claiming that they're all the half missing on each other. In Ravenloft, the Half unites in small villages on the edges of the Mists, trying to use the fear and paranoia to create a sense of unity to survive the horrors of the world. In the dark fantasy world of Alacritas, the gods have long abandoned humanity, so humanity decided to unite among the remnants and thrive. If the gods no longer care, the Half believes they need to care for each other to get through this endless tribulation. All that are accepted into the Half's fold are family, all that reject it and condemn it will suffer the same human ire the gods faced and deemed too dangerous to love.

There are plenty of ways to play a Middle's Blade. You can be someone excited that recently joined the Middle or relevant criminal gang and want to show your worth to your brothers and sisters. Usually a Middle's Blade is young and unafraid, ready to show their potential and grow within the gang. There's also the possibility that you are not a part of the Middle but would love to be, and have been cosplaying and working hard to become one of their members. Either way, you are someone dedicated to the Middle that would stop at nothing to be recognized by them.

entries.name: The Middle Never Forgets, Y'Know?
entries: {@i "Wanna come read with me and see who our next kill's gonna be, if you're not busy?"}

During combat, the enemy that dealt the most damage to you or your allies this round gains a {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. This lasts until the end of the next round, or until you fall unconscious. If no enemy has dealt damage this turn, the stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} is given to the enemy that last attempted to attack you or an allied creature.

If two enemies dealt the same amount of highest damage, the stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} goes to the latest enemy that dealt this damage. Outside of combat, whenever someone rolls an ability check to hurt or damage your character or their reputation, they will also gain a point of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} until your next short rest.

If combat is initiated right after an instance of this by rolling an initiative check, then the enemy with the highest initiative roll gains {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} until the end of the first round of combat. Whenever you hit an enemy with a stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, they gain 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. This number increases to 2 at level 5.

If you or a friendly creature within 60 feet of you is hit by an attack from a creature with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, your attacks deal an extra {@damage 1d4} bludgeoning damage to them until the end of your next turn. This number increases to {@damage 1d6} at level 5, {@damage 1d8} at level 11 and {@damage 1d10} at level 17.

entries.name: Thermal Weapon
entries: {@i "Duking it out with a badass Fixer, beating the crap outta each other 'till I pop their head off-nothing tops that, right?"}

Whenever you start your turn within 30 feet of a creature with counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, gain 1 count of {@condition Thermal Blades|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. Gain 1 more count of {@condition Thermal Blades|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} if a creature within the area is also suffering from counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

Additionally, you can do cool poses to strike fear into your enemy's heart. You gain advantage on Intimidation ability checks, and, as a Bonus Action, you can make a Charisma (Intimidation) check contested by a creature's Wisdom (Insight) check. If your result is higher, they become {@condition Frightened} of you for 1 minute. They can repeat this ability check at the end of their turn, ending the effect on a success.

You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a long rest. Any creature {@condition Frightened} by you this way takes an additional {@damage 1d4} dice of damage whenever taking ( {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or) {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. damage. Additionally, they become more willing to provide you information, usually not requiring a Charisma (Persuasion) ability check or decreasing its DC by 5.

subclassFeature.name: Crossing Dervish
entries: {@i "Leaping across rooftops of the City~ To protect its peace and safety~"}

You have reached a point in your life where your knowledge has branched out to cover famous criminals and adventurers, and your battle skills are unrivaled. Once per Long Rest, you can cast {@spell legend lore} without expending a spell slot, however, it will also work for adventurers even if they are not yet of legendary importance.

If you have cast {@spell legend lore} this way to obtain information on a creature, you may choose to have this creature gain {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} until your next Long Rest. Finally, you gain the following benefits. The DC for them is 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier:

items: When you take the {@action Dash} action, you leave a fire trail behind you until the start of your next turn. Any creature that moves into or ends their turn inside the area must perform a Dexterity saving throw against your save DC. On a failed save, they take {@damage 2d6} fire damage. On a successful save, they only take half that damage.

When you take the {@action Disengage} action, choose a creature within 5 feet of you. They must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be forced to drop one of the items they're holding at random as you kick at them to fain momentum to escape.
When you take the {@action Hide} action, your next attack that hits deals an extra {@damage 1d6} damage of the weapon's type.

subclassFeature.name: You're Gonna Burn Up
entries: {@i "Teehee. You malding, bro? Whatchagonna do about it?"}

You have learned how to keep your blades searing hot at will. With an Action, you can heat up your blade for 1 minute to cut through non-magical items and structures. You deal double damage to objects and structures with your weapon attacks. This feature has no effect on magical objects.

Additionally, while your sword is burning this way, you deal an additional 2 counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} when you hit a creature with an attack roll. Whenever an attack of yours would inflict a count of ({@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} this way, inflict the same amount of) {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the target.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: While this ability may appear simple at first, feel free to use it in creative ways. Carve a hole on the ground to create a trap for an enemy, destroy a wall to block the path and create difficult terrain, or even destroy walls to quickly get through locations. The world is the Middle's oyster!

subclassFeature.name: Violet~ Breaking Slam
entries: {@i "Phew... Well, that takes care of the last of the 'Up-and-Coming Fixer Offices' featured in Fixers Monthly."}
The power of the family's love and old, famous catchphrases from brave adventurers fill your heart with wonder and a burning desire to never stop fighting.

As a Reaction when a creature with {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} hits you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you, you may immediately perform a melee attack against them if you are within range, moving up to your remaining speed towards them if necessary. If the attack hits, choose one of the abilities below to trigger:

items: {@b I Do Not Forgive You. VIOLET SWORD!} This attack deals an additional amount of damage equal to half your Sneak Attack dice.

{@b The Show's Over. ALL-OUT ATTACK!} Immediately after you attack, you may choose a friendly creature within 30 feet of you to spend their Reaction and perform an attack against the same creature if within range.
{@b Siblings of the Family, I WILL LEND YOU MY ENERGY!} Choose a creature within 30 feet of you to recover 1 use of their Middle Tattoo feature.
{@b My Life Has No Regrets. FIRE BLADE!} Double all counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the target.
{@b Don't "What?" Me. YOU'RE ALREADY DEAD!} Double all counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the target.

entries: You can use this ability twice, and you regain all expended uses on a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Blackened Hands
entries: {@i "That's that, and this is this."}

A Fighter with Blackened Hands is someone who has the risk of having all that matters escape their grasp like sand. The only thing keeping them together is their own will to survive as a great warrior, yet the path they thread is forked and oftentimes in solitude or with very few important people.

Some walk a path that cannot be heard, gracefully embracing the shade and coming out only to leave the remains of their targets to be displayed-a magnificent, silent spectacle. Those are masters of stealth and sometimes embodying a chivalric essence with prowess and dignity that is hard to mimic.

Others have lost everything, being resigned to the path marked not only by shade but becoming one with that darkness themselves, wielding a righteous fury that drives men and women mad like a weapon to scorch the earth they thread upon. That path is one of sorrow and where one cannot stop to mourn the angels that are gone.

What binds both, where all roads meet is that it's from their heart and experience that all their power comes from. Every little skirmish, every little scar left on them and by them forms a story that causes the one with Blackened Hands to be a unique being in the way that they paint whichever world they reside in black.

entries.name: Canti ai Grandi Paladini
entries: {@i "L'arme e gli amori, e i cavallier, l'audaci imprese io canto."}

Through a rigid mastery over many weapons and experience, you have developed your own technique to employ your own symphony of varied weapons, turning your very fingers into an instrument to tap into your entire arsenal.

You have managed to create a small storage within your own heart, a demiplane connected to your core known as a Lasting Arsenal, formed by a combination of magical items or an innate, magical manifestation of your own inner being.

You may store up to your proficiency bonus' worth of weapons in your Lasting Arsenal, being able to store any weapon not held by another creature as a Free Action you may take while grasping them, and have a stored weapon appear on your hand as another Free Action.

If you would attempt to add another weapon while your Lasting Arsenal has no space left, you must replace any of your already stored weapons with the new one, with the replaced one being manifested in your empty hand.
While a weapon is a part of your Lasting Arsenal, you are considered Attuned to it. This Attunement does not count toward your maximum Attuned items.

entries.name: Cavalier in Nero
entries: {@i "Orlando, il più prode de' paladini, armato di Durindana e di coraggio senza pari, non temeva alcun nemico."}

Your mastery in arms is unparalleled, being able to wring out the best of any one weapon that graces your hands. While a weapon is part of your Lasting Arsenal, you gain special benefits listed at the end of this subclass.

These have both passive effects that are active as long as you are wielding the weapon or they are stored inside your Arsenal, and active Flourishes which can be used every other turn per weapon as an Action.
If you use a Dagger's Flourish in one turn, on the next turn you may still use another weapon's Flourish but not your Dagger's.

entries.name: Cavalier in Nero Flourishes
entries: The following Flourishes have passive effects that are granted while within your Lasting Arsenal and active effects that may be used in place of an Attack as part of your Attack action. For any weapon not directly named, you may refer to the Weapon Groups table, such as a Rapier counting as a Shortsword for its Flourish bonuses. If a Saving Throw is requested, your DC is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your choice of your Strength or Dexterity modifier.

entries.name: Dagger's Agility
entries: Daggers grant unparalleled agility and mobility, granting you an additional 5-ft. of movement.

entries.name: Flourish: Rock Bottom Bounceback
entries: You may throw the dagger in a way that it'll ricochet right back to your hand after being thrown. When you do so, perform a ranged attack roll on a target within its Thrown range, ignoring Partial Cover. Regardless of if you hit or miss, the weapon is flung back to you after hitting any surface.

entries.name: Greatsword's Destruction
entries: A greatsword in your hands is a weapon that neglects the need for any shield, cutting through any attack with ease, reducing any damage you take by one plus any Bonus Modifier to hit the weapon has.

entries.name: Flourish: District Cleaver
entries: You may swing the Greatsword to cover great arcs, perform a melee attack roll against a target within reach. The result also counts as if it were targeting any other creatures 5-ft. beside the original target, when you roll damage you do so once for all targets hit.

entries.name: Handaxe's Versatility
entries: The Handaxe is the perfect weapon to cover for any other arm's weakness. You still add half your relevant Modifiers when dealing damage with your Bonus Action attack, as per Two-Weapon Fighting rules.

entries.name: Flourish: Sinking Reverb
entries: You throw your Handaxe at any target creature within its minimum thrown reach. On a hit, you may instantly rush toward them, moving to be within 5-ft. of the target.

entries.name: Heavy Gauntlet's Dukes
entries: A good pair of Gauntlets easily help with maintaining an overall defensive stance, granting you a +1 bonus modifier to Constitution and Dexterity saving throws.

entries.name: Flourish: Clawing Out the Wind
entries: You deliver a particularly powerful punch to the target's lungs, beating the very air out of them. Perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach, on a hit they must pass a Constitution saving throw or have their movement speed halved and Attack Modifier reduced by half your proficiency bonus until the end of their next turn.

entries.name: Katana's Airwall
entries: The dexterity needed to wield a Katana properly is nothing to scoff at, and it's bursts of action teach a special means of defense against projectiles. Ranged attacks against you suffer a -2 negative modifier to hit.

entries.name: Flourish: Gone in a Blink
entries: You ready your Katana and slash without giving your target a moment to perceive it. You perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach. If your Katana is sheathed, you have Advantage on this attack and deal additional damage equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down) on a hit. Furthermore, if able you may move to be 5-ft. behind the target.

entries.name: Lance's March
entries: The Lance is a movement in of itself, a constant that cannot be broken, granting you the ability to move through up to 15-ft. of Difficult Terrain each turn without needing to spend any additional movement speed.

entries.name: Flourish: Slaughterline
entries: You prepare for a mad dash with your Lance at the forefront. Choose an empty space within 20-ft. to move to, all creatures in the line required for you to move to there must pass a Dexterity saving throw or be impaled, taking your Lance's damage die and being both knocked {@condition Prone} and forcibly moved into the space in front of where you end, or the closest unoccupied space instead.

entries.name: Light Hammer's Wedge
entries: A Light Hammer's head can easily be used to wedge out even the nastiest attack from being a hit. You gain the ability to use your Reaction to increase your AC by one when you would be targeted by an attack, before or after its rolled, potentially turning a hit into a miss.

entries.name: Flourish: Arsenal Breaker
entries: You may use the Hammer's head to hook and tear away your opponents weapon with ease. Perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach, on a hit they must pass a Dexterity saving throw or have one weapon of your choice that they are holding be flung toward any space within 15-ft. of them.

entries.name: Longsword's Lockstep
entries: The Longsword's elegant maneuvers ease into a dance of attacks in your hands, granting you a +1 bonus modifier to hit whenever you move before attacking

entries.name: Flourish: Inescapable Void
entries: Though simple in nature, a well-used Longsword is a weapon to put fear into your foe's hearts. You perform a weapon attack roll against a target within reach. On a hit, the target must pass a Wisdom saving throw or be {@condition Frightened} of you. While {@condition Frightened}, the target cannot willingly move away from you, as they are paralyzed by your presence.

entries.name: Mace's Siege
entries: The strength needed to wield a Mace is one to tear down anything in your path, granting you the ability to deal double any bludgeoning damage to objects and buildings.

entries.name: Flourish: Sundermind
entries: You bring down your Mace in a particularly nasty blow to the head. Perform a melee weapon attack against a creature within reach, on a hit they must pass a Constitution saving throw or receive a negative modifier to their Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma saving throws equal to half your proficiency bonus until the end of their next turn.

entries.name: Revolver's Deadzone
entries: The Revolver is a versatile weapon, but that versatility is brought out fully only when you have a perfect vision to acknowledge multiple targets at once, granting you the ability to deal an additional 2 damage whenever you first hit a different creature than your last target during your turn.

entries.name: Flourish: Grand Slaughter
entries: Instead of performing a single attack against a single target, you'd rather empty your Revolver and the remaining hostile roster all at once. You perform one ranged weapon attack per each remaining bullet in your chamber, as per the {@itemProperty RLD|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Reload} property. Each of these attacks must target a different target creature and you don't add your Dexterity modifier to your damage rolls.

entries.name: Rifle's Positioning
entries: To wield a Rifle perfectly you must learn how to keep the distance between you and any other threat, granting you the ability to spend your Reaction whenever a hostile creature moves into 5-ft. of you to quickly dash away into a 10-ft. line in any direction of your choice. Any Opportunity Attacks that are triggered from this are done at disadvantage.

entries.name: Flourish: Shooting Stars
entries: You take aim to pierce only through soft tissue. Instead of performing an attack roll, all creatures within a line whose range is equal to the minimum Range of your Rifle must pass a Dexterity saving throw or be hit, taking the damage you would do with a regular weapon attack using your Rifle, or half on a success.

entries.name: Shortsword's Denial
entries: The Shortsword's elegant maneuvers ease into a dance of attacks in your hands, having you deal +2 bonus damage on a hit whenever you move before attacking.

entries.name: Flourish: Retake Control
entries: You maintain dominance through any battlefield. Perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach, on a hit the target is moved back 5-ft. each time you hit it until the end of your turn.

entries.name: Poesie per il Silencio Weapon Groups
entries: The following weapon groups are meant to simplify the use of certain abilities of both of your 3rd and 10th level subclass features while wielding specific weapons that are not directly mentioned, listing the Main Weapons and the weapons within their groups.

items: {@b Dagger:} Dart, Javelin.
{@b Greatsword:} Battleaxe.
{@b Handaxe:} Trident.
{@b Heavy Gauntlet:} Unarmed Strike, Greatclub, Maul, Quarterstaff.
Single-Stroke Katana.
{@b Lance:} Glaive, Spear, Pike.
{@b Light Hammer:} Halberd, Net, Whip.
{@b Longsword:} Flail, Morningstar.
{@b Mace:} Club, Greataxe, War Pick, Warhammer.
{@b Revolver:} Hand Crossbow, Light Crossbow, Shortbow, Sling.
{@b Rifle:} Heavy Crossbow, Longbow, Wooden Staff.
{@b Shortsword:} Double-Bladed Scimitar, Scimitar, Sickle.

entries: Any weapons without required properties such as {@itemProperty DRW|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Draw} or {@itemProperty RLD|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Reload} may be considered as if they had them. Ranged weapons within the Revolver group are considered to have Reload (5).

entries.name: Graziosa Pazienzia
entries: {@i "Muovea il cavaliere con passo misurato e gesto gentile, ché ogni azione traduceva onore."}

The marks and scars of your training and expertise fit your fingers like a glove, yet they are worn not only as a symbol of brutality but of grace and restraint. You gain proficiency in your choice of Sleight of Hand or Stealth, or Expertise instead if you were already proficient with the chosen skill.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: If you wish to employ Two-Handed Fighting with this subclass is subclass, you may count both weapons as single one for the sake of storing them into your Arsenal while consuming only one "Equipment Slot", but to summon them you need both hands free, instead of being able to summon each individually.

subclassFeature.name: 7th-level Notice
entries: Upon reaching 7th-Level in the Blackened Hands Martial Archetype, choose one of the following class features: Scintille un di Pazzo or Muto Errante.
Upon reaching 18th-Level, you gain the feature corresponding to the one you have picked: Orlando Furioso for Scintille un di Pazzo, and Orlando Innamorato for Muto Errante.

entries.name: Scintille un di Pazzo
entries: {@i "Gridando va, senza dir cosa che s'intenda."}

The seed of a growing madness and fury has been planted in your heart, having your personhood and the way you portray yourself be tinted in a darker shade than most. Whenever you suffer damage you may use your Reaction to enter a Fury state. While Furious, you gain the following effects:

items: You gain a bonus modifier to hit and to damage rolls equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down.
After first knocking another creature below one hit point or killing them, you deal one additional damage die on melee weapon attacks until the end of your next turn.
You suffer a negative modifier to Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma saving throws equal to half your proficiency bonus, rounded down.

entries: You may enter this state once per long rest and remain in it for one minute. This state ends early if you are knocked {@condition Unconscious} or are the target of the {@spell calm emotions} spell.
You may enter a Fury state twice per long rest after reaching 14th level.

entries.name: Muto Errante
entries: {@i "Rimase Orlando, e non parlò parola."}

You are a professional in your line of work, rising to be the brightest star you can be in the only way to know how: obfuscating that shine and only revealing yourself after the job is done. Your Arsenal has developed further, allowing you to coat your hands in a fine black substance that dampens all sound around it, save for your weapons cutting through the air.

You may don and doff this coating as a free action, and while having them on any noise within a 15-ft. radius of you is silenced unless you choose it not to be, except for the sounds of your weapons being fired or swung. While donning the coating you also gain advantage on Stealth Skill Checks that involve sound.
When first gaining this feature, you may choose to gain Proficiency in the Stealth or Sleight of Hand skills, or Expertise if you were already Proficient with the chosen skill.

subclassFeature.name: Poesie per il Silenzio
entries: {@i "La vittoria ama chi più osa."}

Much like a poet weaving hymn and rhyme together, your varied weaponry is swung not with wild abandon, but with a rhythm that unites all you can give. Whenever you perform a weapon attack, if your next attack is made with a different weapon you gain special effects as per the last weapon used. These are as follows:

items: {@b Dagger:} Your next attack gains the Dagger's Thrown property and range.
{@b Greatsword:} Your next attack inflicts additional damage equal to your proficiency bonus.
{@b Handaxe:} Your next attack is done with advantage.
{@b Heavy Gauntlet:} You may choose to move yourself and the target 5-ft. forward after this attack and on your next attack's hit.
{@b Katana:} Your next attack gains the Katana's {@itemProperty DRW|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Draw} property and is treated as if the weapon is sheathed.
{@b Lance:} Your next attack gains the Lance's Reach property.
{@b Light Hammer:} Your next attack considers its target as if it had 1 less AC.
{@b Longsword:} Your next attack deals damage even if missed. Roll your damage die without any modifiers, the target takes half the value rolled.
{@b Mace:} Your next attack deals an additional damage die.
{@b Revolver:} Before your next attack you may move up to half your movement speed toward any target creature within your attack range without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
{@b Rifle:} Before your next attack you may move up to half your movement speed away from any target creature without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
{@b Shortsword:} our next attack has a +1 bonus modifier to hit.

entries: More weapons can be found at the end of this subclass, separated into weapon groups according to the effects above.

subclassFeature.name: A Chi Piange Questa Spada
entries: {@i "A chi la impugna, questa spada è morte;"}
The manifestations from your inner self have rooted deeply in your heart, blossoming out into an even stronger Arsenal that flows as easily as you breathe. You gain the following benefits:

items: Weapons linked to your Arsenal cannot be destroyed by any means other than the {@spell wish} spell, even if you die.

When attacking with a weapon linked to your Arsenal, you always use the bonus modifier of the highest magical weapon stored in your Arsenal, such as if you attack with a +1 dagger but have linked a +3 sword, you may instead consider the dagger as if it had a +3 modifier instead.
You have advantage against being {@condition Grappled} and skill checks regarding being disarmed in any way.

entries.name: Orlando Furioso
entries: {@i "Le donne, i cavallier, l'arme, gli amori, le cortesie, l'audaci imprese io canto..."}
Something inside you has fundamentally broken, like a realization that was meant to be wasn't ever truly concluded. While Furious, you also gain the following:

items: You gain one Extra Attack.
You gain Advantage on Saving Throws.

Choose one of the weapons in your Arsenal to become your Signature weapon. This weapon becomes bound to you and cannot be used by any other creature. Furthermore, you have a +1 bonus modifier to hit with it and it scores a Critical Hit on a roll of 18-20. This bonus does not benefit your 15th Level feature.
Additionally, when you use your Action Surge while Furious, whenever you hit with a weapon your next weapon attack is done at Advantage.
If you are Two-Weapon Fighting, you may immediately perform an additional attack with the weapon on your off-hand without it counting toward your total attacks.

entries.name: Orlando Innamorato
entries: {@i "Amor mi strinse con sì dolce nodo, che mai da poi non fui di me signore."}
Your heart has become a fulfilled thing, your mind enlightened by a confidence in all your work, and your steps silent as you bring others into the black with ease. You gain the following benefits:

items: Your experience has shaped you to be versatile not only with your weaponry, but also with your other abilities.
You gain Expertise in one Skill of your choice that you are Proficient with.
Whenever you hit a Surprised creature or while Hidden you may choose to forgo one of your attacks as part of the Attack Action, instead delivering the full brunt of your force in one decisive attack.

This attack benefits from double the effects of your Poesie per il Silenzio feature (Doubling the value of any range, die or other value.) and deals an additional 3 damage die that match your weapon's damage type.
Whenever you kill another creature or knock them {@condition Unconscious} for the first time you may spend your Reaction to {@action Hide}, as per the Hide Action.

subclassFeature.name: The Living Will
entries: {@i "You may brood over curiosities regarding the Will of the Prescript, yet inquiry bears no weight in its execution. What is absolute can only be obeyed."}

A Warlock who serves a patron known only as the "Living WIll" is one who is either purely devoted or forced into submission by forces way past any sense of recognition except acceptance. They are usually highly organized and may even follow a hierarchical structure, unlike many other of those who have made pacts - to the point they may be confused even for clergy with their regimented arts.

When playing with this subclass, consider your character's relation to the Living Will itself and its ordinance, such as if the character is one to follow whatever orders they are given blindly or have questions about them and their vagueness. A good theme to go in line with this choice of subclass is nearly always having your character question their sense of freedom and how much their own will affects themselves and the world around them.

In worlds such as the Forgotten Realms, the Will manifests itself as a by-product of the fall of the great Netheril - a series of magical constructs that melded together into a collective conscience that outlived the fallen empire. In others, such as Thespis, it is instead a creed nurtured by the Nushae, grand lizardkin who worship the Wyrd, taking the Will as the Wyrd's very own and using such force to shape the material plane in its image.

entries.name: Expanded Spell List
entries: The Living Will lets you choose from an expanded list of spells when you learn a warlock spell. The following spells are added to the warlock spell list for you. You also gain the {@spell First Lightlock|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} cantrip as one of your Warlock spells.

entries.caption: Living Will Expanded Spells
rows: 1st
{@spell command}
2nd
{@spell Sense Quarry|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, {@spell spiritual weapon}
3rd
{@spell sending}, {@spell tongues}
4th
{@spell Binding Chains|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, {@spell locate creature}
5th
{@spell geas}, {@spell scrying}

entries.name: Will of the Prescript
entries: {@i "The Index finger points; as does the Prescript that indicates the path we must tread."}

The Living Will is a patron who always unavoidably contacts you, immersing you in orders to be fulfilled for your continued existence and grace. The form of contact may differ, from simply appearing as a paper slip in your pocket to having another such follower of the Will approaching you to deliver a message.

At the start of a combat or at the start of your next turn whenever there isn't a target of a Will's Paper Slip, a random hostile creature who has rolled Initiative becomes the target of the effect. To do so, roll an appropriate sided die to the amount of creatures around you, using the dice that matches double the value of creatures if it is only two or an odd number of creatures, then halving the result ( adding one on an odd result ), such as if there are only three creatures you roll a d6 and on a result of 3, you attack the second hostile creature in Initiative.

The Will's Paper Slip effect has four ranks which increase whenever certain conditions are met, starting at 1 and being reset after you or its current target are killed or knocked Unconscious. Whenever advancing the ranks of this Effect, your attacks surge with the Living Will's power, granting bonus effects when triggered. For these effects and how to advance ranks, see the following table:

entries.caption: Will's Paper Slip
rows: I

Roll a d4 when the Paper Slip is first drawn, with 1 being Bludgeoning, 2 being Slashing and 3 being Piercing. 4 is any other damage type. Ascend this Slip whenever you deal damage to the target according to the result.
You inflict double your proficiency bonus in additional damage and double your Sinking count on a hit.
II
Ascend this Slip whenever you deal damage to the target three times after first reaching Rank II.
You gain one Grace of the Prescript until the end of combat and two Poise count.
III
Ascend this Slip whenever you hit the target with a Warlock spell or have them fail one of your Spell Saving Throws. Cantrips do not count toward this ascension.
On ascending past this rank, the target suffers triple the amount of Sinking that would usually be dealt on a hit. You gain the same value in Poise count.
IV

This Slip cannot be ascended. Kill the target or knock them Unconscious to trigger the following effect. If you are fighting against a single stronger target ( Such as a boss, as per the DM's choice ) you trigger this effect whenever it loses more than a fourth of its maximum hit points, rounded down. If this effect is triggered in this way, this Slip reverts to rank I.
You gain two counts of Grace of the Prescript until your next short or long rest.

entries: In addition to that, you always deal an additional amount of damage equal to your proficiency bonus and half that value (rounded down) in Sinking count to targets afflicted by the Will's Paper Slip. The effects of the above table are only triggered upon an ascension (except of fourth rank) and do not stack.

If you are knocked Unconscious while another creature is the target of the Will's Paper Slip effect, you suffer one count of Karmic Consequences. You also suffer one count of the effect if combat ends while a creature is suffering from the Will's Paper Slip or if they are killed by another non-friendly creature.
{@i "The index finger points; as does the Prescript that indicates the path we must tread. That is what gives the Index its name."}

entries.name: Follower of an Order
entries: {@i "It is said that the Will of the Prescript and the Will of the City are one and the same."}

Regardless of the presence of combat or not, the Will always communicates something for you to perform every single day, so that its whims are set in motion even if you cannot understand. Once per long rest you roll a d100, receiving a Prescript in accordance to the result, a small slip of paper containing a set of orders to follow. These Prescripts may be found at the end of this document.

When complete, you gain one Devotion point, which may be spent to re-roll any roll performed by you or a friendly creature. You may have up to half your proficiency bonus' worth of Devotion points at any given time. You may spend Devotion after any die are rolled, but before its consequences.

You may also spend a Devotion point to have an item of common rarity appear within an unoccupied space in a 30-ft. radius of yourself. This is a result of another follower's dedication to the Will that has set up this item for your use.
If not complete until your next long rest, you suffer a count ofKarmic Consequences.

subclassFeature.name: Woven Blessings
entries: {@i "Hmm. Refraction of light through a polygonal mirror... This cannot be an appropriate interpretation of the Prescript to 'split the lights.'"}

You are granted a special cloak to wear over your armor and garbs as a reward for your dutiful devotion to the Will. You have a piece of Prescript-Woven Fabric, which grants you an amount of Temporary Hit Points equal to your Warlock level times two plus your proficiency bonus. Whenever these Temporary Hit Points would be reduced, you may spend your Reaction to reduce the damage you would take by 1d8, and an additional 1d8 after reaching 16th level in Warlock.

While these Temporary Hit Points remain, you gain an additional two of them whenever you gain a count of Grace of the Prescript, but are instantly reduced by two whenever you gain a count of Karmic Consequences.
If lost or broken through your Temporary Hit Points reaching zero, you magically gain another piece of Prescript-Woven Fabric during a long rest.

subclassFeature.name: Locked Potential
entries: {@i "As the Prescript commands-my blade strikes."}

The Living Will has graced you with presence beyond direct communication, permeating your arms and weapons to fully envelop you as an instrument of your whims. After you have spent all your Warlock spell slots and if you've spent them without casting any given spell more than once since your last short rest, you enter a Blade Unlocked state until your next short rest. While in this state, gain the following:

items: Whenever you would deal damage through melee attacks, you may choose to have its type be force damage instead of its original type.
Any Cantrips you use deal additional damage to hostile targets equal to half your Warlock level, rounded down. While in this state, they count toward ascending from the Will's Paper Slip III.

At the start of your turns, roll a d4 as of the Will's Paper Slip I effect. You gain a +2 bonus modifier to hit until the end of your turn, as long as the attack would deal the resulting type of damage.

subclassFeature.name: Unerring Undertaker, Unavoidable
