entries: {@i "A new Prescript has arrived: 'Behead seven dwellers of the Backstreets who resist when a blade touches their throat.' The tally aligns-seven of you stand before me. I shall commence."}
While in your Blade Unlocked state, you gain additional effects, as per the following:

items: Once per short or long rest, when first entering theBlade Unlocked state you regain all your Warlock spell slots, except these may only be used to cast your Living Will Pact Spells and to fuel the following abilities:

items.name: Castigation
entries: You may spend your Action and one Warlock spell slot to empower your weapon to its limits, punishing those who defy the Will's action through you. You instantly perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach, dealing 4d12 piercing damage on a hit and dealing additional piercing damage equal to the sum of Sinking count on the target with your current Poise count times two. The target's AC is reduced by 5 for this attack.

items.name: Decapitation
entries: You may spend your Action and one Warlock spell slot to momentarily sever another's soul from their body, shattering it with a force that governs the world around you. You perform a melee weapon attack against a target within reach, dealing 5d8 slashing damage on a hit and causing the target to suffer a further 4d6 force damage at the start of their next turn alongside having them deal only half of any damage they would deal in any attack, spell or otherwise until the end of their next turn.

items.name: Eradication
entries: You may spend your Action and one Warlock spell slot to channel the Will directly, creating a number of mechanical arms that swing down from the heavens to crush any creature of a choice within 120-ft. of you. Any target within reach must pass a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell Save DC, suffering 6d10 bludgeoning damage and being knocked Prone on a failure or only suffering half that damage on a success.

condition.name: Butterfly
entries: {@i "Long ago, people believed that they would become beautiful beings with small wings when they died."}

A creature suffering from Butterfly is suffering two-fold, having a deep-seated lament cocoon around their heart and a grief for the departed flutter out as a pain that can hardly be avoided. For the sake of ease, the Butterfly Condition is also spread in two parts, starting out as Butterfly [The Living] when first applied to a creature and then turning into Butterfly [The Departed] at the end of the afflicted's turn.

entries.name: [ The Living ]
entries: Overflowing with lament for those yet to perish, a creature suffering from this Condition suffers an equal amount of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count as it's current Butterfly [The Living] at the end of their turns, then turning any remaining Butterfly [The Living] into Butterfly [The Departed]. {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} gained at the end of a creature's turn this way is applied after being halved as usual.

entries.name: [ The Departed ]
entries: With grief unto death, any attack that inflicts Butterfly against the creatures deals an additional amount of psychic damage equal to half it's current Butterfly [The Departed]. count, to a maximum value equal to the attacker's proficiency bonus. Butterfly [The Departed]. count becomes 0 at the end of the afflicted's turn.

items: You have disadvantage on {@skill Perception} checks, Strength, Dexterity and Constitution saving throws and ranged attacks.
As a bonus action, you can yell at one of your allies to do better, granting them advantage on their next ability check, saving throw or attack roll, your choice

When you hit a creature that is {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burning}, {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Tremoring}, or Both, you deal an additional {@damage 1d6} die of damage of equal damage to your weapon's damage type
You can substitute one of your attacks for a Sezionatura di Cervo.

condition.name: Escalating Duel
entries: The rush of an Escalating Duel is that of a hunt going through its crescendo, building up for a magnificent climax. You gain the following effects according to your current count:

items: {@b 1 Escalating Duel.} You deal an additional 1 damage on melee weapon attacks.

{@b 2 Escalating Duel.} You gain a +1 bonus modifier to hit and deal an additional 2 damage on melee weapon attacks. Additionally, you inflict your choice of a {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on hit.
{@b 3+ Escalating Duel.} You gain a +2 bonus modifier to hit and deal an additional 3 damage on melee weapon attacks.

entries: Additionally, you inflict 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count on hit and may choose to trigger {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the first melee weapon attack you hit during your turn.

condition.name: Eye of Precognition
entries: You have 15 counts of Eye of Precognition. While you have counts of this, you gain the following benefits:

items: Your walking speed increases by 10 feet
Your Armor Class increases by 3

When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

entries: Whenever you hit with an attack, you lose 1 count of Eye of Precognition. Likewise, you lose 3 counts whenever a creature misses an attack against you due to your AC bonus, and 5 counts whenever you take no damage after succeeding on a Dexterity saving throw.
Once you lose all counts of Eye of Precognition, you immediately gain 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition - Overheat|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

After completing a Long Rest, you immediately lose all counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition - Overheat|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} and gain up to 15 counts of Eye of Precognition, ensuring you have that maximum count of the Condition.

condition.name: Eye of Precognition - Overheat
entries: While you have counts of this, you gain the following characteristics:

items: You always roll an additional damage die of the weapon you are attacking with
Your Armor Class decreases by 3
Whenever taking Fire damage, take an additional damage die of the same value as your eye socket burns.

entries: Whenever you hit with an attack, you lose 1 count of Eye of Precognition - Overheat. Likewise, you lose 3 counts whenever a creature hits an attack against you due to your AC decrease, and 3 counts whenever you take additional Fire damage from a hostile source. Once you lose all counts of Eye of Precognition - Overheat, you immediately gain 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

After completing a Long Rest, you immediately lose all counts of Eye of Precognition - Overheat and gain up to 15 counts of {@condition Eye of Precognition|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, ensuring you have that maximum count of the Condition.

condition.name: Game Target
entries: You may choose to make the last creature you attacked on your turn become your Game Target.

When you hit your Game Target with an attack roll, once per turn, you may choose to convert all of their counts of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} into {@condition Tremor - Scorch|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Tremor Scorch}. Furthermore, whenever you apply counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, to your Game Target, they suffer 1 additional count of each applied.

condition.name: Insight
entries: While you have Insight you gain a bonus modifier to unarmed attacks and Intelligence skill checks equal to half of your current count of the Condition. Additionally, you gain a bonus modifier to your Intelligence saving throws and skill checks equal to your current count. You may have a maximum count of the Condition equal to your proficiency bonus.

If you spend Ki to perform an ability that requires you to have a minimum amount of Insight, you lose one count at the end of your turns. Otherwise, your count is reduced by one per minute spent outside of combat.

condition.name: Severed Tendons
entries: A creature suffering from Severed Tendons has had their movement options sliced clean through, reducing their movement speed by 5-ft. per count of the Condition. Furthermore, this debilitation hinders them further the worse it gets, having the creature suffer a cumulative negative modifier to Dexterity skill checks and saving throws for each 2 count.

One count is removed per hour spent without gaining more count or upon recovering any amount of Hit Points. All counts are removed upon being the target of the Restoration or {@spell Greater Restoration} spells.

condition.name: Vengeance Mark
entries: During combat, the enemy that dealt the most damage to you or your allies this round gains a Vengeance Mark. This lasts until the end of the next round, or until you fall {@condition unconscious}. If no enemy has dealt damage this turn, the stack of Vengeance Mark is given to the enemy that last attempted to attack you or an allied creature. If two enemies dealt the same amount of highest damage, the stack of Vengeance Mark goes to the latest enemy that dealt this damage. Outside of combat, whenever someone rolls an ability check to hurt or damage your character or their reputation, they will also gain a point of Vengeance Mark until your next short rest. If combat is initiated right after an instance of this by rolling an initiative check, then the enemy with the highest initiative roll gains Vengeance Mark until the end of the first round of combat.

condition.name: Rhythm
entries: A creature with this Condition has been enraptured by the god-rending melody of your carnage, and can't help but want to partake in it as musician and instrument, dealing and suffering an additional amount of damage equal to your Charisma modifier whenever they deal or suffer damage ( respectively ) equal to your 3 times your Rhythm count that they currently have. Whenever a creature declines receiving Rhythm, they halve the counts of the Condition they currently have, rounded up. Additionally, if a creature with this Condition benefits from your Bardic Inspiration rolls the minimum value rolled is always equal to their current Rhythm count, being increased if it was lower.

A creature with Rhythm gain an additional count whenever they first kill a creature during a round, except for summoned creatures. Additionally, a creature with 3 or more count may spend one count to perform an additional weapon attack or cast an additional spell of 3rd level or lower during their turn.

condition.name: Corpus Ingredients
entries: You, however, do not limit yourself to using your own body as material, also acquiring one Corpus Ingredients count whenever you successfully deal damage to a creature within 15-ft. of you. You have a count limit equal to double your proficiency bonus, and due to a tendency to dutifully spend any leftovers on smaller projects during a short or long rest, you may only have up to your proficiency bonus worth of Corpus Ingredients after such.

condition.name: Nails
entries: A creature suffering from {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Nails} has a number of them embedded in their flesh, drawing out blood and the faith of certain individuals in equal measure. At the end of their turns, a Nailed creature halves their {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Nail} count and gains the same value halved as {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count instead.

{@condition Fanatic|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Fanatical} creatures gain a +1 bonus modifier to attack rolls against Nailed creatures for each 15 {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Nails} they are currently suffering from, to a maximum of +3.

condition.name: Immolation
entries: A creature beset by {@condition Immolation|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} is suffering from the holiest of flames, taking an amount of {@dice d4} radiant damage equal to their current {@condition Immolation|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count at the end of their turns, also halving its total count. When at one {@condition Immolation|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count, it extinguishes at the end of the creature's turn.

condition.name: Haste
entries: A creature that is going through {@condition Haste|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} has a spring to their step, pushing themselves to move faster or are being carried through magical effects to become nimble as the breeze.

This creature gains 5-ft. of additional walking speed and, if already available flying speed for each {@condition Haste|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count they are benefitting from, to a maximum value of 5 times their proficiency bonus plus 5. All count of the Condition is lost at the start of the creature's next turn.

condition.name: Open Wound
entries: A creature suffering from {@condition Open Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} has a recent tear or puncture in their flesh that is still oozing with blood, and although they may not yet feel the pain from sheer adrenaline coursing through their body they already have difficulty in moving.

This creature has their movement speed reduced by 5-ft. per count of the Condition and upon reaching 2 counts, they lose that count and suffer from one count of {@condition Deep Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} instead.

Additionally, whenever a creature with Open, Deep or {@condition Fatal Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} suffers {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, they are converted to {@condition Tremor - Hemorrhage|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count instead. If they were already suffering from any of the two Conditions, their sum is converted as well.

condition.name: Deep Wound
entries: A creature suffering from {@condition Deep Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} has had a deep gash form in their body, great enough to assail them with pain constantly - And one that can be pushed to the edge with ease.

While suffering from the Condition, this creature has their movement speed reduced by 10-ft. and whenever they suffer a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} they also suffer 3 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. A creature suffering from this Condition cannot gain {@condition Open Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} counts.

condition.name: Tremor - Hemorrhage
entries: A creature suffering from {@condition Tremor - Hemorrhage|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} is one that is currently bleeding out from countless cuts that rove and worsen inside their being.

A creature with {@condition Tremor - Hemorrhage|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} counts suffers {@damage 1d4} damage whenever they perform any action ( Each Attack counts as a different Action, also including Bonus Actions and Reactions, but not Free Actions ) and then the Condition's count is reduced by one count. Creatures that have no blood are immune to this effect.

When a creature with {@condition Tremor - Hemorrhage|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} suffers {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} by other means, they take a number of {@damage 1d6} damage equal to the total count of the Condition they are currently suffering from, then losing all remaining counts of the Condition. The Condition is also lost after the creature is knocked {@condition unconscious}. If they are healed to their Maximum Hit Points they instantly lose all counts of the Condition, also losing 2 counts whenever they are healed by any amount of Hit Points.

condition.name: Fatal Wound
entries: A creature suffering from {@condition Fatal Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} isn't long for this world, having a clear and brittle opening to the doorway that leads to their demise.

While suffering from the Condition, this creature has their movement speed reduced by 10-ft. and whenever they suffer a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} they also suffer 6 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. Furthermore, a creature has their minimum Critical Hit threshold increased by one, ex: They suffer a Critical Hit on an attack roll of 19-20. A Critical Hit against them triggers {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and then removes their {@condition Fatal Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} Condition.
A creature suffering from this Condition cannot gain or have any Open or {@condition Deep Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count, which is instantly removed if gained or sustained.

condition.name: Fanatic
entries: Whenever you enter your Rage you may choose to instead enter a state of sheer {@condition Fanatic|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Fanaticism}. While in that stage you have all the features you'd gain by being Raging, alongside the following:

items: Your faith burns brighter than anything, drawing holy wrath down the wounds poked into your foes. You deal an additional {@damage 1d6} radiant damage on and inflict {@condition Immolation|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count equal to the target's {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count on a melee weapon attack hit.

Your blind fanaticism may propel you to do grand things, but it also has you convinced of certain tribulations you simply must suffer entirely. Whenever you would be forced to make a saving throw or ability check, you may roll a {@dice d4}. On an odd result, you gain a bonus modifier equal to your proficiency bonus. On an even result, you get the same value as a negative modifier to the roll. If you are below half your Maximum Hit Points, you must always roll this {@dice d4}.

condition.name: Torn Memory
entries: Whenever you kill a {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} creature you gain {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to your proficiency bonus and one {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count, as the already dissolving mental image of that which you have shattered lingers on in your aim. If you kill or knock a friendly creature {@condition unconscious} you gain one {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, yet you may only gain one count per creature per combat.
During your turn you may spend {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} as a Free Action you may take once per turn for the following:

items: {@b Reload, Then Fire.} By spending one {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} you may perform an additional attack as part of your Attack action during your next turn. This extra attack does not stack. Additionally, any ranged weapons you are wielding are instantly reloaded at the start of your next turn provided you have enough ammunition on your person.

{@b Designated Target Fire.} By spending at least three {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count you may spend your Action to perform a special attack, coating an 15-ft. radius within your weapon's range in a red haze that reeks of lingering sweat and charred hair. All creatures of your choice within that radius must pass a Dexterity saving throw or suffer an amount of d10 piercing damage and a sum of 2 {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the amount of {@condition Torn Memory|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} spent. Creatures who succeed take half that damage and count instead. Afterward you gain one {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count for each creature damaged through this, with an additional 8 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count if you have killed your {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} creature through this attack. These 8 count do not count toward your turn limit. You cannot gain an amount of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} in a single turn greater than double your proficiency bonus through this way.

condition.name: Stigmatized
entries: At the start of your turns you may choose to have a creature become {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, the centre of your everlasting hatred. You may only do so provided there is no creature already {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, or you can use your Bonus Action to switch the victim of your Stigma.

condition.name: Concussion
entries: A creature suffering form a {@condition Concussion|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} has their senses flare up as if a worm was crawling and rattling the inside of their head, making any further breaks all the more painful. While suffering this Condition, they suffer the following:

items: Whenever the effects of {@condition Rupture|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} are triggered, they count as if the triggering creature's Proficiency Bonus was its actual value plus one.
Whenever {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} is triggered, the damage die dealt are one step greater, such as d4s instead being d6s.
The afflicted creature loses one count of {@condition Concussion|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} at the end of their turns.

condition.name: Pink Petals
entries: A creature affected by Pink Petals feels their body become covered in greenish roots feeding petals that weigh down on their soul. They gain the following downsides:

items: For every 5 counts, take 1 extra point of cold damage from attacks that either deal cold damage or inflict counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
If you have 5 counts of this, gain an additional count of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} whenever you suffer it.
When suffering a {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, take additional {@damage 1d4} psychic damage equal to half the proficiency bonus of the attacking creature.

entries: A creature can only have a maximum of 15 counts of Pink Petals. They lose 1 count of it at the end of their turn.

condition.name: Pheromone
entries: A creature affected by Pheromone lets out a citric smell that infuriates nearby creatures. They gain the following characteristics:

items: Any creature within 15 feet of you who targets a creature other than yourself with a melee attack must first make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or your Bee Save DC (DC = 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Constitution modifier), your choice. On a failed save, the creature chooses you as the target or loses the attack.
Whenever you are hit by a melee attack, the attacker suffers 3 counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries: A creature loses Pheromone at the end of combat or after 1 minute has passed while not in combat.

condition.name: Pheromone Mark
entries: A creature Marked by Pheromones is much more susceptible to being hurt by fire. For each 3 counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} that they have, they take an additional {@damage 1d4} fire damage once per turn when attacked, to a maximum of {@damage 3d4}. They lose Pheromone Mark at the end of their turn.

condition.name: Fragility
entries: A Fragilized creature feels their interiors becoming brittle, and any blow could easily break them as the weakness sinks in, rendering attacks much more effective against them. A creature suffering from Fragility has the next damage type they take considered as if their resistance was one step down, with immunities becoming resistance, resistance becoming normal, and normal becoming a vulnerability. After taking damage like this, one count of Fragility is removed.

condition.name: Hyped-Up
entries: A creature that is Hyped-Up is in a musical frenzy, hitting extremely hard, but being hit just as hard in return, You gain the following characteristics:

items: Whenever you hit a creature with an attack, you deal an additional {@damage 2d4} psychic damage for each count of Hyped-Up you have.
Whenever you are hit by an attack, you must roll a {@dice d20}. On a roll of 5 or lower, you become {@condition Stunned} until the start of your next turn.

entries: You lose all counts of Hyped-Up at the start of your next turn. A creature cannot have more than 3 counts of Hyped-Up at once.

condition.name: Desperado
entries: A creature with Desperado knows that their resources are coming to an end and will not go down without a fight. You gain the following characteristics:

items: Any ranged attack that spends Ammunition deals an additional {@damage 1d10} Piercing damage.

You gain the Evasion ability. If you already have it, then when you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Wisdom saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail.

entries: A creature loses all counts of Desperado at the start of their next turn.

condition.name: Target of the Prescript
entries: A creature who is the The Prescript's Target will soon feel the Living Will fall upon them.

Whenever a Target is dealt damage by a character that is aligned with the Will, such as a Living Will Warlock or Procuration Paladin, they suffer half their attacker's Proficiency Bonus in {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count and the attacker may once per turn re-roll one of their damage die, taking the new result.
Other Conditions such as Will's Paper Slip also count as The Prescript's Target to any creature that isn't already benefiting from the equivalent Condition.

condition.name: Grace of the Prescript
entries: The blessings of the Living Will course through your veins like oxygen through your lungs, empowering your every movement and granting you a closer sense toward enlighten. You gain the following:

items: You gain a bonus modifier to your Attack Rolls and Saving Throws equal to half the count of Grace you currently have ( rounded down ).
You gain an amount of {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to the count of this effect at the start of your turns, with this value remaining until the end of your turn.

entries: This effect ends whenever you are knocked {@condition Unconscious}. You lose one count of Grace of the Prescript whenever you suffer {@condition Karmic Consequences|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. You may have 9 maximum counts of Grace.

condition.name: Karmic Consequences
entries: As negative Karma builds up from your inaction and disregard for what must be done, a crippling force presses down on your soul, slowly bringing you to nothingness. You suffer the following effects according to how many Karmic Consequences you are suffering from:

rows: You have disadvantage on Ability Checks.
You have disadvantage on Attack Rolls and Saving Throws.
Your maximum hit points are halved.
You are instantly knocked {@condition Unconscious}. This Condition lasts until your next short rest.

entries: Your Karmic Consequences count is reduced by one upon a short or long rest, and is reduced by 3 whenever the {@spell lesser restoration} spell is cast upon you, or reduced by 6 whenever the {@spell greater restoration} is cast upon you.

condition.name: Procuration [Hermes]
entries: This Effect is granted and defined by the To Become a Canvas, Slowly Painted feature of the Fatalism Domain.

condition.name: Sizzling Wound
entries: This state is granted and defined by the Masked Wounds feat.

condition.name: Needle
entries: A creature inflicted with counts of Needle suffers from a unique form of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. When you take slashing damage, gain 2 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and lose 1 count of Needle.
At the end of your turn, you lose 1 count of Needle and gain 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

condition.name: Curse
entries: A creature inflicted with Curse rolls a {@dice 1d4} on the start of their turn, getting one of the following corresponding effects until the start of their next turn:

items: On a 1, the inflicted creature has a −1 on attack rolls and ability checks
On a 2, the inflicted creature has a −1 to their AC.
On a 3, the inflicted creature has a −2 on attack rolls and ability checks.
On a 4, the inflicted creature has a −2 to their AC.

entries: After gaining one of these effects, reduce your Curse count by 1.

condition.name: Moonlit Azure Blade
entries: A creature with counts of Moonlit Azure Blade has honed their precision and instincts during the fight, connected as one with their blade. You gain the following effects:

items: At the start of your turn, you gain {@dice 1d4} Temporary Hit Points. If you have 2 counts, you gain {@dice 1d6} instead, {@dice 1d10} if you have 3, {@dice 1d12} if you have 4, and {@dice 2d6} if you have 5.
If you score a Posture Critical hit or a Critical Hit, you add {@damage 1d8} force damage to the roll. If you have at least 3 counts, it becomes {@damage 2d8} instead.

entries: You lose 1 count of Moonlit Azure Blade at the end of your turn and all counts at the end of combat. You can only have a maximum of 5 counts of Moonlit Azure Blade at once.

condition.name: Thermal Blades
entries: A creature inflicted with the Thermal Blades effect feels their blades have turned into searing hot weapons of burning incision. You gain the following effects:

items: If you hit a creature that has counts of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, gain {@dice 1d4} Temporary Hit Points. This becomes {@dice 1d6} at level 5, {@dice 1d8} at level 11 and {@dice 1d10} at level 17.
Whenever an attack of yours would inflict a count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, inflict the same amount of {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on the target.

entries: You lose 1 count of Thermal Blades at the end of your turn and all counts at the end of combat.

condition.name: Blooming
entries: A Blooming is slowly being overtaken by roots growing around their body and a constant haze clouding their mind. While suffering this Condition, they are under the following effects:

items: Whenever they suffer {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, they suffer an additional count.
Their {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count cannot be reduced under 3 times their Blooming count.

entries: Upon reaching 5 counts of Blooming, the creature must pass a Wisdom saving throw or become Fully Bloomed until the start of your next turn, also losing all Blooming count. On a success they lose half their count instead, rounded up. While under this Condition, they suffer from the following:

items: Their {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count cannot be reduced.

Whenever they suffer damage, they suffer additional psychic damage equal to half their {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, for a maximum value equal to double your proficiency bonus.
The creature is {@condition Stunned} for the duration. After becoming Fully Bloomed, that creature gains Advantage against the effect for the next three turns.

optionalfeature.name: Fighting Style: Sacrifice
entries: As a Reaction when you see a friendly creature within 30 feet of you miss an attack roll, you may immediately use your remaining movement speed to jump towards them and make an attack roll against the creature they tried to hit if it is within reach. If you're successful, you deal damage to both creatures, but an additional {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage to the creature you hit. This damage cannot be diminished or prevented in any way, and they suffer any statuses as normal.

optionalfeature.name: The Disgrace
entries: {@i "I'll be damned before I let you ruin this! Not after toiling like a goddamn dog for decades, climbing up the ranks...!"}

What have you done? You should already know the answer to that question, after all it has been repeated in your head as often as you can recall. There's something you did, of your fault and folly, that has rendered you a complete and utter disgrace to those around you, a shame that would be best left erased. Yet still, your exhausted, spiteful fingers grip onto your remaining life like a starving animal does to its last meal.

This {@variantrule Core Bursts|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Core Burst} is recommended for characters who have screwed up phenomenally and even more-so as that failure being of their on fault. That single event is something that has defined them more than anything else in the past, even more-so if they were someone important before their horrid fall from grace. These are often seem as bitter and arrogant people.
Upon activation of your {@variantrule Core Bursts|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Core Burst}, you gain the following effects:

items: Hatred, spite and bitterness overtake your emotions to create a rage-fueled drive towards all your actions, granting you Immunity to becoming {@condition Frightened} or {@condition Charmed}.

You gain 4 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count at the start of your turns. Whenever you deal damage, you deal an additional amount of damage equal to half your current {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, to a maximum value equal to your proficiency bonus.
Whenever you would inflict {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, you inflict an additional count.

Additionally, the anxiety to re-instate your greatness has you become even quicker on your feet as it grows. Each time an attack hits you, your AC increases by a +1 bonus modifier. You lose this bonus whenever you are missed with an attack.

optionalfeature.name: The Custodian
entries: {@i "Listen. We live in a binary world. The world that is luscious... and the world that is bristly. Are you aware of their differences?"}

Style, force and loyalty are words that radiate through your gait wherever you walk, exhaling a powerful aura that booms through the hearts of others, either shaking them to the core or having them fall under the protection of your beat.

This {@variantrule Core Bursts|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Core Burst} is recommended for characters who are great leaders and bolster both courage and imperativeness toward their fellows, taking care of any under them like a grand family that extends far beyond the bonds of blood. These are driven by and for their groups and factions as the first thing in their world, going to great lengths just to make sure they are happy and safe, also being reasonably vengeful at whoever wrongs them and their kin.
Upon activation of your {@variantrule Core Bursts|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Core Burst}, the following apply:

items: Describe how your presence extends like a bursting melody that has others quake in their boots. When first triggering this Burst, all hostile creatures that can see or hear you within a 360-ft. radius must pass a Charisma saving throw or become {@condition Frightened} of you for the next minute, also being able to retry this saving throw to end the Condition early at the end of their subsequent turns. While Frightened, a creature under this Condition suffers 2 {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count at the start of their turns, losing one count after each ability check, saving throw or attack roll.

You feel a surge of power at your fingertips - Confidence made manifest in pure, raw bravado. You gain unarmed weapons that you are proficient with in the shape of your fists and legs for the duration. These have the Finesse and Mesmerizing properties, dealing {@damage 1d8} bludgeoning damage on a hit. If you already had an Unarmed Strike option, you instead deal an additional {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage on your Unarmed Strike hits.

Your feet are stepping on air when it comes to being near those you care about. As a Bonus Action during your turns you may instantly move upwards to 30-ft. in a single leap, having to end your movement within 5-ft. of a friendly creature within that reach. If you are to occupy the same space as a hostile creature you may attempt a Shove attempt against them as part of the same Bonus Action, pushing them 5-ft. toward any direction and taking their space on a success or being forced to land within 5-ft. of that creature on a failure.

Whenever you hit a creature that has {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} with an Unarmed Strike, you deal an additional {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage against them and may choose to instantly push them back 5-ft.

optionalfeature.name: The Ward
entries: {@i "Anyhoo, has anyone here actually read 'The Cloudburst Blade?' If ya did, well... if I may have but 3—no, 4 hours of your time, good sir..."}

To be a ward is to be a waif in your life, you might still be under the graces of your master - your captor - your guardian, whatever they may be to you, and you may still somewhat believe in them but your heart, so carefully forged, has already seen through cracks that you might not be so keen to accept.

This {@variantrule Core Bursts|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Core Burst} is recommended for characters that are living a dichotomy of being attached to a reality that they hold immense fervour toward, but also having that reality being no more than a farce that could break under their feet at any moment. They are those who possess immense knowledge of specific topics but may seem sheltered to the outside world or have trouble accepting certain truths no matter how hard they stare them in the eye.
Upon activation of your {@variantrule Core Bursts|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Core Burst}, you gain the following:

items: The sheer energy pent up in you bursts out like a fire, granting you an additional 10-ft. of movement speed and having all your weapon or spell attacks inflict an additional 2 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

Your fervour is a dual-edged blade, both blinding you to what would leave most quaking but also obfuscating certain alluring dangers. You are Immune to being Frightened but suffer Disadvantage on saving throws against being Charmed.

You gain proficiency in the {@skill History} skill, or Expertise if you were already proficient. You and your DM may discuss a topic of particular interest to your character when first taking this Core Burst, then gaining Advantage on {@skill History} skill checks related to this interest after it is agreed by you and the DM. Additionally, you gain one of the following depending on your current relation to your guardian or symbol of affection:

{@b House of Glass Dreams.} If your relationship is of admiration or an otherwise positive outlook to this false idol, whenever you perform a Critical Hit or have success in a skill check or saving throw within sight of your idol, they may spend their Reaction to Praise you. When they do so, you may add a {@dice 1d8} bonus modifier to one roll of your choice until the end of your next turn and may only do so before you roll.

{@b House of Scattered Hopes.} If your relationship has been broken or is otherwise negative to this false idol, you suffer a {@dice 1d6} negative modifier to all rolls while you can see them within 160-ft. of you as a powerful heartache easily overtakes you. However, after this pain your broken hopes can still be picked up and become stronger through your turmoil. Whenever you have a Critical Success or have success in a skill check or saving throw you gain Confidence. You may spend one Confidence after you roll any of the aforementioned rolls to add an additional {@dice 1d6} to the final result, and may hold up to three Confidence count, which is only reset after a short or long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Passion
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, you inflict 1 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. Additionally, you gain advantage on {@skill Performance} checks whenever performing with ( or to impress ) other friendly creatures or against a hostile creature.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Skull Bursting
entries: Whenever you hit a Grappled creature you may choose to suplex them and cause them to become {@condition Prone}. When you do so, for the remainder of the duration this creature remains {@condition Prone} you may choose to re-roll any damage die against them, taking the greater result. You may do so once per die.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Needle Fractures
entries: You can sink the ink in this tattoo to create binding points in your muscles that take out the force of whatever hits you as a Reaction you may take whenever you suffer damage. When you do so, reduce the damage taken by your choice between your current amount of tattoos or proficiency bonus. You cannot reduce force damage this way and may use this tattoo an amount of times equal to your proficiency bonus, regaining spent uses after a short or long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Vicious Burns
entries: You learn the {@spell vicious mockery} spell. Whenever you causa damage to another creature using it, you may choose to fire damage instead of psychic and one {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} for each damage die rolled. If you are not a spellcaster your DC for this spell's saving throw is 10 + your Charisma modifier + your proficiency bonus + any bonuses gained from being Attuned to a magical weapon.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Turtle Skin
entries: You may spend your Bonus Action to have the ink from this tattoo spread out and flow over your skin, creating a protective layer over it. As long as you aren't wearing armor or are wearing a Tattoo Set armor, you gain a bonus modifier to your AC equal to half your current magical Tattoo count until the start of your next turn. For each attack performed against you in that duration this modifier is reduced by one. You may use this tattoo an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, regaining spent uses after a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Mutual Discombobulation
entries: Once per turn you may choose to change one of your attacks as part of the Attack Action with a Headbutt. To do so you perform a melee Unarmed Strike that you are proficient in against a creature within 5-ft. of you. On a hit, you deal {@damage 2d10} bludgeoning damage and inflict half your proficiency bonus' worth of {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, then suffering half the damage dealt yourself and the same amount of the Condition's count. When you gain it this way, you only lose this count at the end of your next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Entrenched Ankles
entries: You gain 10-ft. move speed. Whenever you attempt to climb a surface, you can spend up to 10-ft. of walking speed at a time to successfully climb the same amount of feet spent by kicking and locking your feet into the surface, remaining there without falling at the end of your turns.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Threadmarks
entries: As an Action during your turn you may brace yourself for a violent sprint. When you do so, you gain 30-ft. of walking speed until the end of your turn and any damage dealt to you through Opportunity Attacks is halved. Whenever you move through another creature's space they must pass a Dexterity saving throw or be caught in your wild trample, being knocked {@condition Prone} on a failure and suffering an amount of d10 bludgeoning damage equal to your proficiency bonus, or half that value on a success. The DC for this is 8 + your Strength modifier + your proficiency bonus. When you do so you may choose to Grapple up to your Strength modifier's worth of creatures instead of Knocking them {@condition Prone}, then knocking them {@condition Prone} in a pile onto of any unoccupied space within 5-ft. of you at the end of your turn. You may use this ability an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, regaining spent uses after a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of an Thunderstorm
entries: Whenever you would be forced to attempt a Dexterity saving throw to resist the effects of a spell or attack that affects a radius, line or sphere that has a physical form ( Such as a {@spell fireball|PHB|Fireball}, {@spell lightning bolt|PHB|Lightning Bolt}, Ballista Bolt or Cannonball ) and pass, you may spend your Reaction to suffer no damage if you would take half and punch through the attack, redirecting it to instead hit another point of your choice within 60-ft. of you. When you do so, all creatures within this new area must attempt the same saving throw against the original DC. You may use this ability an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus, regaining spent uses after a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Tattoo of Starburst
entries: Whenever you deal a Critical Hit against a target creature, you deal an additional 2 damage die equal to the attack's current damage. Additionally, you inflict an amount of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Immobilized|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count against the hit creature equal to the amount of damage die rolled and when you perform this your fists burst into bright-light that covers an 30-ft. area around you. All hostile creatures within that reach must then pass a Constitution saving throw or be Blinded until the end of their next turn.

optionalfeature.name: Relocator Fighting Style
entries: Wielding certain weapons that are a menace from afar has become second nature to you, and you have learnt how to better grip and shove all on your way to shape the battlefield to your liking. Whenever you hit with a weapon that has the Reach property, you may move the target up to 5-ft. closer to you if they were within 10-ft. of you or push them away if they were within 5-ft. of you.

optionalfeature.name: Headshot Focus Fighting Style
entries: You are particular with where you aim your weaponry, focusing for a quick and clean kill whenever able. Whenever you target a creature that has a head with a ranged weapon attack, you may choose to Aim For the Head. When you do so, the following applies:

items: The Target's Armor Class is increased by their proficiency bonus.
You cannot hit the target unless you beat their AC, regardless of scoring a Critical Hit.
If you would Critically Hit yet miss the targets AC, you still roll damage, dealing half that amount as your shot grazes them.
You Critically Hit on this attack with a Critical Threshold reduced by 2, such as rolling an 18-20 on your dice, before any modifiers.

optionalfeature.name: The Veteran
entries: {@i "Thanks to that, I'm free to point the barrel at anyone I want. No matter where I fire it, this shotgun can blast anyone into fireworks like it hit them point blank, how wonderful is that?"}

Your life has been a warpath going from battle to battle, conflict to conflict. This might not be in the case of a literal war, but instead of various minor conflicts that have led you along to be hardened by them, granting you an askew view of your surroundings and the people that walk near you.

This Core Burst is recommended for characters who have been put through conflict for most of their lives be that by their own volition or otherwise. They are often found lurking over memories of their own path or attempting not to overlap their sights with something that isn't really there, but vary wildly in how they cope with their experiences.
Upon activation of your Core Burst, you gain the following effects:

items: You gain Resistance to psychic damage and the Frightened Condition.
You gain {@dice 1d4+1} Poise count at the start of your turns.
You gain Advantage on ability checks and saving throws against being Grappled or Blinded.
You are considered Proficient in the {@skill Athletics} skill if you weren't, and to have Expertise in said skill if you were.

entries: Additionally, choose one of the following to determine which feature you gain based on your own personality traits. If you see people still as a precious thing and value life greatly, gain this:

items: Whenever a friendly creature that you can see within 120-ft. of you is healed or protected by another creature, such as per the Protection Fighting Style, you gain Hope For Your Fellows until the end of your next turn. While clinging onto this Hope, you may reduce any damage you suffer by two die that equal double your proficiency bonus. ( Such as a +2 being 2d4, +3 being 2d6 and so on. ) Additionally you may, as a Free Action at the start of your turns, pass this Hope and its effects to a friendly creature within the same reach as first described.

entries: If you see people as resources to be spent toward your goal, gain this:

items: Whenever a friendly creature that you can see within 120-ft. of you suffers damage for the first time in the round, you gain one Poise count. Whenever a friendly creature within that same reach dies or first falls Unconscious during this combat, you gain Woe For Your Foes until the end of your next turn. While clinging into this Despair you may choose to re-roll once any individual damage die you roll on weapon attacks after first rolling them, having to take that result.

entries: And finally, if apathy towards life is all that fills you, gain this:

items: You may spend your Reaction when suffering damage to reduce your damage taken by a value equal to your current Poise count plus your proficiency bonus, as you only try to thread forward in the never-stopping march of life.

entries.name: Designer's Note
entries: For more information on Core Bursts, see the Fatalist Domain cleric.

optionalfeature.name: Scattering Aroma
entries: {@b Cost: 2 Sorcery Points.} As a Reaction to when you would be targeted for an attack, you may use your own magic to momentarily disperse the thoughts of your attacker, imposing Disadvantage on the attack. You may so after the creature rolls to hit but before the DM determines the result.

optionalfeature.name: Spreading Floral Breeze
entries: {@b Cost: 1-4 Points.} As a Free Action during your turn you may have your magic solidify roots sprouting from your shoulders or around your back that mimic your hands, acting in unison to deliver more at once. Your next weapon attack or cantrip spell attack until the end of your turn may target an additional different target for each Sorcery Point spent, provided the targets are still within reach.
If the cantrip you would cast can already target multiple targets, you just choose one more target for each Sorcery Point spent.

If you would deal additional damage with sources such as Divine Smite, that additional damage is divided evenly toward all targets, rounded down and with a minimum of one die or value of extra damage.
{@b Ex:} If you would deal an additional {@damage 5d8} fire damage from a magic weapon against four creatures, each suffers only an additional {@damage 2d8} fire damage.

optionalfeature.name: The Fatebound
entries: {@i "It must've been fate that brought us together. To think that I'd ever meet a husband like you..."}
Your heart beats to the tune of the fates, scattered to the waves until it stops. Even though volatile, you always make sure that when you crash, it will be glorious.

This Core Burst is recommended for characters who are marked by a certain detachment with everything else, those with a turbulent attitude toward their goals or characters who are ultimately fatalists.
Upon activation of your Core Burst, you gain the following in accordance to your current missing Hit Points:

items: While you are below half your Maximum Hit Points, deal an additional d6 damage whenever you damage a creature. This damage is of the same type as your original attack.
While below half of your Maximum Hit Points currently missing, gain a +1 bonus modifier to hit on your attack rolls. While below a quarter, gain a +2 instead.
Whenever you would gain {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count, gain two additional counts of the effect.
Once per turn per creature, whenever you deal damage to a creature suffering from being {@condition Frightened} or {@condition Charmed} and you aren't, deal an additional 2d4 psychic damage as well.

optionalfeature.name: The Truthseeker
entries: {@i "Even if I don't have much happiness, I know where to go in the immediate future. And that's enough for me."}

You have always bene ticked off by the small rips at the seams of the world and the thoughts of what might move in the shadows. You may not always know how or why, but your heart yearns to understand the world and its many meanings.

This Core Burst is recommended for characters who just can't stand still when they've got the feeling that something is off, those with great intuition and those inclined to try to face the truth even if they may not be able to withstand it fully.
Upon activation of your Core Burst, you gain the following effects:

items: You gain Advantage on {@skill Perception} and {@skill Insight} checks.
You gain Advantage against resisting and perceiving Illusions of any kind, you also gain Advantage against Enchantment spells.
While you are above half your Maximum Hit Points, all damage you suffer is reduced by 1d4 as you feel like you can handle any erosion from seeing what you shouldn't.

While you are at or below half your Maximum Hit Points you feel the weight in your mind start to become heavy, yet a supernatural focus has been unlocked in your being. You suffer a −2 negative modifier on Wisdom and Charisma saving throws, but gain 2 {@condition Poise|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} at the start of your turns and whenever you trigger a Posture Critical, that damage cannot be reduced through any means.

optionalfeature.name: The Shackled

prerequisite.other: A Wisdom score of 18 or lesser

entries: {@i "I... I have to move forward... F-follow the shadow...!"}

You have a profound dependency or love for a particular subject, be that an object or a person. That is what keeps you going through anything so you can keep its safety and possible happiness guaranteed at any cost.

This Core Burst is recommended for characters that have developed a deep and ( although not always ) unhealthy obsession with something or someone, those who would split the word in two to complete what is requested for them or characters who are ultimately seeking some form of validation or to have others be proud of them.
Upon activation of your Core Burst, you gain the following effects:

items: Name a creature or object as your Desire when first activating your Burst. Whenever they suffer damage or are grabbed by another creature ( respectively ), you gain a cumulative +1 bonus modifier to hit and to damage on your next attack against the creature who harmed your Desire. This bonus is reset after dealing damage to them.

While your Desire is {@condition Unconscious} ( if it is a creature ) or is within a hostile creature's possession ( if it is an object ), you deal an additional 1d8 damage when dealing any damage while being within 15-ft of your Desire.
You gain a bonus modifier to your AC equal to half your proficiency bonus while within 15-ft. of your Desire.

You are permanently under the effects of the {@spell guidance} cantrip when tasked by your Desire ( if they are a creature ) to attempt something that would require a Skill Check or while using your Desire. ( if they are an object. )

entries: If your Desire is an object, you and your DM must agree that it is important enough for you to value it greatly. That item can be a weapon that has accompanied you through your journey and that has the possibility of being pried away from you, or a memento that keeps you steady through the hardest of times, such as a carved totem that reminds you of home or something of the sort.

optionalfeature.name: Random Targetting
entries: Sometimes an ability or feature may ask you to choose a random creature. To do so, refer to an order of the possible creatures to be chosen ( Such as groupings of hostile or friendly creatures, also making preferential use of the Initiative order if in combat ) and rolling an appropriate die for the number of creatures.

For a two or three creatures, simply roll a d4 or d6 respectively, with each creature having a "weight" of 2 on the roll, such as when rolling a d6 on a result of 1–2 creature A gets picked, while 3–4 would be creature B and a 5–6 results in creature C.

For creatures greater than that in an even number, simply roll an appropriate die, such as a d4 for 4 creatures, d6 for 6 and so on. In the case of odd creatures, roll the closest die rounded up, such as rolling a d8 if there are 7 creatures to be chosen. If the result is an unassigned number, simply re-roll until the result is a listed creature, or pick the last creature in order if this is repeated more than twice.

optionalfeature.name: Nailing Scissors
entries: Whenever you hit an attack roll with your scrap scissors, the target suffers 2 counts of {@condition Nails|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. This count increases to 3 upon reaching level 9.

optionalfeature.name: Cursed Scissors
entries: Whenever you hit an attack roll with your scrap scissors, the target suffers 1 count of {@condition Curse|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. This count increases to 2 upon reaching level 9.

optionalfeature.name: Pinstack Scissors
entries: Whenever you hit an attack roll with your scrap scissors, the target suffers 2 counts of {@condition Needle|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

optionalfeature.name: Sharper Scissors
entries: Your Scrap Scissors deal an additional {@damage 1d8} slashing damage. This damage increases to {@damage 2d8} upon reaching level 9. If the Scrap Scissors are being held with two hands, the d8 becomes a d10 instead.

optionalfeature.name: Pushing Scissors
entries: After you hit a creature with your Scrap Scissors, they must succeed on a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC or be pushed 5 feet back. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Frightening Scissors
entries: After hitting a creature with your Scrap Scissors, you can force them to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC, or become {@condition frightened} of you for 1 turn. A creature affected by this can repeat their saving throws at the end of each of their turns, ending the effect on a success. You can use this ability a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and you regain all expended uses on a long rest.

optionalfeature.name: Molar Scissors
entries: Instead of attacking a creature, you may choose to grapple them with your Scrap Scissors instead. You may choose to perform an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) ability check instead of a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) ability check for the grapple, and you may perform the ability check with advantage.

optionalfeature.name: Divided Scissors
entries: Your Scrap Scissors can now be split into two separate blades for each hand. When separate, they each count as a {@item handaxe|PHB} you are proficient with, with the exception that they also have the finesse property. You may unite or separate them as a free action.

optionalfeature.name: Bleeding Scissors
entries: Whenever you apply counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} with your Scrap Scissors, you apply that many counts + 2 instead. Additionally, friendly creatures within 5 feet of you apply 1 additional {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count when they hit a creature with a melee attack.

optionalfeature.name: Critical Scissors
entries: Your attack rolls with your Scrap Scissors can score a critical hit on a roll of 18–20.

optionalfeature.name: Preserving Scissors
entries: Your attack rolls with your Scrap Scissors do not remove counts of {@condition Needle|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} from affected creatures.

optionalfeature.name: Aiding Scissors
entries: After you hit a creature with your Scrap Scissors, the next attack that targets them has advantage.

optionalfeature.name: Powerful Scissors
entries: Your Scrap Scissors gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with it.

optionalfeature.name: Wounding Scissors
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with your Scrap Scissors and the attack deals more than half their hit points in damage, or was a critical hit, you may roll on the Lingering Injuries table to cause a wound on them.

optionalfeature.name: Singleton
entries: A spell may have a part of its text contain the "Singleton." keyword. This signifies that the spell has a special benefit to the first time it is cast until your next long rest, with this effect being written following the "Singleton." keyword itself If you cast multiple "Singleton." spells within the same long rest, their special effects trigger once per each individual spell.

item.name: First Seal Removed: Lævateinn
entries: A legendary sword acquired very deep underground after defeating a deadly guardian. Not everyone can wield it, and even less can unlock its full powers.

While attuned to it, you have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and you gain the following characteristics (if any of them require a save DC, it is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier):

entries.name: Burning Hot
entries: You gain Resistance to Fire damage.

entries.name: Follow-Up Attack
entries: Whenever you take the Attack action, you may use a Bonus Action to attack an additional time, but you don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative, and you don't inflict any Conditions.

entries.name: Wounding Inferno
entries: The first time you hit a creature with this weapon, they suffer 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} and {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}, your choice.

entries.name: Slam Them Down
entries: You can use an Action to slam your sword into the ground, turning a 10-foot area around you into Difficult Terrain. All creatures within that area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 3d6} bludgeoning damage and fall {@condition Prone}. On a successful save, they only take half that damage and suffer no additional effects.

entries.name: Looks Like I Gotta Unbox the Second Layer, too.
entries: Upon reaching level 10 in the Vengeance Fighter class or being a worthy wielder of the sword, this Greatsword becomes able to turn into {@item Second Seal Removed: Lævateinn|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. To do so, upon hitting a creature with an attack, you may choose to unseal the sword and release the casing on top of them. They must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 2d8} bludgeoning damage and become {@condition Frightened} until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects.

item.name: Lævateinn
entries: A legendary sword acquired very deep underground after defeating a deadly guardian. Not everyone can wield it, and even less can unlock its full powers.

While attuned to it, you have a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, as well as an extra {@damage 2d6} Fire damage. You also gain the following characteristics (if any of them require a save DC, it is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier):

entries.name: Scorching Hot
entries: You gain Immunity to Fire damage.

entries.name: Armor of the Fire Giant
entries: As a Bonus Action, for 1 minute you gain a +1 bonus to your Armor Class. Additionally, whenever a creature hits you with an attack roll, they take {@damage 1d8} Fire damage. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Follow-Up Attack
entries: Whenever you take the Attack action, you may use a Bonus Action to attack an additional time, but you don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative, and you don't inflict any Conditions.

entries.name: Wounding Inferno
entries: Whenever you hit a creature with this weapon, they suffer 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries.name: Melt Away and Die
entries: On a Critical Hit with this weapon, the target creature's skin blackens like charcoal, their veins glowing orange like lava. For the next minute, they suffer a {@dice 1d8} penalty on all ability checks and saving throws. If you score another Critical hit against the same creature, no matter when, they must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or be immediately killed, their body melting away into nothing.

entries.name: Slam Them Down
entries: You can use an Action to slam your sword into the ground, turning a 20-foot area around you into Difficult Terrain filled with molten lava. All creatures within that area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 8d6} bludgeoning damage and fall {@condition Prone}. On a successful save, they only take half that damage and suffer no additional effects. Any creature other than you that enters the area for the first time on their turn or starts their turn within the area immediately takes {@damage 1d6} Fire damage.

entries.name: Burn Through Any Opposition
entries: As an action, you can touch a nonmagical flammable object with this sword and cause it to ignite. If the object isn't being worn or carried, it is reduced to ash at the end of your turn. Additionally, as an action, you can touch a nonmagical wall, floor, or similar structure and melt a 5-foot cube of it, provided the material can be melted by heat.

item.name: Sealed Lævateinn
entries: A legendary sword acquired very deep underground after defeating a deadly guardian. Not everyone can wield it, and even less can unlock its full powers.
While attuned to it, you gain the following characteristics (if any of them require a save DC, it is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier):

entries.name: Burning Hot
entries: You gain Resistance to Fire damage.

entries.name: Follow-Up Attack
entries: Whenever you take the Attack action, you may use a Bonus Action to attack an additional time, but you don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative, and you don't inflict any Conditions.

On a failed save, they take {@damage 1d6} bludgeoning damage and fall {@condition Prone}. On a successful save, they only take half that damage and suffer no additional effects.

entries.name: Time to Unpack!
entries: Upon reaching level 7 in the Vengeance Fighter class or being a worthy wielder of the sword, this Greatsword becomes able to turn into {@item First Seal Removed: Lævateinn|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. To do so, upon hitting a creature with an attack, you may choose to unseal the sword and release the casing on top of them. They must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 1d8} bludgeoning damage and become {@condition Frightened} until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects.

item.name: Second Seal Removed: Lævateinn
entries: A legendary sword acquired very deep underground after defeating a deadly guardian. Not everyone can wield it, and even less can unlock its full powers.

While attuned to it, you have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, as well as {@damage 1d6} additional Fire damage. You also gain the following characteristics (if any of them require a save DC, it is equal to 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier):

entries.name: Burning Hot
entries: You gain Resistance to Fire damage.

entries: As a Bonus Action, for 1 minute you gain a +1 bonus to your Armor Class. Additionally, whenever a creature hits you with an attack roll, they take {@damage 1d8} Fire damage. Once you use this ability, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Follow-Up Attack
entries: Whenever you take the Attack action, you may use a Bonus Action to attack an additional time, but you don't add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative, and you don't inflict any Conditions.

entries.name: Wounding Inferno
entries: The first time you hit a creature with this weapon, they suffer 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries.name: Slam Them Down
entries: You can use an Action to slam your sword into the ground, turning a 20-foot area around you into Difficult Terrain. All creatures within that area must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 4d6} bludgeoning damage and fall {@condition Prone}. On a successful save, they only take half that damage and suffer no additional effects.

entries.name: Burn Through Any Opposition
entries: As an action, you can touch a nonmagical flammable object with this sword and cause it to ignite. If the object isn't being worn or carried, it is reduced to ash at the end of your turn. Additionally, as an action, you can touch a nonmagical wall, floor, or similar structure and melt a 5-foot cube of it, provided the material can be melted by heat.

entries.name: Unsealed Phenomenon: Lævateinn
entries: Upon reaching level 15 in the Vengeance Fighter class or being a worthy wielder of the sword, this Greatsword becomes able to turn into {@item Lævateinn|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. To do so, upon hitting a creature with an attack, you may choose to unseal the sword and release the casing on top of them. They must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take {@damage 4d8} bludgeoning damage and become {@condition Frightened} until the start of your next turn. On a successful save, they only take half the damage and suffer no additional effects.

item.name: Little Book of Vengeance
entries: Prerequisites: Be part of the Middle through a Subclass, Background or Feat.

This Book of Vengeance is awarded to all Little Brothers and Sisters of the Middle, and is connected to all other Books of Vengeance of the organization. Anything that is written in the book is shared among all Books of Vengeance, and no matter its size, it manages to magically contain every single page of vengeance. You can read its contents as a free action, and your DM will let you know whether there is any mission currently available for you to undertake and exact vengeance for the Middle.

Additionally, you can write down someone's name on the Book of Vengeance, and any other person that carries a Book of Vengeance will be able to read it and hunt that creature to earn the rewards below.
When you complete a quest from the Little Book of Vengeance, you gain the following benefits:

items: Until the next long rest, with every attack that you hit, you deal {@damage 1d4} extra damage of the same type as the attack.
Until the next long rest, you gain advantage on an ability check of your choice.

item.name: Young Book of Vengeance
entries: Prerequisites: Be part of the Middle through a Subclass, Background or Feat.

This Book of Vengeance is awarded to all Young Brothers and Sisters of the Middle, and is connected to all other Books of Vengeance of the organization. Anything that is written in the book is shared among all Books of Vengeance, and no matter its size, it manages to magically contain every single page of vengeance. You can read its contents as a free action, and your DM will let you know whether there is any mission currently available for you to undertake and exact vengeance for the Middle.

Additionally, you can write down someone's name on the Book of Vengeance, and any other person that carries a Book of Vengeance will be able to read it and hunt that creature to earn the rewards below.
When you complete a quest from the Young Book of Vengeance, you gain the following benefits:

items: Until the next long rest, with every attack that you hit, you deal {@damage 1d6} extra damage of the same type as the attack.
Until the next long rest, you gain advantage on two ability checks of your choice.
You gain a single point of Inspiration that can be used until your next Long Rest.

entries: {@note Little siblings usually take easier quests, suited for players from levels 1 - 5. Young siblings take quests from levels 6 - 10, Big siblings take levels 11 - 17 and Great siblings take quests from levels 18 and above.}

item.name: Golden HHair Coupon
entries: This is a golden ticket to utmost lusciousness, separating those with bristly hair from gods in humanoid form. This ticket is glistening gold, resembling the quality of shininess provided to follicles upon its use and has ancient engravings to allow use for any reputable and/or irreputable hair salon, filling the stylist with vigour and granting them the capability to cultivate the mane of dreams even if they wouldn't be able to cut a shrub with their fingers.

This item may be given to any hair stylist over the course of downtime or a long-rest for you to receive a luscious hair cut, consuming the item in the process. Any stylist must pass a DC 30 Wisdom saving throw or be compelled to give you the hair cut for free, as per the ticket demands. This process takes approximately 30 minutes, and afterward your Charisma score increases by 4, to a maximum of 24. Additionally, you permanently gain Proficiency in one Charisma skill of your choice and Expertise in another Charisma skill of your choice.

If you have not the access to a hair stylist at the given moment, you may read upon the faint engraving at this hair coupon's title, which at first seemed like a misprint doubling the "H" is actually fine print for "Haunted", indicating the capability of invoking a stylish poltergeist that will give you the hair cut instead of a living being in exchange for the ticket when it is folded neatly and then cut in two, as part of the phantom's ghastly ritual of utter lavishness.

{@b Cursed: Smells Like Chocolate.} This item is a magnet to be stolen by lowly street dogs, as such any other creature has Advantage on {@skill Stealth} and {@skill Sleight of Hand|Sleight of Hands} to steal this item. When stolen, the thief permanently gains {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, even if they die and are revived. You deal an additional {@damage 1d10} bludgeoning damage on Unarmed Strikes against that creature.

item.name: Sunglasses of Surmountable Style
entries: A pair of golden trimmed and purple lensed sunglasses that radiates stylishness, being one of the few that most people can and should accept to be worn even during night. It is a symbol of class and power within certain families.

{@b Advanced Lusciousness} Your Charisma score becomes 23 while Attuned to this item as long as it was lower than this value. Additionally, if you weren't proficient in the Persuasion or {@skill Intimidation} skills you still add half your proficiency bonus to skill checks of either.

{@b Curricular in Castigation.} Let your heart beat and be beaten in the name of the family. At the start of your turn you may spend a Bonus Action to adjust your sunglasses and let them shine with a challenge to all - kill you or die trying. You gain Vulnerability to all damage types until the start of your next turn. At the start of your next turn and until its end any damage you deal to others has them be considered Vulnerable to that damage type. If you or a creature made Vulnerable this way would have Resistance to a damage type, they only take an amount of damage equal to the normal damage they would take plus half that same damage. If either were Immune to a damage type, they suffer that damage as if they were not Immune instead.
{@b Quality Eye Protection.} You gain Advantage on rolls against effects that would cause you to be blinded. These glasses are just that good.

item.name: Chains of Loyalty
entries: A set of heavy, ostentatious golden chains that are usually rolled up around the wrists and forearms as a symbol of loyalty and the weight of family. To be used they are gripped in the hand and swung like a whip.
If you have any levels in a Middle subclass or the Sibling Background you are considered proficient in this weapon even if you normally wouldn't be.

item.name: Knuckles of Loyalty
entries: A set of heavy golden knuckledusters, housing enough weight to break a face and still retain their luscious shine.
If you have any levels in a Middle subclass or the Sibling Background you are considered proficient in this weapon even if you normally wouldn't be.

item.name: Premium Brand Top Sib's Hair Gel
entries: A premium brand of hair gel that leaves you cool to the touch.

Whenever you hit a friendly creature using this item, you may choose to instead of chucking the bottle full force at their head, having it be a glorious splatter of gel onto their hair. When you do so, you deal no damage and the creature gain a +1 to their Charisma modifier until the end of their next turn.

item.name: Adhesive of Moral Reinforcement
entries: A small sheet of powerfully adorable stickers that can be glued to others to fill them with great happiness.
This sheet holds 5 Stickers that may be spent in the following ways:

items: You may spend a single Sticker to glue it to another creature within 5-ft. of you as a Bonus Action, giving them positive reinforcement and {@dice 1d6} temporary Hit Points. While these Hit Points remain they may once per turn add an additional {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to an ability check, attack roll or saving throw before or after rolling the die, but before the DM determines a result.

You may spend two Stickers at once as an Action to attempt to make another creature within 5-ft. of you find some happiness in their life, instantly causing them to be affected by the {@spell calm emotions} spell with a DC of 10 + your proficiency bonus + your Charisma modifier. Irrelevant to this effect's result, the creature feels a little less sad from being recognized in some way.

You may spend three Stickers at once as an Action to overwhelm another creature within 5-ft. of you with resolve, granting them the effects of the {@spell heroism} spell for the next minute. The temporary Hit Points gained through this are instead {@dice 3d4} temporary Hit Points plus your Charisma modifier.

entries: After its effects, any Stickers glued remain through fire and rain, clinging to belongings like memories. Memories are important, after all.

item.name: Beating Box
entries: An overwhelmingly sturdy boombox that has been attached to a set of golden chains. Its beats are solid, ground-breaking and positively skull-crushing.
Bards are considered Proficient with this weapon.

While used by a Bard, this weapon counts as a musical instrument that may be used for Spellcasting and {@skill Performance} checks. Additionally under the same condition this weapon gains the Splash (1d6) property and may be used to deal thunder damage instead of bludgeoning, as a Bard best knows how to lay a beatdown with sound alone.

item.name: Tattoo Set of Confidence
entries: A set of intricate tattoos that make use of their wearer's confidence to harden muscles to protect the flesh from any damage the user would suffer. These are usually worn with leather or pelt-based clothing onto to further bolster their wearer's confidence in themselves.

This armor is a set of tattoos that glow whenever active, as such it cannot be doffed without specialized means yet may be covered by other clothing or even armor. While wearing armor over a Tattoo Set, you must choose to benefit from the effects of only one of the armors.

Due to the glow of these tattoos you have Disadvantage on {@skill Stealth} checks unless you are proficient in the {@skill Deception} skill or have expertise in the {@skill Stealth} skill, as you are more knowledgeable on how to mask such unnatural lights as a common part of the scenery or obfuscate that glow altogether.
