item.name: Cursed Fireworks
entries: A modified lever-action rifle that acts as a shotgun. However, this modification is only the make-up for a much more devilish change that has been granted to this cursed creation.
You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
{@b A Pact With The Devil.} This weapon's long range does not incur Disadvantage on attacks.

{@b The Power to Tear Open All Sides.} Only one attack may be made using this weapon during your turn. When you do so, all creatures within 5-ft. of the original target are also targeted by the attack. You roll to hit only once and consider that result against the individual AC of each affected creature, also rolling damage only once for all.

{@b Iron sights on a Hazy Heart.} This weapon is cursed to blow up the beloved persons in one's heart. If you are aware of two people who love each other platonically or romantically and deal damage to one while the other can see or hear, the other also suffers half the damage dealt as psychic damage. Whenever you Reload this weapon, if you have a beloved person yourself they suffer {@damage 3d8} piercing damage upon you firing the last bullet in this weapon's magazine. You may choose to otherwise suffer that damage yourself.

item.name: Beak-Shaped Necklace
entries: A mysterious necklace made with small pellets reminiscent of gunpowder bullets and a sharp beak from an unknown bird at the center. Whenever you make a ranged attack that spends ammunition, you gain 5 feet of movement for ammunition spent this way until the start of your next turn. If all attacks you made hit, you gain advantage on ranged attack next turn.
Additionally, your attacks that inflict counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} deal an additional {@damage 1d6} piercing damage.

item.name: Staticky Two-Way Radio
entries: A strange communication device that never seems to reach anyone, it only transmits a buzzing static sound. Whenever you make a ranged attack that spends ammunition, you gain 5 feet of movement for each ammunition spent this way until the start of your next turn. If all attacks you made hit, you gain advantage on your first ranged attack next turn.
Additionally, your attacks that inflict counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} deal an additional {@damage 1d6} cold damage.

item.name: Pink Petals
entries: A vine covered in a bundle of pink petals that produce an aroma which brings with it feelings of melancholy and nostalgia. Whenever you would inflict counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} inflict 1 count of {@condition Pink Petals|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} as well. Inflict 1 additional count of {@condition Pink Petals|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} if the creature already has 5 or more counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

item.name: Still-Warm Coffee
entries: A cup of coffee that never loses its warmth, no matter how many days it spends out in the cold. This item holds no nutritional value, but drinking from it brings a powerful boost. As a bonus action, you can drink from this beverage to give yourself {@dice 1d10} temporary hit points. If you have all of your Hit Points, you also gain advantage on your first attack each turn for 1 minute.
If you drink more than 1 Still-warm Coffee before a Long rest, you suffer 1 point of {@condition Exhaustion} when its effects wear off.

item.name: Royal Jelly Perfume
entries: A strange bottle of perfume made from an extract of monstrous bees. As a Bonus Action, you can spray yourself with the perfume bottle to gain {@condition Pheromone|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, which lasts for 1 minute or until the end of combat if you enter one while it is still active. Whenever a {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules|Burning} enemy hits you, the damage you take from the attack is reduced by {@dice 1d8}.

Additionally, at the end of your turn, the creature that dealt most damage to you during the last round suffers from {@condition Pheromone Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} If no creature dealt damage to you, choose 1 hostile creature at random.

item.name: Harmonics
entries: A strange, bloodied instrument infused with dark magic and put together with scraps of a dark machine. Whenever a creature is knocked {@condition Unconscious} or suffers a Critical Hit, every creature that is not {@condition Deafened} within 30 feet of you suffers 1 count of {@condition Fragility|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

If you or a friendly creature within 30 feet of you applies counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} while there are Fragility creatures within 30 feet of you because of this effect, all friendly creatures within 30 feet of you lose 1 count of {@condition Fragility|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, and the attacked creature suffers an additional 3 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

item.name: Walking Bass
entries: A serrated instrument infused with dark magic and put together with scraps of a dark machine. At the start of your turn in combat, you may choose to gain 1 count of {@condition Hyped-Up|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} as a free action. Whenever you hit a creature with an attack, but before you apply damage, roll a {@dice d20}.

On a roll of 16 or higher, you and 1 random friendly creature within 30 feet of you that isn't {@condition Deafened} gains 1 count of {@condition Hyped-Up|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} If it was an attack that inflicts counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} or {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} it happens on a roll of 11 or higher instead.

entries.name: Curse
entries: You love the sound of your own music too much, so you can't go without listening to it during the chaos of combat. If you spend more than 2 turns without Hyping yourself up, you hear discordant notes inside your mind, taking {@damage 2d6} psychic damage that cannot be reduced in any way.

item.name: Desperado
entries: A skull steel case filled with empty rounds of Ammunition that somehow empower you by their presence alone. You gain 10 feet of movement and a +1 to all Ranged attacks that spend Ammunition, as long as you already don't have a +3 from external sources.

At the start of your turn, if you only have 6 or less pieces of ammunition remaining, gain 1 count of {@condition Desperado|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. At the end of your turn, you can spend a Bonus Action to make an additional Ranged attack against a creature within range as long as you have counts of Desperado Additionally, you always recover all spend Ammunition when searching for it after a fight as long as it wasn't destroyed.

entries.name: Not My First Rodeo
entries: As a Reaction to when a creature moves or uses an Action, Bonus Action or Reaction within reach of one of your ranged weapon attacks, you can immediately make a Ranged attack against them. If it hits, they must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC = 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Dexterity modifier) or become {@condition Stunned} until the end of their next turn. Once you use this ability, you can only do so again after the next dawn if the creature failed the saving throw.

item.name: Pink Bouquet
entries: A magical bouquet of flowers empowered by the energy of a Domain of Pleasure's Spring season. Once per turn, when you hit a creature with a ranged attack, you deal an additional 5 ({@damage 1d10}) piercing damage until the end of your next turn. Whenever you knock a hostile creature unconscious with a ranged attack, you gain an additional 10 feet of movement for 1 minute.

Additionally, whenever a friendly creature within 30 feet of you inflicts counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} on a creature, that creature also suffers 1 count of {@condition Pink Petals|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} the creature is already Sinking they suffer an additional count of {@condition Pink Petals|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} and 1 count of {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.
At the start of your turn, choose a creature within 30 feet of you that is Sinking, they lose 10 feet of movement until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Spring's Genesis
entries: As an Action, all terrain within a 100-foot radius centered on you becomes fertile, and immediately grows patches of grass and pink flowers. If there were already seeds planted on the ground, they germinate immediately and yield fruits.

If you do this in an area already taken over by nature, the plants grow beyond their natural abilities and the area becomes thick and overgrown with plant life, turning into difficult terrain. Any ice or snow present within the area immediately thaws and melts, and any fire burning outside of a container is extinguished.
Once you use this ability, you can only do so again after the next dawn.

item.name: BongBong Orange
entries: This slimy, yet delicious bubble dropped from a verminous creature is extremely healthy and, sadly, addictive. As a Bonus Action, any creature may eat this or feed it to a willing creature. The creature regains {@dice 6d4 + 6} hit points. They must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 14) or become addicted to the substance and unable to heal from anything else or eat anything else until their next Long Rest. This DC increases by 2 each time this item is consumed before a Long Rest.

item.name: Bolt Rifle
entries: A powerful weapon made to take targets down from afar, possessing a bolt-action mechanism to fire rounds at unparalleled speed and force.

item.name: Heavy Gauntlet
entries: A metallic glove made specially to allow for heavy punches instead of the usual defense a gauntlet provides.

entries.name: Special
entries: Heavy Gauntlets are meant to facilitate the use of your hands while being donned, yet still have their limitations. While donning a Heavy Gauntlet, you can still use that hand to cast Somatic components or interact with objects, but the metal makes it impossible to wield another weapon over it.

item.name: Heavy Revolver
entries: A steel-made revolver capable of causing heavy damage, but remaining unwieldy due to it's unwieldy kickback.

item.name: Single-Stroke Katana
entries: A sleek sword meant to end fights quickly after it's drawn from its sheath.

itemProperty.name: Unarmed
entries: A weapon with the Unarmed property is usually light enough to be worn over the hands as more of an accessory than a tool. While wielding those, you count any attacks done with them as unarmed weapon attacks.

feat.name: Ink Thicker Than Blood

prerequisite.other: You aren't of a Middle Subclass

entries: You've found yourself a place in a greater family and it shows in your skin with pride and pomp. When you take this Feature, consider how your character was first introduced to the Middle, how they came to join and how they look up to their older Siblings. Nevertheless, you gain the following:

items: Your choice of your Strength or Charisma scores increase by 1, to a maximum value of 20.
You instantly gain a 3rd level Tattoo of the Middle, as per the Path of Grievance's rules. You gain an additional one upon reaching 6th level, another at 10th and a final one at 14th level.

During combat, the enemy that dealt the most damage to you or your allies this round gains a {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. This lasts until the end of the next round, or until you fall unconscious. If no enemy has dealt damage this turn, the stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} is given to the enemy that last attempted to attack you or an allied creature. This applies after any other Middle Subclass characters application, going toward the creature that dealt the second most damage if applicable. Outside of combat, whenever someone rolls an ability check to hurt or damage your character or their reputation, they will also gain a point of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} until your next short rest. If combat is initiated right after an instance of this by rolling an initiative check, then the enemy with the highest initiative roll gains {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} until the end of the first round of combat.
Whenever you hit an enemy with a stack of {@condition Vengeance Mark|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}, they gain 1 stack of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entries: When first you take this Feature you gain a {@item Little Book of Vengeance|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} from another Sibling that acts as a courier for you.

feat.name: Masked Wounds
entries: {@i "I keep it covered because it hurts to even look at."}
You've been horribly disfigured in one way or another that left part of your body ever-aching, and you've procured a means to mask such a painful memory. You gain the following:

items: Your Constitution modifier increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You always have a means to procure a way to mask your wound, instantly recovering one roll of your Hit Die in Hit Points during a short rest.

Whenever your current Hit Points are reduced to or below half their Maximum Value, you enter a {@condition Sizzling Wound|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} state, as your pain soars to an unbearable amount, causing your mind to fully focus on drenching that wound in blood to quench the aching.

entries: While in this state your AC is reduced by 2 and you deal an additional 1d6 fire damage when dealing damage, also inflicting {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count equal to half your proficiency bonus. If the attack already deals fire damage, inflict a count equal to your proficiency bonus instead.
This state lasts until your next short rest or you recover all your Hit Points.

feat.name: Guided by the Will
entries: {@i "According to the city's will, its volition... The City's will matches the will of the people living in it."}

You are a follower of the Living Will and may have your orders appear to you in a small slip of paper at any given moment, standing by for the next goal. You are able to receive Prescripts in the following ways:

items: As a Free Action during your turn you may draw a Prescript, as per the Follower of an Order Prescripts and the Magicked Prescripts Tables. Upon completion, you gain one {@condition Grace of the Prescript|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} which remains until your next short or long rest. Upon failure, you suffer one {@condition Karmic Consequences|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} You may do this up to an amount of times equal to half your proficiency bonus per short or long rest, rounded down.

You may choose to draw from the Crawling Prescripts table upon finishing a long rest. Upon its completion, you gain three {@condition Grace of the Prescript|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. Upon a failure you suffer three {@condition Karmic Consequences|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} instead.

entries: Additionally the Will benefits you in certain moments of need. Once per turn you may spend one {@condition Grace of the Prescript|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} count to re-roll your damage die or a saving throw. You must do so before the DM determines it a success or a failure in the latter case.

prerequisite.other: You have no levels in a Living Will subclass.

feat.name: Hearts Cast Aside
entries: {@i "Qui si spoglia l'elmo e la corazza... e getta via la spada Durindana."}

Sometimes, your emotions become so turbulent that the only thing you manage to do to claw away from your aching heart is to sever what ties it down. While at half your maximum Hit Points or lower, you may spend your Bonus Action to grip a Magical Item that you are Attuned to in one of your free hands, instantly shattering the item into pieces and inciting a mad fury to beat from your heart, drawing more power to yourself. This power is according to the item's rarity, as follows:

entries.caption: Hearts Cast Aside
rows: Uncommon
You gain a +1 bonus modifier to all your Attack Rolls until the end of combat.
Rare
You gain a +1 bonus modifier to all your Attack Rolls and to your AC until the end of combat.
Very Rare
You gain a +2 bonus modifier to all your Attack Rolls, to your AC and to Strength, Dexterity and Constitution until the end of combat.
Legendary

You gain a +3 bonus modifier to all your Attack Rolls, to your AC, Saving Throws and an {@dice 1d4} bonus modifier to ability checks to all Ability Checks until your next Long Rest. Furthermore, when you would be reduced to one Hit Point you instantly gain half your Maximum Hit Points as Temporary Hit Points. When you gain these Hit Points, you may also let out a guttural scream, causing all creatures within 30-ft. of you to attempt a Strength saving throw or be pushed 10-ft. and become {@condition Frightened} of you for the next minute, or only be pushed back 5-ft. on a success.
Artifact
You gain the same effects as when you would Shattering a Legendary item. Additionally, while having Temporary Hit Points from this feature all damage you deal ignores Resistances and Immunities.

entries: You may use this ability once per Long Rest and the item is cannot be restored through any means other than a {@spell wish} spell. You may use this ability an additional time per Long Rest after reaching 16th-Level. If you attempt to shatter an Artifact, it is instead cracked and loses all its properties for {@dice 1d6} months. You gain the same value rolled in Exhaustion points after your next Long Rest, as your aching heart fails to cease its fervent beating.

feat.name: Retaliator
entries: {@i "Non trova pace il cor, né quiete il petto, se non vendica l'ira e'l suo disdegno."}
The world might beat and beat and beat you, but you never back down, not fully. You always end up striking back with all your might, granting the following benefits:

items: Your choice of your Strength, Dexterity or Constitution Attribute Score increases by 1, to a maximum of 20.

Whenever you suffer damage from another creature within your attack reach you may spend your Reaction to perform a weapon attack against them. You may also instead use a damaging cantrip to do so instead of a weapon attack.

_: A set of fancy clothes bearing purple all over them
at least two sets of golden chains
a wallet containing 10 gp and another 5 GP's worth of beer and other party drinks

entries.name: Feature: Middle Finger to the World
entries: Your family has gotten your back no matter what happens, but that can hardly matter when you are adventuring nigh and high with other folk, so they provide you the best they can when you're away from them. You have a 25% discount on any magical tattoos you'd purchase for yourself or trusted creatures.

Additionally, whenever you are within Middle controlled territory you have advantage on {@skill Intimidation} rolls and other siblings will easily provide food and shelter for you and any friends you bring along.
Alternatively, with your DM's permission ( or if you are playing with '24 Backgrounds in general ) gain the {@feat Ink Thicker Than Blood|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} Feat.

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: The vast majority of those adopted into the Middle are colourful figures who are a living party unto themselves, with many was to show that. Despite the seeming union of the faction as a whole, there are those who are around for power rather than just the ones who are looking for true loyalty and camaraderie. Nevertheless, a great knowledge for their extensive grudges is a must for any of them.
The Middle is defined by some form of relation to the rest of the gang, be that a quirk toward them or a way you particularly enjoy being part of the whole thing.

entries.caption: Familial Quirk
rows: I spend an embarrassingly massive amount of gold on cute stickers to award to others.
I look up to others easily and feel afraid of disappointing them.
Blasting loud music is the same as breathing to you, screw what others say.
I write every. Single. Little. Slight. In the book. No exceptions.
I spend excessive time every single day taking care of your luscious mane of hair.
I tend to butt heads with your siblings often in good humour, making sure everyone has enough strength to carry their chains.
I are a collector of trivia and information about each persons tattoos, usually recognizing people by their ink before their faces.
I always look cool to your younger siblings and you don't know why. After all, its simply your job to take care of them.

entries.caption: Personality Trait
rows: I meet any slight with immediate retribution in the form of violence.
I tend to give others a second chance, even if it is after giving them a well-deserved punch.
If my neck-line isn't invisible from the sheer weight of my chains, I am not stylish enough.
I can't calm down without a good beat in the background.
I live my life by the book, both in vengeance and in my lifestyle, preferring to have my routines be sacred and unchanging.
I can't deal with technicalities and hedge-cases that are complex, so I just always default to the worst case scenario on the basis of a single coin flip.

entries.caption: Ideal
rows: The reason I joined the family is freedom, I want to do whatever the hell I want whenever I want! (Chaotic)
Loyalty to your fellow is the most important thing in life. Breaking away from that is unforgivable. (Lawful)
I enjoy loud music. Environments with clear regulation are also favorable. (Neutral)
This is all about having a good time for me, what's truly right is making sure our little siblings are fine while the oldest to try and deal fairly with whatever comes our way. (Good)
Taking care of those close to you is important. (Any)
So what if I want to take some things for myself first? Family is about making sacrifices, after all. (Evil)

entries.caption: Bond
rows: Some asshole stole something precious from me. I want it back.
At first I was nothing more than just related to someone from the Middle, but after certain events that took them away from me I decided to enter in their honour.
I want to become a Great Sibling.
Some freakish calamity overtook the branch of the Middle that I am a part of, and I'm still picking myself up from the floor after that.
Out of all my siblings there are a handful some that I consider the closest to me.
My Book of Vengeance is to become the most well-written and well-executed Artifact in the history of the Middle.

entries.caption: Flaw
rows: In the end I see that the Middle really is just a bunch of nobodies clinging to one another. They're as expendable to me like any other joe, the only difference is that they're loyal.
I lose my cool way too quickly at the slightest transgression.
I can't find it in myself to forgive anyone who has wronged me, and much less so whenever someone crossed one of my loved ones.
I believe that rules exist for a reason, and must not be broken in any circumstance.
Doubts about joining have began clinging to me after joining and I don't know what to do.
I expect loyalty to be repaid with absolute obedience.

_: All the items of the background you are faking
a crumpled paper that reminds you of what you wish to become. (Or what was chosen for you to become.)

entries.name: Feature: Facsimile
entries: You've trained yourself to become something that you are not. Your walk, your manner of speech, even the abilities you openly display have been trained to craft a delicate persona that you perfectly maintain. When you choose this Background, choose another Background.

You gain a +1 bonus modifier on rolls using the Skill Proficiencies of the other Background. If this background would give you a bonus to rolls, you gain half the value you would add to those rolls, to a minimum of +1. This is always rounded down.

If it gives you protection or information of some sort, you cannot get it for sure, but have enough knowledge on the topic and an ability to weasel your way inside, gaining Advantage on checks related to that goal.
You add double your {@skill Deception} modifier to checks regarding maintaining your persona.

entries.name: Persona.
entries: Fakers can come in all shapes and sizes, and they'll convince you that they are something else. They aren't just liars or schemers, instead they are someone pretending to be what they ultimately are not at all given moments. To aid with a choice of who to become, you may roll on the following table or make up a Persona of your own:

rows: I was born poor and alone, always wanting to protect others, and so I used my strength to do just that, no matter if some betrayed me or not. (Folk Hero Background)
I am no one, but I have a dream. A dream to reach the highest- reaching factions and stand shoulder to shoulder to them all. (Urchin Background)
I have lost what once was my heart, yet its ghastly beat remains reverberating in my chest. I'll take my time to grow back into strength and take my dazzling revenge. (Soldier Background)
My friends, I always thought I'd protect them, that I'm a hero, but I'm not so sure anymore. I can't help but to run away from where I should be, like any weeping coward would. (Charlatan Background)
I am looking for my lost child, as I have been for so long and will keep doing so even if I need to tear the world apart to reach them. ( Far Traveler)
I have beckoned people towards a just cause, to a brighter future. I truly believe what I preach, even if most around me don't feel the same yet. (Sage Background)
My family is dead, my road thus far has been that of blood-shed, pain and suffering to those left in my wake. I will never go back to what once was. (Criminal Background)

I followed someone who I truly believed in to the bitter end, and my place in the world was lost in the process. Nevertheless, I am one who has earned and embodied my position even as I look toward the future. (Acolyte Background)

entries.name: Suggested Characteristics
entries: Now, one such as you has varied characteristics that even you might forget at times, as your Persona's have been superimposed onto you. Roll in your chosen background's Tables.

spell.name: Summon Wartime Rainfall
entries: You crush the metallic casings in your hand and blow their dust upward to form a localized storm cloud that forms various crimson magic circles that pelt down bullet fire as if raindrops. Choose an area you can see within range, a cloud of bullet hail sprouts to cover a 30-ft. by 30-ft. cube centered at that point.

Any creature must pass a Dexterity saving throw whenever they start or end their turns within that area, suffering {@damage 2d12} piercing damage on a failure, or half on a success. These bullets come from every direction at once, causing Large or greater creatures to suffer one additional damage die as per each additional 5-ft. of space they occupy in a line. ( This only counts a line traced between the start and end of where a creature occupies, such as having Large creatures suffer an additional {@damage 1d12} piercing damage, or Huge ones suffering an additional {@damage 2d12} and so on. )

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 4th level or higher, the damage increases by {@damage 1d12} for each slot level above 3rd.

spell.name: Frontliner's Baton March

components.m: a glass shard from a broken picture holder

entries: You conjure forth a plume of reddish smoke that lingers on the feet of your target, spreading outwards with movement and reinvigorating spirits as if it were a flare to focus aim onto a single victorious future. The target gains an additional 15-ft. of movement speed until the end of their next turn. At the start of their turn they gain 2 Poise count and gain an additional 2 count for each friendly creature they first enter within 5-ft. of until the end of their turn. Creatures passed by this way gain an amount of Poise count at the end of the runner's turn equal to 2 + the amount of creatures passed by.

spell.name: Sprouting Strike

components.m: a seed or piece of bark

entries: You enchant and flick the seed for rapid growth after sticking to the target. You a ranged spell attack against a target creature within reach and dealing 1 piercing damage on a hit. As a Free Action you may take after planting a seed on the creature you may cause it to sprout into heavy vines that dig into the ground, trapping the creature in place until it is destroyed. A creature trapped this has their movement speed reduced to 0.
These vines have 20 Hit Points, an AC of 12 and are Vulnerable to fire and slashing damage. They naturally vanish after one hour, wherein the seed also grows permanently dormant if not sprouted.
You have Advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth}) checks to hide the casting of this spell.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 2nd level or higher, the vines Hit Points increase by 10 and AC increase by 1 for each slot level above 1st.

spell.name: Blooming Manifestation

components.m: a handful of petals or leaves

entries: You toss three petals into the air and have the winds guide them to be buried in different unoccupied spots in the ground, causing them to quickly bloom into small branches that twitch and grow with unstable magic. Whenever a hostile creature moves into or around 5-ft. of one of these Branches, the Branch quickly moves to whip and grab at them, absorbing their willpower for sustenance. That creature must pass a Dexterity saving throw or fall {@condition Prone}, take {@damage 2d6} bludgeoning damage and 3 {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count. On a success, the Branch simply whiffs and remains in place.

Upon hitting a creature a Branch blooms and becomes a regular, yet beautiful plant. All others that have not bloomed simply shrivelling up and dying after the spell's duration passes or your Concentration is broken.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you create an additional Branch for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Rattling Smite

components.m: a scrap of paper with a symbol that you can peer into and see yourself

entries: You start channelling your magic into your weapons to have it shake and build up a horrible vibration. The next target creature you hit with a melee weapon attack suffers {@damage 1d8} additional thunder damage and three {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

spell.name: Shock Bubbles
entries: You conjure three spheres of pure vibrating energy that bend and break the shape of space around them.

You perform three ranged attacks against one target creature within range, or divide each attack towards different targets. On a hit, the target creature suffers three {@condition Tremor|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} counts and takes {@damage 2d6} thunder damage. If three spheres hit the same target, it suffers from {@variantrule Tremor Burst|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, you create an additional Sphere for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Time for Harvest
entries: You shoot out a razor-sharp vine coated in flowers that was bathed in your blood for its initial growth, and let it sink into a target creature to drain them of their life.

You perform a ranged spell attack against a creature within reach that you can see. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 2d12} piercing damage and have the seed sink into their being. For the spell's duration, whenever the target suffers damage they suffer additional piercing damage equal to your spell attack modifier and you recover Hit Points equal to half that amount, rounded down.

If you end your turn more than 60-ft. away from the linked creature, the vine connecting you both is severed and the spell ends early. The vine itself has an AC of 22 and 42 Hit Points, being vulnerable to fire and necrotic damage. Whenever targeted by another creature for a melee attack, the attacking creature suffers {@damage 1d8} piercing damage as its thorns grow to feed.

spell.name: Curse of Eroding Will
entries: You deliver a mind-shattering curse to another creature, forcing them to pass a Charisma Saving Throw or suffering from their will rapidly eroding in a horrible lapse into dread. On a failure, they suffer a negative modifier to their attack rolls, ability checks and Strength and Wisdom saving throws for each 5-ft. of movement speed they have reduced and 9 {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count.

Additionally, this breach in their resolve causes them to lose 5-ft. of movement speed per each 3 {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count they are suffering from, to a maximum loss of 20-ft. of movement. This negative modifier cannot surpass a -3 either.

spell.name: Heart-Breaking Smite
entries: The next time you hit a creature with a weapon attack before this spell ends, the weapon's figure distorts to seem cracked and its material slowly melting. The attack deals an additional {@damage 2d6} cold damage to the target and inflicts half the damage dealt ( rounded down. ) as counts of {@condition Sinking|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the extra damage increases by {@damage 1d6} for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Weaver's Wright
entries: You fold the piece of cloth and consume it, then point to up to six creatures within reach. Each of those creatures is wreathed by a woven mantle of white that protects them from whatever is to come, granting them {@dice 2d10} + your Spellcasting modifier's worth of Temporary Hit Points.

While these Temporary Hit Points remain, any damage taken that exceeds their value is reduced instead to become however many Temporary Hit Points remain, as the mantle takes the brunt of any attack before it can be directed at its wearer.
Ex: If a cloth-wearing creature is dealt 26 damage and they have 15 Temporary Hit Points, they instead only take 15 damage from that source.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, the amount of Temporary Hit Points granted increases by {@dice 2d10} for each other slot level above 4th.

spell.name: Baleful Brand

components.m: a crumpled paper with your genuine hopes and dreams

entries: You clasp your hands together and wring writing out of thin air, manifesting your magic into solidified threats that erode all it touches. You then point toward a creature within reach, performing a ranged spell attack against them. On a hit, the target suffers {@damage 6d10} psychic damage and suffers from their heart being slowly eroded. Until the end of the targets turn after their next turn, anytime it would suffer damage it suffers an additional 4 points of acid damage that cannot be reduced by any means. Furthermore, whenever the target ends their turn ( including the turn where this effect ends ) they suffer 10 acid damage that also cannot be reduced in any way.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 6th level or higher, you may choose one additional target within reach for each slot level above 5th.

spell.name: First Lightlock
entries: You crush the petal under your thumb to have its remains form a glowing sigil of a petal behind your shoulder, simultaneously creating increasing gashes of concentrated light. You perform a ranged spell attack roll against a target creature within reach, dealing {@damage 2d6} slashing damage on a hit.

Each time you cast this spell, you may use your Action during your next turn to spend a Spell Slot of one level greater to cast this spell at a greater Unlock rank, causing additional effects to trigger as per the following:

entries.name: Unlock II
entries: The second time this spell is cast you perform an additional ranged spell attack roll against the target, dealing {@damage 3d8} piercing damage on a hit. You have advantage on this roll if you hit the first attack.

entries.name: Unlock III
entries: The third time this spell is cast, the slashing damage it deals increases to {@damage 3d6} and the piercing damage it deals increases to {@damage 4d8}.
After using any greater Unlock rank, you may spend it's corresponding Spell Slot Level to cast this spell and make use of it's corresponding effects until the end of your next long rest.

entries.name: Singleton
entries: After causing the effects of Unlock III, you regain one first-level spell slot.

spell.name: Sense Quarry

components.m: a slip of paper wishing for peace

entries: You press your hands together and allow the slip of paper to be burnt, with its ashes forming a wave that washes around you, highlighting the silhouette of any creature within range that is actively fighting or harbours immediate hostile intent toward another creature.
You can discern what or who a creature is if you are familiar with their general shape but may not determine the target of their hostility.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 3rd level or higher, the range increases by 100-ft. for each slot level above 2nd.

spell.name: Binding Chains
entries: You reach out your hand toward a target within reach, swirling your arm as five flashes of light appear around them and soon transforming into burning bright chains that bind them. You choose one target within reach to perform a Strength saving throw, becoming bound for the duration on a failure. They may re-attempt this saving throw at the end of their turns.
While bound, the target has their movement speed halved and a negative modifier to their Attack Rolls, Dexterity and Constitution saving throws equal to your proficiency bonus.

entries.name: Singleton
entries: The target also suffers the same negative modifier to Strength and Wisdom saving throws.

entriesHigherLevel.name: At Higher Levels
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you may target an additional creature within range for each slot level above 4th.

monster.name: Stigmatized Memory

ac.special: 12 + your PB, chosen when summoning this creature

hp.special: 4 times your Ranger level plus your PB

languages: understands any you know, but can't speak other than unintelligible murmurs

trait.name: Designated Execution
entries: Whenever killed by a Fell Memoir Ranger or a creature who similarly clutches memories to use as fuel, the killer deals an additional {@damage 1d8} damage until the end of their next turn. This extra damage is of the same type of the creature's attacks.

action.name: Shambling Jab
entries: {@atk mw} {@hitYourSpellAttack} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}3 ({@damage 1d6} + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier) bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Re-Enactment of the War
entries: {@atk rw} {@hitYourSpellAttack} to hit, range 60/90 ft., one target. {@h}2 ({@damage 1d4} + your Wisdom or Charisma modifier) piercing damage.

reaction.name: Obey Firing Order
entries: When ordered by their summoner, the {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} Memory performs a Shambling Jab attack or a Re-Enactment of the War attack against a target creature of the summoner's choice.

reaction.name: Obey Repositioning Order
entries: When ordered by their summoner, the {@condition Stigmatized|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} Memory spends their Reaction to move up to 20-ft. in any direction of the summoner's choice.

trait.name: Pack Tactics
entries: The BongBong [Orange] has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of BongBong [Orange]'s allies is within 5 ft. of the creature and the ally isn't {@condition Incapacitated}.

trait.name: Tailed for the Palate
entries: When BongBong [Orange] hits a creature with an attack, they lose 5 feet of movement until the end of their next turn.

trait.name: The Secret of Taste
entries: When BongBong [Orange] dies, roll a {@dice d20}. On a roll of 16 or higher, it has a chance of spraying its blood in the creature's mouth, making them regain {@dice 4d4 + 4} hit points.

trait.name: Wandering Ordeal
entries: Whenever BongBong [Orange] uses its burrowing speed, it does not provoke opportunity attacks.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: BongBong [Orange] makes 2 Pounce attacks or 1 Gnawing Gobble and 1 Pounce attack.

action.name: Pounce
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 8} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}15 ({@damage 3d6 + 5}) piercing damage and the creature suffers 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. If the target is already Bleeding, deal an additional 3 ({@damage 1d6}) die of piercing damage. If the attack hits, the creature must succeed on a {@dc 16} Constitution saving throw or suffer vulnerability to piercing damage until the end of their next turn. A creature that succeeds this effect becomes immune to it for the next hour.

action.name: Gnawing Gobble
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 8} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}12 ({@damage 3d4 + 5}) piercing damage and the creature suffers 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. If the target is already Bleeding, deal an additional 2 ({@damage 1d4}) die of piercing damage.

action.name: Orange-flavored Bubble Supplement
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 8} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}10 ({@damage 2d4 + 5}) necrotic damage and the creature suffers 3 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. If the target is already Bleeding, deal an additional 2 ({@damage 1d4}) die of piercing damage. If the attack hits, a 5-foot area around the target becomes difficult terrain as the bubbly liquid sticks to the ground.

action.name: Add a Note of Bubbly Flavor
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 8} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}18 ({@damage 3d8 + 5}) piercing damage and the creature suffers 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. If the target is already Bleeding, deal an additional 4 ({@damage 1d8}) die of piercing damage. If the target has vulnerability to piercing damage, they must succeed on a {@dc 16} Dexterity saving throw or lose their tongue as the BongBong [Orange] pounces to devour it.

footer.name: Loot
entries: Once killed, BongBong [Orange] will always drop 1 {@item BongBong Orange|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}.

footer.name: Bestiary
entries: A mysterious insect-like creature with acidic blood that, when in contact with air or diluted enough, turns into a sweet beverage. This creature seems to know how healthy another creature is and prioritizes attacking targets that are healthier than others to serve as their food source.

trait.name: Food Production
entries: When BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange] is killed, it summons a {@creature BongBong [Orange]|TheUndertomesProjectMoon} where it used to be. The BongBong [Orange] rolls its own initiative.

trait.name: Fragile Orange Bubble
entries: Any creature aiming a Ranged Attack against BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange] can choose to target the bubbles on its back. BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange]'s DC increases by 5, but if the attack roll hits it deals maximum damage. Any hostile creature within 5 feet of it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw ({@dc 17}) or take {@damage 1d10} Acid damage from the burst of the bubble.

trait.name: Pack Tactics
entries: The BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange] has advantage on an attack roll against a creature if at least one of BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange]'s allies is within 5 ft. of the creature and the ally isn't {@condition Incapacitated}.

trait.name: Wandering Ordeal
entries: Whenever BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange] uses its burrowing speed, it does not provoke opportunity attacks.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange] makes 2 Chomping Gobble attacks or 1 Filling a Medium-sized Orange Bubble and 1 Chomping Gobble attack.

action.name: Chomping Gobble
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 11} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}23 ({@damage 4d8 + 5}) piercing damage and the creature suffers 1 count of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. If the target is already Bleeding, deal an additional 4 ({@damage 1d8}) die of piercing damage.

action.name: Filling a Medium-sized Orange Bubble
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 11} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}21 ({@damage 3d10 + 5}) piercing damage and the creature suffers 3 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. If the target is already Bleeding, deal an additional 4 ({@damage 1d8}) die of piercing damage. If the attack hits, the creature must succeed on a {@dc 17} Constitution saving throw or suffer 1 count of {@condition Fragility|TheUndertomesProjectMoon}. A creature that succeeds this effect becomes immune to it for the next hour.

action.name: More Potent, More Plentiful
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 11} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}18 ({@damage 3d8 + 5}) necrotic damage and the creature suffers 3 counts of {@condition Bleed|TheUndertomesGeneralRules}. If the target is already Bleeding, deal an additional 4 ({@damage 1d8}) die of acid damage. If the target is a creature, it is {@condition Grappled} (escape {@dc 17}). Until this grapple ends, the target is {@condition Restrained}, and BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange] can't use this on another target.

action.name: Feed Consumption for BongBong Procreation
entries: The BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange] makes one More Potent, More Plentiful attack against a Large or smaller creature it is grappling. If the attack hits, that creature takes the attack's damage and is swallowed, and the grapple ends. While swallowed, the creature is {@condition Blinded} and {@condition Restrained}, it has total cover against attacks and other effects outside the BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange], and it takes 21 ({@damage 6d6}) acid damage at the start of each of the BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange]'s turns.

If the BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange] takes 30 damage or more on a single turn from a creature inside it, the BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange] must succeed on a {@dc 15} Constitution saving throw at the end of that turn or regurgitate all swallowed creatures, which fall {@condition Prone} in a space within 10 feet of the BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange].
If the BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange] dies, a swallowed creature is no longer restrained by it and can escape from the corpse using 15 feet of movement, exiting prone.

footer.name: Loot
entries: Once killed, BunBun [Juicy Squeezer - Orange] will always drop 4 {@item BongBong Orange|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|BongBong Oranges}.

footer.name: Bestiary
entries: A mysterious insect-like creature with acidic insides that, when in contact with air or diluted enough, turns into a sweet beverage. This creature seems to prefer easier prey and prioritizes attacking targets that are slow, usually going for those with less movement or that are lower in the initiative count.

table.name: Crawling Prescripts
table.caption: Crawling Prescripts
rows: Among those you consider your companions, find out which of them is the youngest and acquire as much currency as you can. On the final day of the week, spend all of it to throw a party for your youngest companion.
Nurture the next wounded creature you see back to health, then eat it as dinner after it is healed.
Investigate the first murder you come across and after finding the culprit, abandon the case.
Destroy something which is priceless in front of one who values it.

Create 3 paintings of the most beautiful things you know, then throw them into a fire. (You must truly capture the beauty. To do so, you must spend at least 3 hours or a Long Rest to create a painting by attempting a {@skill Performance} check, successfully painting a work that satisfies you on a DC of 16.)

For the foreseeable future, greet every third person you come across. If reciprocated, you must reverse their gravity centre onto the ground. (You must successfully Grapple the creature and suplex them as an Action, dealing 3d8 + your Strength modifier on a success.)
Slay a beast that is larger than you yet smaller than the last room you have slept or stayed more than 15 minutes at. (This may be a creature of Aberration, Beast or Monstrosity type.)
For the next three days: become the smartest eater. (You must use a combined tool for eating, such as a spork, fpoon or switchblade. You cannot consume food without its use.)
See that no creature finds their eyes open by the end of your violent engagements.

Become a saint in red. (Gift something worth at least 1 gold to 10 or more children. This Prescript is instantly failed if you cause the children to cry or if any harm befalls them until the Prescript is undertaken.)
Cook three waffles and stack them while putting mayonnaise on the bottom waffle. Then serve them to the 9th person you saw this week and wish them a happy birthday.
Stalk the third person you see. In within 7 days but not less of 3 days, attempt to win their heart and break it. Record this experience.

Embrace and conjoin the way of a Hero. (Within a week, bite off one piece of a fresh apple and change into a new personality according to the Heroes Journey every day. (Roll a 1d8, no repeats) (1: Act of the best of intentions (Hero), 2: Guide those who are lost or without reason (Mentor), 3: Assist those who are in trouble (Ally), 4: Give those without reason a task (Herald), 5: Disrupt those with a goal with a hurdle (Trickster), 6: Be of aid or of disdain (Shapeshifter), 7: Test the position of the able-bodied fighters, kill if they are unworthy, spare if they are worthy (Guardian), 8: Vow to kill the first able-bodied fighter you see in a day (Shadow).)

Paint one picture of yourself exclusively using paints made of cadmium and sell them for a week. (You may attempt Sleight of Hand or {@skill Performance} checks for your works quality. The resulting rolls become the DC that any creature who spends more than a day within vicinity of this painting must pass as a Constitution saving throw or become {@condition Poisoned} until receiving medical or clerical aid.)

Find god in a tomato. (Pray every day and plant a whole fruit in the ground while reciting prayers, then roll a d100. On a roll of 90 or greater, it sprouts to a tree sapling mere moments after being planted as if by godly will and you are successful in this Prescript.
Become a mirror of the next being reflected in your eyes. (Act as the first creture that you see after getting this Prescript until someone else points it out.)
In one week, win 5 left shoes in games of cards.

Spread one's wings. (You must help any random person of your choice pursue and at least begin reaching a dream of theirs. An example would be aiding one who wishes to become a wizard enroll in an Arcane Study Institution.)
Act as new. (Act as a person who is incredibly naive and unaware, often unsure of their actions and doubts their every move until someone questions why you are acting in such a way.)
Embrace the natural downpour of greater hearts. (If it rains or snows, use no weather protection and instead stay under the phenomena until the Prescripts completion or until the event ceases.)

Be unlike yourself. (Your alignment must be reversed for the Prescripts duration, neutrals remain neutral with inversed values, such as if they hated undead they now must act as if they love them. Lawful characters must act chaotic and so on.)

Kidnap a person every day for 4 days, on that same day, ask them the meaning of life and why they don't wish to die. If any answer yes, pre-emptively leave and avoid that person for the rest of their life. Otherwise, take note of the answers and leave it in a cleaned plate of food of the next tavern or inn you visit.
Be as of the accursed birds of black feather. (Communicate only by mimicking other's words.)

Experience what it is to be alive. (Within the next seven days, feel the emotions of Hate/Resentment, Anger/Wrath, Anxiety/Bad, Joy/Pride, Calmness/Peace, Disgust/Envy, Innocence/Curiosity, Sadness/Gloom, Shock/Fear, and Love/Longing.)
Steal the hearts of the people who fought and died against you.

Paint your view of heaven and what you wish to see after death. Then show it around to your fellows and hear their opinions. ( This creation must be sincere and contain both your sufferings and yearnings. You may attempt {@skill Performance} checks, yet they mean nothing. When you do so, you must spend at least 5 days doing so, if not longer. Upon each long rest, describe what are the feelings your character is having to go through to reach this ideal vision. In the end, question if it is something you'd deserve or still need to get within grasp of.)
Provide safe passage and sanctuary to the next wounded creature you see. Ask nothing of return except for a single story of their lives.
Do not aid the dreary. (Do not do anything that would result in other creatures being Stabilized, recover Hit Points or that would result in a negative Condition of theirs ending early.)
Visit a church not of your own God and learn their truths and falsities. Then commit either a sin or ten good deeds in their eyes.

Trace the direction of your homeland on a map, then acquire a bow and arrow. Set the ammunition aflame and shoot it toward the sky at midnight for three nights. If it ever hits or narrowly misses a person, monster or creature, regale them with the food of your homeland in a show of genuine hospitality.
Do not ask a single question. Only do as you know best.
Be exceedingly courteous, no matter how rude or debauched your fellows might add.

Play a song to mesmerize the hearts of all that could hear. (If you do not know how to play an instrument, seek a master to do so. After being taught, you permanently gain Proficiency in that instrument.)

In a single swig, drink a glass bottle's worth of poison. (If not Immune to the {@condition Poisoned} Condition: Roll a number of Hit Die equal to your level divided by 3, rounded down. Your Maximum Hit Points are deduced by that value for a week. This Prescript is instantly completed upon consuming the poison.)

Bite your tongue. (Speak only in one language other than Common. If you know no other languages, either only communicate through emoji if playing virtually or through mimicking your meanings if in person or through video.

Become a pretty picture in a pricey wall. (Ask your party members how much they think their heads are worth. Then print or commission an artist to make several bounty posters of your party with their ascribed values. Post them in whichever Tavern, Guild Hall, or Public Post Sign you can.)

Part ways with that which has greatly aided you. (Discard one magic item you have been Attuned to since the last long rest. This item may not be cursed nor be given to a permanent member of the party.)

Speak only in rhymes. If you come across something wearing or that is of orange color, only lie to them instead of rhyming. (This extends to simple conversation, such as saying "Good night" as simple courtesy while it is day.)
At night, before sleep, confess your most painful secret to the one who sleeps closest to you.
Do nothing as the products of your heart stand in the face of death. (Do not heal any friendly creatures or Stabilize them for any reason.)
Embrace the first ideal presented to you, no matter how you may feel about it.
Mock those in power, aggrandize those who have nothing.
Revel in filth and disease. (You must Poison yourself and at least five other creatures.)
Act like a legendary hero or villain of the region. (You must dress like them, change your appearance to be like them and attempt to imitate their personality.)
Harbor no doubt, plant no regrets. (Draw another Prescript. You gain double the effect you would gain upon its completion or failure.)

Push yourself to your limits. (You must reach at least 5 Exhaustion points. You may, once per roll give yourself Advantage after failing a attack, check or save, taking the new result and gaining a point of Exhaustion. You must do so after rolling but before the DM announces the result.)
Spread the word of the Prescripts to seven people. (You must convince seven creatures to Draw at least one Prescript.)
Clutch with the golden hand what is yours. (Do not spend a single gold piece, use an item on another creature or otherwise grant them a gift or material gain.)
Take a measured stride always. (Never take the Dash Action or willingly attempt an {@skill Athletics} or {@skill Acrobatics} check.)
Become yourself. Act like you would before getting your first prescript. (Do you even remember who you were then?)
Handle your share in your utmost lonesome. (Do not accept or take the Aid, help or counselling from other creatures.)
Make peace. (Successfully end hostilities or at least form a truce between yourself and another creature or faction. Alternatively, do so as a mediator between two parties.)
Light the sparks of war. (Successfully pit one party against another without being linked as the source of the conflict.)
Take no part in mysticism. (While out of combat, cast no spells and use no magic items.)
Discover the secrets of at least three of the people that share a meal with you.
Spread or fabricate a legend or myth across your current settlement, or the next one you come across if within the wilderness.
Decline matters of subtleness. (You cannot willingly attempt {@skill Stealth} checks and must always either loudly knock on doors before coming through or kick them open if locked.)

Atone for your past sins while enduring the interminable hell of your own making. (You must do so in a way that is found acceptable after confessing to your nearest Cleric or spiritually adjacent creature. They must dictate how to better atone. For the duration, you must not recover hit points.)
Whenever you tell a lie or are untrustworthy, bite down your tongue with force. (You suffer 3d8 piercing damage whenever you do so. Untrustworthiness delineates lying, cheating or spreading secrets.)
Draw in black the lines of suffering on your body. (Your body must be marked with black dotted lines at the articulations. Hostile creatures gain Advantage to hit you while within 5-ft. of you)

In lack of acknowledgement, light yourself ablaze. (If you do not take responsability for your actions and see them through, as per the DMs discretion, you must set yourself on fire as an Action. You suffer 16 {@condition Burn|TheUndertomesGeneralRules} count instantly.)
Understand the searing pain of death. (Harm yourself with an iron weapon whenever you kill another creature or, if out of combat, cause harm to them. You cannot reduce the damage taken by any means.)
Destroy the sound. (Whenever a creature speaks in a tone louder than casual conversation, such as a scream, perform a weapon attack against them until they are silent. This includes yourself.)
Clap without a sound, slash without a voice. (Start any Combat Hidden and do not fail a single {@skill Stealth} check.)

Refuse yourself the graces, disable your own recital. (Do not make use of your Channel Divinity feature. If you are of another class, do not use its main resource, such as Rage, Ki or Sorcery Points, Sneak Attack and so on. The DM determines what the main resource is. For full-casters such as the Wizard, they cannot spend their highest level Spell Slots or 5th level Spell slots or greater.)
Hold your fellow being as if dancing whenever addressing them. (You must hold a creatures body whenever directly talking to them or Grapple a creature before attacking them during combat.)
Welcome the Wills in minor scale. (During combat, at the start of your turns always draw a Prescript from the Magicked Prescripts table. [From the Oath of Procuration Subclass])

Loudly proclaim your fair crew's namesake at the heat of combat. (Whenever your party has triumph over a challenge, such as interacting with an adverse character, winning a game of dice or entering battle, scream your party's name loudly.)

Act by unpredictable whim. (Always choose your targets randomly. If there are multiple ways of approaching a situation through Skill checks, do so randomly. If you have to make a decision that can be summarized as "yes or no", pick a side and toss a coin to decide.)

Always harm that which harms the Will. (You must always deal damage at least once per turn to creatures {@condition Target of the Prescript|TheUndertomesProjectMoon|Marked by the Prescript}. If any other creature refuses or speaks ill of your god, engage in combat against them. You may not kill them.)

Knock on three front doors of three different homes at midnight during three different days. If attended to, ask for food. If refused, starve until a creature gives you food, if given food grant the one who fed you a gift of your choice the next day. (You suffer one point of Exhaustion for each night spent without food.)
Cook three waffles and stack them while putting mayonnaise on the bottom waffle. Then serve them to the 9th person you saw today and wish them a happy birthday.
Acquire a relic of some importance and grant it as a boon to the nearest blacksmith or merchant. (You must give a Magic Item that you have acquired after drawing this Prescript.)
Eradicate that which must not be known, burn a wound into history. (Attempt to burn any books and parchment you touch or a creature intends to give to you within a timespan of 5 minutes.)
See not the world for what it is, but instead of what you wish it to be. (You must blindfold yourself for the duration of the Prescript, becoming {@condition Blinded}.)
Learn of others and have others learn of others in tow. (Ask someone to tell you a personal story and repeat it truthfully to another creature before the week ends.)
Be precise in your curiosity. (In any interaction, you may only ask any individual creature only up to three questions per long rest.

Become a part-time historian, grant the gift of knowledge to the mystics. (Learn the name and history of any landmarks you come across. Log them in a leather-bound book and then give it to another spellcaster.)
Find an object left unattended and attempt to return it to its owner. Upon failure, willingly lose one object of your own choice that is similar to the first object lost.
Lift others burdens, aid those without ability. (You must take the Aid Action whenever another creature attempts a skill check, aiding them.)

Embrace the sheer inexplainable force of luck. (Whenever you roll a d100, do so three more times then decide which is the true roll by rolling a d4. The d100 are presented in the order they were rolled.)

When in doubt, ask the stars. (If your character has a question, ask around the table for other players answers. The DM selects one of the responses given and your character imagines that response while looking up to the sky.)
Once a day for the next week, when the sun hangs at it's highest, find the 5th person you see. Challenge them to duel, if you win thank them for their time. If you lose, apologize for your weakness.

Be a retainer to your friend, sneer your foes. (Act as if you were the humble servant of one party member of your choice. Actively mock and disrespect any who come to disrespect that creature in any way. You may choose pets and companions as a party member for this Prescript.)

Leave no slight unpunished. (If a creature lies to you, you must lie to them enough that they feel unsure of what they are doing in life. If a creature harms you, you must at least leave a lasting injury on their body, such as severing a finger. If a creature slights you, you must make them cry.)

Interrogate nature and reach a tune with it. (Attempt to interview any critter or beast you find in a conversation. The 6th beast you come across gives you a random trinket of your DMs choice, as per their discretion or rolled on any trinket table.)
Simulate a better person than who you are. (Help the homeless when able, avoid killing other creatures and do not commit any sins against any Deities.)
Ignore social etiquette and always respond with the first thing that comes to your mind.

Fish a fish greater in length than your head. Then grill it. Then feast on it with your comrades. Then carve knives out of its bones. Leave these knives within the third hole you see this week after eating the fish. (The length of your head includes horns.)
Be free-spirited in vour consumerism. (Always accept and consume any potions, drinks, food and drugs given to you.)
Allow the stressed hard workers to rest. (For all nights you remain in a settlement, convince and work in stead of an tavernkeeper or similar professional to the best of your ability.)
Whenever you come across a shunned topic or forgotten knowledge, start a conversation around it and attempt to restore any form of glory it once might have had.

Call out your every action. (Creatures have Advantage on {@skill Perception} checks against you. Furthermore, all Spells you cast gain the Verbal component. If they would require a target to attempt a Strength, Dexterity or Constitution saving throw, they gain Advantage.)
Arrange a collection of your favorite colour. (You must pick up and constantly carry all objects of the chosen colour in your person until the end of this Prescript.)

Log your adventure's next three days for those who will come. (Keep a detailed diary of whatever you and your party has done during the day and update it at night. Then leave it at the nearest Inn, Tavern or public space.)
When faced with multiple paths, always take the hardest known route.

Learn and help another learn of the story they tell at night for the next three nights. (Before the next long rest, ask another party member about their most recent dreams and relate it back to them in your own words. Repeat this three times.)
Follow along your path. The Will is watching you. (Simply keep progressing towards your Party's current objective. Acknowledge that it is all part of a grander plan.)
Try something you have never once done in your life.

Have your hair groomed to absolute lusciousness. If you have no hair, have your head shined to a sparkling sheen. (You must spend at least 60 * your Level GP to do so. After doing so, your Charisma score increases by 2 for the next week.)

table.name: Magicked Prescripts
table.caption: Magicked Prescripts
rows: Designate the first creature you see as your sibling, refer to them as such for the remainder of the day. If any slights are committed against your sibling no matter how minor, violently avenge them.
After defeating a foe, take their weapon and carve out their initials on their face. (You must spend your Bonus Action to do so.)
Move toward the closest enemy, then kneel down before them and aim for their left leg without damaging their bones. (Do not deal bludgeoning damage.)
When facing the one who had harmed you, return the favor through a minor inconvenience of your choosing.
Hum an unpleasant tune out loud, and attack the second person who is annoyed by it. (You do so as a Free Action.)

When face to face to the one harming you, stand still and strike a pose or approach them slowly until they have hit you. (You must move only half your movement speed per turn toward a creature hostile to you.)
Throw dust over the eyes of the first person (or thing) that intends to touch you.

Challenge the next person that intends to hurt or heal you to a match of Rock, Paper, Scissors, then attack them with the damage most synonymous with the winning throw. (Rock -> Bludgeoning | Scissors -> Slashing | Paper -> Piercing. If they fail to play, you may conclude the Prescript by dealing damage to the target.)
Give the creature closest to you a Prescript. If they do not conclude it until the next 12 seconds, you fail this Prescript.

If you or any creature you view as an ally is slighted or harmed in any way, you must attempt to learn the name of the offending creature and write it down on paper along with the offense they commited and read it aloud to the offending creature.

Scare or Flirt with the person (or thing) that intends to hurt you. If they react to you, cut their eyeballs. (You may perform a Persuasion Check against the targets passive Insight score. On a success, they are Charmed until the start of their next turn.)
Approach the person intending to hurt or heal you in a cheery jog, then, dropkick them. (You become Prone on a hit or a miss.)
When attacking the person who has not attacked you, adjust your hair upwards while doing so. (You must have a free hand to do so.)
On the first round of combat, Grapple the nearest creature to you. Then declare that you are the king of watermelons with pride." (You are a king despite your gender.)
Target any foe that wears purple or cares too much for there hair.

Before killing another foe, ask them for mercy. If they do not grant it, strike yourself instead. If they do, slay them immediately. (You must perform a melee weapon attack against yourself. You hit automatically.)
In your next combat encounter, hop like a frog to reach your enemy. (You can only move using the jump action.)

For the next 24 hours proclaim each of your attacks in overdramatic ways. (You conclude this Prescript if you execute until the start of your turn, but retroactively fail it if you fail to do so for the duration.)
Only speak in Haiku for a while. (You must speak a successful Haiku at least once until the start of your next turn.)

Recite the lyrics of a song or poem to the next person you fight, only stopping once they're Unconcious or dead. (You conclude this Prescript if you execute until the start of your turn, but retroactively fail it if vou fail to do so for the duration.)
Murder five small critters, and attach them to a body.
When choosing a target may your blow fall 10 feet. (You must have the source of your attack, such as a blade or arrow, fall at least 10-ft. before hitting your target.)

If someone looks at you, punch their face. (You must perform a unarmed weapon attack against that target. Their AC is increased by 2 if they have one head only. On a hit, the target is Blinded until the start of your next turn.)

Make a soup for someone who has wronged you or an ally. Upon serving one portion to the individual, remind them that you do not forgive them and splash another portion into their face. (You may prepare this soup as an Action during your turn provided you have any liquid and anything that could be considered edible within within 5-ft. 5-ft, of you.) (Applying fire to heat it may be done as a Free Action if you have a viable source. After you spend your Action to do so, ask the table out of character if the Soup is "Crap", "Mid", "Good" or "Outstanding". You may serve the soup and toss it as a Bonus Action.? (Upon tossing it, make a weapon attack roll against a target within reach. You are proficient in this if you are proficient in Cook's Utensils. If the majority chose the first, the creature suffers 1d8 poison damage when eating the soup and another 1d8 of the same damage upon having it thrown upon their face.) (On the second, the creature is suffers 1d4 damage when the soup is tossed. If its Good the creature is healed by 1d4 hit points when consuming the soup and suffering 1d4 cold or fire damage when it is tossed, and if the soup is "Outstanding" they are healed by 1d12 hit points when consuming the soup and suffer 1d4 psychic damage when it is tossed.)

Take the weapon of the next creature you slay, until the end of the brawl, use only it. (The Prescript is considered complete when you first equip the weapon and is retroactively considered incomplete if you deal damage using anything else other than the weapon or your Paladin spells.)
Whatever you do, do not stop dancing. (Spend at least half your movement speed on your turn.)
Distance yourself from your friends, allies and acquaintances. (You must end your turn at least 30-ft. away from friendly creatures.)
Become touchy-feely. (You must end your turn at least 5-ft. within a friendly creature.)

Do not strike another foe until your current one lies dead. (Do not switch targets after first dealing damage to a creature within your turn. This Prescript counts as concluded upon first ending your turn after hitting said creature and is retroactively failed if you switch targets.)
Be as a dog and walk upon nature. (Only crawl to move until the end of your turn.)
Become a magic man. (Act like the setting's closest thing to a moustache-bearing parlour magician until the end of your turn. You cannot use true spells.)
Act unpredictably in the face of your foes. (Use only different Actions than what you used in your last turn of combat, even if it was a different combat.)

Become a simulacra of a beloved person to your left. (Imitate te tl the closest ally to your characters immediate right. Mimic their voice, mannerisms and use the closest weapon or spells available to you compared to theirs.)

Take the next hit aimed at you. Give it back twofold. (Spend a Bonus Action to lower your AC by 5 until you are hit once. During your next turn, you apply your damage dice twice whenever you next hit a creature with an Attack.)
Drink a potion. If you have none, attack your closest ally.

Aid your closest ally so you feel hopeful of your immediate future. (Take the Help Action targeting the closest friendly creature. If they pass their next roll, you gain the effect of Help for the next two turns.)
Dialogue with the closest hostile creature. Attempt to difuse the situation. If they can't understand your language, do everything in your power to attempt to make them understand.
Make the most of your time. (You must spend your Action, Bonus Action and perform a Free Action until the end of your turn.)

Be merciful on your next fight. (Do not kill anyone present in your next combat. The Prescript is fulfilled once you knock a creature Unconscious, and retroactively Failed if you kill one of the creatures afterward.)
Punish only those you can't touch. (You must only perform ranged attacks until the end of your turn.)
Do as you're told. (Always perform actions dictated by other creatures. You have infinite Reactions until the start of your next turn.)
Fight with your eyes closed for 6 seconds.
Whenever you hit a foe, also headbutt them. (You and the creature suffer 1d6 bludgeoning damage whenever you do so.
Kick a dog. (Or animal closest to a dog. If able, a tortoise.)
Wrestle your foes to submission. (You may refer to WWE wrestlers and other augmented-reality-fighters to do so. Even games like street fighter count.)
Get up close and personal with your foes. (You must only perform melee attacks until the end of your turn.)

Remove the tongue of whomever has disrespected you or people in high-ranking positions. (To do so, you must land an Attack while choosing to have the target have their AC have a +5 bonus modifier. On a successful hit, the target is unable to speak until their tongue is restored.)
Invoke the fury of the elements. (A suggested mechanic for this is only dealing fire, cold or lightning damage until the end of your turn. The DM may choose to accept any other interpretation.)

Wildcard. (Ask the player to your immediate right [Or above you if playing online] for a Prescript. That becomes this Prescript. If it is toward your detriment, that player gains an Inspiration they may use until the end of the fight.)
Crash someone through a window. (You may use the Shove Action to do so. If you do, the creature suffers 3d8 piercing damage.)
Tear of your armor and fight without fear of death. (You unequip your armor as a Bonus Action when done this way.)
Go unseen from the beholding's eyes. (Take the Hide Action until the end of your turn and do so successfully.)
Embrace your pains and endure. (Allow every single attack aimed at you to hit you. Do not become Unconscious until the start of your next turn.)

Impress your friends with a dazzling weapon flourish. (Roll a Performance check with a DC of 14 + half your Paladin Level. On a success, gain half your Paladin Level + 2 of Poise Count. These are halved down.)
Strike yourself once in the rib.
Rob a corpse bare of its belongings and toss them in the nearest trash heap, corpse or body of water.
Start a debate of morals with the one who has hurt you the most. Win it.
Do whatever is in your power to have the creature closest to you mimic an animal of your choice until the start of your next turn.
Give a meaningful gift to one of your foes. If they accept and are commoved by it, cease fighting them immediately unless they strike you.

Shoot upward near another and believe. (You must name one of your ranged attacks and be within 5-ft. of another creature. You and the controller of that creature roll a d100. The one who rolled the lowest is hit.)
Crush your left foot with your right foot. (You take 1d8 plus your Strength modifier in bludgeoning damage and lose 10-ft. of walking speed for two turns.)

Eat this Prescript. If unable, eat a dagger (If you eat the Prescript you must pass a DC 16 Constitution Saving Throw or be Poisoned for the next minute, being able to retry this this Save Save at the end of your next turns.)
Only walk in the direction of lights in respect of those who are gone.
Strike unjust ones with blunt force trauma. (Use bludgeoning damage only. Target creatures who are hostile to creatures of lower level or CR than them.)
Kill all the doors of the ceiling. (Kill at least one hostile creature above you.)
Breach down the walls and forsake those who would forsake you. (Attack a hostile creature that is behind a wall. On a successful hit, that cover is broken if possible.)
Do not acknowledge anyone else but your foes.
Recite your tenets or beliefs aloud, proceeding to strike any being that questions or dares criticize them.
Start a fire and impede it from being put down, for it is not a dog.

Tell your dreams and wants to one of your enemies. If they answer truthfully, ask them for a duel and spare them on a win. If they lie, kill them at all costs. (This Prescript lasts until the end of combat.)
Breach a taboo of the area you are living in. (If in the City as your setting, you may only break a social Taboo. Don't kill yourself over this, please. The Claws have better things to do.)
Stay by your fellows side, defe defend them at all costs. (You must end your turn within 5-ft. of a friendly creature and they cannot have suffered damage until the start of your next turn.)

Give away half your money to the creature farthest from you that you can reach. Toss it with your full force. (You have a reach of 30-ft. times your Strength modifier for this, with a minimum of 15-ft.)

If you see a critter, follow it. (The DM may have any tiny creature such as a butterfly appear to guide you. This may last for up to three turns. At the end, your DM may choose to have you find nothing, an uncommon magic item or a map to somewhere you don't recognize.)
Clean all the dirt and grime from your immediate surrounding. (15-ft. radius centered around you.)

Cause pain with a _ _ _ (This Prescript is blurred out. You can make out the word with a little effort. To make this effort, read the Prescript aloud to your table, the first object named by your party or DM is the word.)
If it is bright, shoot the sun. If it is night, find shelter. (Attack the biggest or shiniest creature or enter cover respectively.)
Tell your greatest fears to your foes whenever you cause them harm. Tell them to spread word that you will hunt these fears down at any cost.
Be a liar, but always involve flowers in your lies.

After the dust settles, compose a song about your exploits in this battle. Sing it at the next one. Draw another prescript. (You complete this upon singing at your first turn of the next battle and may ignore this Prescript toward the total drawn in a single turn.
